pages.title: About AccuMark Explorer
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search About AccuMark Explorer Displays the current version number of your AccuMark Explorer software.

pages.title: AccuMark Explorer Options
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search AccuMark Explorer Options AccuMark Explorer Options are found under the File menu. Tabs are available for Configuration - Set the system preferences for marking, creating new storage areas and other general working tasks. Storage Areas - Perform data management tasks such as checking and back up. Hardware Configuration – Use hardware configuration to configure various devices connected to your AccuMark system, such as the digitizer, tablet, function box,  and plotter. Hardware Configuration can also be opened from the pane. User Settings - Allow you to set user identification preferences as well as import or export PDS and marking settings. Default Open Options - Set the preferred application for opening data items.

pages.title: Advanced Queries

links.label: Find all pieces not currently contained in a model and delete them

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Advanced Queries Advanced queries created in Find allow you to perform complicated searches to locate specific files. Advanced queries can be used to do such tasks as Find all pieces not currently contained in a model and delete them , or Find markers with a length less than 440 inches and generate cut files for a static cutter .

pages.title: Check
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Check If a folder is closed, this command lets you run check on the corresponding storage area. A best practice is to lock a Storage Area before running Check. Also, confirm other users are not actively working in the area. To run check on a storage area: 1. In the All Folders section of the Explorer, right click on the folder you want to check. Do not open the folder first; it must be closed in order for it to be checked. 2. When the Shortcut menu displays, choose Check .

pages.title: Configuration Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Configuration Tab Marking Options , Default Parameter Tables Plotting SQL Configuration Email Configuration Recycle Bin PLM configuration

pages.title: Copy
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy The copy feature duplicates the names and storage locations of the selected data items to the Windows clipboard. This feature does not copy the actual data items to the clipboard — it only copies references to the items. If the Paste feature is then used, the system returns to the original storage location and copies the data items from that point. If data items are copied to the clipboard and deleted from the storage location prior to pasting, the system will not be able to perform the paste. Deleting the items prior to pasting also deletes the references to those items in the clipboard.

pages.title: CSV File Format Details
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search CSV File Format Details The data file you'll be making for the CSV Import Tools is a text file. It is organized in lines and groups of lines. The lines are Comments, Data Types, and Field Values. Data is entered as groups of lines. One or more groups for each data item. For example, an order will consist of its name, general order information, a model, and the list of sizes for that model. It can possibly be followed by other models and the list of sizes for each. After the detailed descriptions that follow, there are some examples. A word of caution: The data in each field must be valid. Valid characters, valid ranges, and mandatory order fields are required. If you do not do this, unpredictable results may occur. Comments: Anything that follows a '#' is a comment. For example, # This is a comment line. Comments may appear as part of other data lines, for example, =:order	#comment - this start of order section. Data Types: Lines which begin with a '=:' signal the start of a new data type. The data type keywords are: =:order =:model and =:sizecode These lines are followed by the fields that make up these data items. Field Values: Each value in the data item is entered using a Field Type, a Colon, and then the Field Value. For example one value needed by an order data item is, m:fall90slacks1 the 'm' is a model name field. The model name is fall90slacks1. A number of fields use numeric values. Many of these values are a count of items. For example, quantity is a count of sizes in an order. However, other values are notation dependent. The marker width can be specified either in inches or in centimeters. In this case, the data is interpreted based on the user environment table P-USER-ENVIRON. For example, w:100 Will be interpreted as inches

pages.title: CSV Import
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search CSV Import The CSV Import Tools converts Comma Separated text files to AccuMark data items, including Orders, Models, and Size Code data. Being able to read text input file and store it in an AccuMark storage area lets you automate your workload by giving you the ability to : -	Transfer data from a central computer. This eliminates the need to reenter order information into AccuMark. Simply generate the text file, and transfer it. -	Do specialized order entry. Orders can be entered from your own planning software. You can do this because you enter Model and Size Code (the alteration information) in the same data file as the order information. These tools read a text file for input. This text file may be generated from any language, perhaps on another computer. A 'C' programmer isn't required to write your custom application. However, someone does have to be able to generate the text file in the correct format. Clicking the CSV Import launches a dialog box to select the file. Select the AccuMark Storage Area for the processing. Checkboxes will allow the overwriting of a data item if it already exists. The source text file can also be deleted after processing.

pages.title: CSV Query
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search CSV Query This program allows you to process simple database style queries directly on a CSV output report.  CSV QUERY will allow you find some information, without needing to import the CSV file into a database. It can also be used to choose which records and columns that are imported into a database. In addition, the csvquery can prepare a list of orders to be processed, delete list of items, or copy a list of items. The csvquery program takes a CSV file as input, and generates a CSV file as output. It has several commands. Query File Name is a required input file. It is the name of the CSV file that has the data to be processed. CSV Import Report Name is a name of the report you are having created by the query. You can specify an optional output file. The results of the query are written to this file. If no output file is specified, then the results go to the screen. Finally,the CSV Query will accept an optional Action command. This optional command specifies what to do with the list of items. It can write the list to the order processing form in the AccuMark. It can delete the list of items, or it can copy the list of items to a new storage area.

pages.title: CSV Reports
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search CSV Reports The CSV tools generate report information for use in a spreadsheet, database, or other programs. CSV files may be easily read by a user written program. In addition to CSV format files, the CSV utilities can also format files in DBF file format. DBF file format makes using the reports from a database program more convenient. The CSV report data can provide many kinds of information. For example, you can load marker header data into a spreadsheet, and sort it from largest to smallest utilization. Another possible use is to load the model information into a database, and query the database.

pages.title: Data items
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Data items Information that can be created in AccuMark, and which is stored as individual files on the system or in a network storage area. This includes: Alteration Rules, Annotation Tables, Blocking/Buffering Rules, Cut Data, Cutter Parameter Tables, Digitized Data, Grade Rule Tables, Laylimits, Layrules, Layrule Search Parameter Tables, Marker Plot Parameter Tables, Markers, Matching Rules, Models, Notch Parameter Tables, Orders, Piece Plot Parameter Tables, Pieces, Plot Data, and Size Code Tables.

pages.title: Date Modified
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Date Modified Use this query information to find data which was created or modified during a specified time span. The time span may be hours, days, weeks or longer. When the fields have been completed and the Find Now button is selected the search will return only those files which meet the date criteria.

pages.title: Default  Open Options
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Default  Open Options Set the default open preferences for Pieces, Models, Orders, Markers, and Reports. Default Open Piece Option- Allows you to set how double click opens Pieces, in the Model Editor or in PDS. Open in Active Work Area will open the selected piece in a previously opened PDS work area. Open in Separate Work Area will open a new instance of PDS with the selected piece. Default Open Model Option- Allows you to set how double click opens Models, in the Model Editor or in PDS. Open in Active Work Area will open the selected model in a previously opened PDS work area. Open in Separate Work Area will open a new instance of PDS with the selected model. Default Open Order Option- Allows you to set how double click opens Orders, with the classic Order Editor or the Easy Order form. Default Open Marker Option- Allows you to set how double click opens Markers, with classic Marker Making or the Easy Marking. Default Open Report Viewer- Internal application will open reports in the AccuMark report viewer. Registered program will open the selected report in an external program such as Microsoft Excel.

pages.title: Default Parameter Tables
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Default Parameter Tables Reset System Defaults — the system will use the standard default parameter tables that come with AccuMark when you create new storage areas. For example, this means a newly created Storage Area will have a User Environment Parameter Table set to metric with a decimal precision set to two. Newly created Storage Areas will also have the default "A" Annotation Editor, "L" Laylimits, and Costorder which is used by PDS when . performing "Process Costing Marker." Set New Defaults —  the system will automatically copy the  all of the parameter tables from the specified storage area when you create new storage areas.  In addition, it will copy all the basic data including Alteration, Annotation, Block Buffer, Laylimits, Rule Tables, and Size Codes from this Storage Area to the newly made one. TIP: If you plan to use "Set New Defaults," create a master Storage Area with all basic data items and parameter tables each newly created Storage Area will need. A warning will display if the New Defaults area is a version 9 Storage Area while creating a version 8 Storage Area.

pages.title: Delete Inactive Records from CAD Relational Database
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Delete Inactive Records from CAD Relational Database AccuMark can be configured through SQL Support to write to a CAD Relational Database. Statistical information for markers, models and its pieces is stored into various tables, along with thumbnail images for the markers and the model’s pieces. Previously when SQL storage area markers, models and their pieces were deleted, and you had the CAD Relational Database configured, the relational database only marked the data items as InActive, but the records still existed in all the database tables. This caused for a lot of extra data in the tables that was no longer needed, and possibly making the querying or retrieving of data from the relational database more complicated and slow. Remove the InActive records from the CAD Relational database: “Delete inactive records” will remove all the entries in all the CAD Relational Database tables that have been identified as InActive for the currently configured database as set in SQL Support.

pages.title: DSN Setup
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search DSN Setup From the Windows Control Panel select Administrative Tools > Data Sources. Then select the System DSN tab. Press the Add Button and highlight SQL Server. Enter a name for the DSN, description and specify the SQL server to connect to. If DSN is the preferred method of communication: one connection per each server in the network needs to be established in all Workstations that will connect to SQL instances. Do not change the method of authentication unless your IT department directs this be done. Accept the defaults in this dialog and click finish. System shows a summary of the DSN creation.

pages.title: To edit digitized data
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search To edit digitized data In the Contents section of the Explorer, select the digitized data item in the storage area that you want to edit. Right click to display the Shortcut menu. Choose Open. In the Edit Digitize window, any errors are listed by line number at the top of the window. To change the Button Type for a line number, click in the Button Type field. Click on the Arrow button at the right of the field and select the correct button type from the drop-down list box. Click OK. If all changes have been successful, you will be prompted to save as an AccuMark piece. Otherwise, repeat steps 2 through 6 to continue making edits. If you make unwanted changes, retrieve the original digitized data and begin editing again or select File/Open without saving changes.

pages.title: Edit Digitized Editor
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Digitized Editor Use this editor to display and edit the digitized data for a piece. This feature displays in sequential order, the button pushes that were made on the digitizing cursor when a piece was digitized. If a mistake is made during digitizing, it can be corrected here. Use Edit Digitize if an attempt to retrieve digitized data was made and an error message was displayed. Note: If the Edit Digitize screen appears blank, the piece will need to be digitized again. If button pushes for the piece display on the Edit Digitize screen, corrections to the piece may be made. Review each line in the problem area, as indicated by the Error Line Number field, located in the Status Field. Move through lines indicated to correct errors. Edit Digitize Screen Field Explanations Status – This field displays a brief explanation of the error. Line # - Indicates the sequence number of button pushes made with the digitizing cursor when the piece was digitized. Button Press – Lists each button press that was made on the digitizing cursor when the piece was digitized. Button Type – Indicates the type of information that was entered when the piece was digitized. Push button followed by a character indicates which cursor button was pressed. Menu followed by one or more characters indicates the items that were selected from the digitizing menu. X Coord – Displays the X (horizontal) coordinate of the corresponding button push. Y Coord – Displays the Y (bertical) coordinate of the corresponding button push.

pages.title: Import from ERP Wizard

links.label: When working with the ERP Wizard, you will be able to automate the following tasks:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import from ERP Wizard Experienced users can benefit from a wizard to streamline order entry into AccuMark as a CSV file directly from your existing ERP system. The ERP wizard serves as an introduction to the power of using CSV files to automate your process.  Once you have used the wizard for a while, you may want to create new CSV files based on the files created by the wizard directly in an application such as Excel by making minor changes to existing CSV files, such as the model name, sizes, or quantities. These simple edits can be quickly done and the CSV files ready processing. The ERP Wizard will also guide you through the steps to build CSV orders when generated from a company’s database. When working with the ERP Wizard, you will be able to automate the following tasks: •	Look up for AccuMark data names needed to produce markers such as fabric width, Lay Limits and Annotation tables, P-Notch tables and if necessary Alteration and Size Code tables to generate mass customization orders directly from your ERP system. •	In addition, the ERP Wizard also provides the ability to group all these items under one table called Fabric Group; when created, the ERP Wizard will speed up the process of data item selection; for example, select a fabric group named “COTTON” and all the necessary information will automatically be populated down below. •	Look up for AccuMark model names and their corresponding size names previously linked (table called Model Sizes.) •	Generate a template CSV file. •	Export sample CSV file to the “Watch Directory”. •	Launch Batch Queue automatically.

pages.title: Getting Started with  Import from ERP Wizard

links.label: first step of the Import from ERP Wizard

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Getting Started with  Import from ERP Wizard The CSV/Import ERP Wizard will allow you to have and choose from any of the following types of data to create a valid csv file your company can use to map up fields in the mainframe database and you can either submit orders directly to the Watch Directory and automatically launch the Batch Queue for processing markers, plot and cut files. 1.	Database Simulator:  builds up sample csv order files with information retrieved from an MS-Access sample database provided with the software to get you started. 2.	Configuration Files (txt files that can be viewed with Notepad or MS-Excel) a second option that builds up sample csv order files with information retrieved from a set of sample txt tables that have been provided to get you started. 3.	AccuMark Storage Area: allows you to access your AccuMark system directly and populate fields by selecting AccuMark data file names. In addition, when using Database simulator you will have the ability to import models with their corresponding fabric names as well as their corresponding sizes by looking up at Model reports (see additional information in the AccuMark Explorer section regarding two new reports: Model Size Line and Model Size Code Reports.)  This feature is only available when using Database simulator: •	Import Model/Fabrics: allows you to read the All Model report; it links the model name with the fabric types specified in the model editor automatically populating the Model Fabric table. •	Import Model/Sizes: allows you to read all model size names and size code names; it links model names and size names to build the Model Sizes table The final CSV Order file created by the wizard will contain the parameters for importing into Batch along with comme

pages.title: Import from ERP Wizard Order Settings
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import from ERP Wizard Order Settings The first step in the ERP Wizard is to enter the information that is usually included in an AccuMark marker order: •	The top section includes the general order information and mandatory fields are marked with an “*”.Other optional order information can also be added if needed for the markers, including order number, description, target length or utilization, as well as shrink or stretch information. •	The bottom section has been grouped as “Fabric Information”; simply select a Fabric Group name (which represents the fabric type in the marker) and the rest of the fields down below will automatically be populated based on the information specified in the Fabric Group table specified in the MS-Access database. Mandatory fields are marked with an “*”. You can overwrite any item at this point in time by selecting other existing item names from the drop down menus or by typing in other names. The required information includes the fabric width, lay Limits, Annotation and Notch tables. If requesting altered sizes, make sure to select Alteration and Size Code. When using outside database or configuration files, Storage Area location is determined later on. When accessing a Storage Area from step 1 then it is defined based on the location the data items are selected from. After making all your selections click Next to continue to the Model Settings .

pages.title: Import from ERP Wizard Model Settings
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import from ERP Wizard Model Settings The next step allows you to set the model information for the CSV file: •	Click on the Select Models button to populate the table. •	Select models for the CSV order, sizes for each model and quantity; fabric type is optional. •	When complete, click Next to continue to Job Settings step.

pages.title: Import from ERP Wizard Job Settings
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import from ERP Wizard Job Settings The Job Settings allow you to define the type of job you want Batch Processing to do. There are two different ways to proceed: •	Select the option on the top “Job Settings” if you are have not used Batch before; next, select the destination storage area you wish to submit your orders to (the items needed to make the marker must exist to generate the markers.) Also, select how the marker will be made (AutoMark, AccuNest or Easy Marking). Last, Check options to plot and/or cut the markers. The destination for the plot file, local or a particular plot queue is set here as well as the Export Directory. •	If you are an experience Batch user and have Batch parameter tables previously created, then select the second option “Batch Table”; the name of the table and the destination storage area name specified in that table will display. The final step is to process to create the CSV File . Click on Next to continue

pages.title: Import from ERP Wizard Process CSV
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import from ERP Wizard Process CSV Once all the steps have been completed, the CSV file is ready for processing: •	The order can be directly submitted to Batch Processing to make markers, and generate plot and/or cut files. •	The CSV file can be viewed in Notepad or Excel. •	Once one CSV file has been created, this page also allows you choose to create the next CSV order file.

pages.title: Exit
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Exit Closes the AccuMark Explorer application. To exit Explorer: From the File menu, choose Exit . Or, click the X button in the far right corner of the title bar.

pages.title: Export Zip
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Export Zip Create a zipped file that includes  selected data items. When the data is being zipped, a dialog box displays that allows the components of the item to be included, for example if a model with its component pieces. When exporting data to a zip file, a dialog box will appear that allows non-AccuMark data items to be included in the zip file. This is a convenient way to group files related to the data, for example assembly instructions in a Word document to accompany a model being sent to another location. Select AccuMark data items to export, then select File/ Export Zip from the File menu. The "Export To" dialog box appears. Choose the directory to which the data is to be Exported. The export screen opens. Items select to be exported will be listed by name, type, size, and date last modified. Select any options such as the components to be included, then choose OK to allow compression of the selected data items and placement in the specified location. An AccuMark Explorer dialog box appears, which reads "Process Complete" to indicate the data export is finished. Select OK . NOTE: Version 8 data may be imported into a version 8 or 9 Storage Areas. Version 9 data can only be imported into a version 9 Storage Area. Beginning with AccuMark version 9.0, version 7 AccuMark Storage Area data is read only, so data cannot be imported into these areas.

pages.title: Export V9 Pieces/Models to V8
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Export V9 Pieces/Models to V8 Use this option to save pieces and models that were created and stored in a version 9 storage area to a data format supported by version 8 storage areas. This will remove the V8 non-compatible features of the data including bookmarks and other characteristics, and provide you an opportunity to shorten names to the V8 restrictions.

pages.title: File Menu
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search File Menu Use the File menu commands to create new AccuMark Storage Areas, new data items or parameter tables, import or export data, print , view software version information and exit. New Import Zip Export Zip Export V9 Models/Pieces to V8 Import Print Print Preview Print Setup Options Help Topics View Version Information About AccuMark Explorer Exit

pages.title: Find all pieces not currently contained in a model and delete them
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Find all pieces not currently contained in a model and delete them This illustrates how AccuMark Find may be used to eliminate unnecessary files: 1. On the Advanced page, select Piece as the Type. 2. Mark the Not Contained In box as active (check mark appears) 3. Check Marker . Click the Find Now button. To delete particular files, select the file name(s). Right click on one of the selected files and select Delete from the Shortcut menu.

pages.title: The Find Utility Window
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search The Find Utility Window Use the Find utility to quickly search for AccuMark data. When items are found they can be acted upon in various ways. For example results can be processed, deleted, and opened. When results display markers, they can even be sorted by status: Made, Unmade, Needs Approval. From the Home tab, select Find from the Editing group. The top half of this window contains four tabs and three menu items: File, Edit, and Help. The bottom half of this window displays the results of a search, including the name of each data item located during the search, the storage area in which each data item was located, the data type and the date the item was last modified. AccuMark Find can be used to find specific data.  Using the Advanced tab, selections can be made to find pieces that are not contained in models or models not contained in markers.  This can be helpful when cleaning up storage areas with unused pieces or models.

pages.title: Data Conversion Utility
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Data Conversion Utility Use the Data Conversion to import and export data  including Rule Tables, Pieces/Models, and Markers. Data can be imported from Assyst, Lectra, Investronica, Standard DXF format from AutoCad, ASMA/ASTM from other CAD ssytem, TIIP, and IGES.

pages.title: Digitizing Processing Options
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Digitizing Processing Options Piece descriptive information that previously had to be entered using the digitizing cursor and menu can be quickly entered in a new dialog box, Digitize Processing Options. To further simplify the digitizing process, when entering the piece descriptive information, the pieces can also be automatically added to a model. If the model does not exist, it will be created automatically. Storage Area Select the target Device and Storage Area name. SQL device/storage areas can also be selected. Piece Name Prefix and Starting Piece Number The Digitize Processing Options dialog will keep track of your digitized piece names by using the Prefix name defined by the user followed by the Starting Piece Number.Using this method, you can enter a name, then starting piece number, and each piece digitized will be automatically assigned this prefix and the sequential number. For example, you can enter “LADIES” as the prefix, the starting piece number “1” The first piece digitized will automatically be named “LADIES1”  the next piece will be “LADIES2” and so on. When you begin digitizing the piece geometry, all the descriptive information has been added by the interface, so begin by digitizing the grain line of the piece and piece perimeter then internals as in the past. To change to a new prefix and/or starting piece number, simply edit the fields. Category You may enter a category for each piece or allow the piece name to be assigned as the category automatically. Same Category as Piece Name Selecting this checkbox will automatically assign the piece name as the category to streamline the piece information entry. Remember that this information can also be edited easily later in the Model. Add to Model name (optional) If a mode

pages.title: Steps to Use the Import from ERP Wizard
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Steps to Use the Import from ERP Wizard 1. Order Settings: The first step in the wizard is to enter the information that is usually included in an AccuMark marker order. The required information includes the fabric width, the order name which will be used for marker naming, an annotation table, a laylimits editor and notch table. Other optional order information can also be added if needed for the markers, including order number, description, target length or utilization, as well as shrink or stretch information. Storage Area location displays based on the location the data items are selected from. 2. Model Settings: The next step allows you to set the model information for the CSV file. Select the model or models for the CSV order, sizes for each model, quantity and fabric type. 3. The Job Settings display the Storage Area name. Here you select how the marker will be made, Automatically made with AutoMark or AccuNest , or manually placed using Easy Marking. Check boxes allow the marker to be plotted and a cut file created. The destination for the plot file, local or a particular plot queue is set here and the directory for export is also set here. 4. Once all the steps have been completed, the CSV file is ready for processing.  The order can be directly submitted to Batch Processing or the CSV file can be viewed in Notepad or Excel. Once one CSV file has been created, this page also allows you choose to create the next CSV order file. Here is a sample as viewed via Notepad and Excel:

pages.title: Grade Rule Editor
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Grade Rule Editor This icon launches the Grade Rule Editor. In this form, grading is recorded as an X, Y value under an assigned grade rule number. When a pattern piece is created, the rule table and rules are applied, grading the piece.

pages.title: Import from ERP
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import from ERP Experienced users can benefit from a wizard to streamline order entry into AccuMark as a CSV file directly from your existing ERP system. The wizard welcomes a first time user, then guides you through the process to create a CSV order with the necessary Batch settings to process it automatically. The wizard serves as an introduction to the power of using CSV files to automate your process.  Once you have used the wizard for a while, you may want to create new CSV files based on the files created by the wizard directly in an application such as Excel by making minor changes to existing CSV files, such as the model name, sizes, or quantities. These simple edits can be quickly done and the CSV files ready processing.

pages.title: PDS
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search PDS Open the Pattern Design software to make pattern modifications.

pages.title: Winplot
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Winplot WinPlot converts and formats plot files from AccuMark and other non-Gerber CAD systems that generate plot files according to the following requirements. After converting for proper page limits, submit these files to a plot queue and plot on any of the Gerber family of plotters.In addition to formatting standard plot files, WinPlot includes utilities to manage the plotter queue, view plot files, and set plotter media characteristics. HPGL Plot Files (.plt)- files that conform to HP 7475  plotter requirements. Generic HPGL format files can also be converted. These include files exported as HPGL files (.plt) from packages such as Micrografx Designer or CorelDraw™. WinPlot does not support arc or circle commands. Unsupported commands will be reported in the log file window. Gerber Plot Files (.gen or other user defined extension) - plot files generated from AccuMark . The plots are submitted to the plot queue, and no conversion is performed. DWG Plot Files (.dwg) -  .dwg files generated primarily from Autocad. The .dwg format is a binary file. The .dwg format allows plots to be generated full size so that WinPlot can process the plot without having to apply scaling. While most .dwg commands are supported, any unsupported commands will be reported in the log file. DXF Plot Files (.dxf) -  plot files generated from Autocad and other CAD software programs. The format adhered to by many CAD packages. DXF files are generally larger in size than the equivalent plot file in dwg format. Most dxf commands are supported. Unsupported commands will be reported in the log file. Gerber Cut Files (.nc or other user defined extension) - Gerber cut files generated from AccuMark or other CAD software. Gerber Job Files (JOB extension) - Specially format

pages.title: Add Jobs
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Add Jobs If a marker or order is the selected data item in the contents pane, then the corresponding data item in the Add Jobs function group is active, allowing you to submit the item to Batch Processing.

pages.title: Clipboard

links.label: To paste data items from the clipboard:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Clipboard Paste - Places data items that were copied to the Windows clipboard into the selected location. To paste data items from the clipboard: 1. After using Copy , select the folder into which to paste data items from the clipboard. 2. Right click on that folder to display the Shortcut menu. 3. Choose Paste or Paste Components . If duplicates are detected, the system displays the Transfer dialog box and prompts: " Data item already exists, do you wish to overwrite? " 4. Choose Yes or Yes to All . The system copies the data items from the clipboard to the selected folder. Paste with Components - Places data items along with the associated components that were copied to the Windows clipboard into the selected location. For example, if the data item was a model, then the model and the component pieces would be pasted to the new location. Cut - Remove a data item from its location. Copy - Create another version of the selected item. Rename - Change the name of the selected item. Delete- Remove the selected data item. Delete w/Components - Remove the selected data item and the associated items. Select All - Highlights all data items in the currently selected location. Invert Selection - R emoves the highlight from the selected data items and highlights all other data items in the current folder.

pages.title: Editing/Find
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Editing/Find The Editing group contains an icon that launches the Find utility, a search engine that is an integral part of AccuMark Explorer. Use this utility to search for specific AccuMark  data using wildcards, date criteria, and other filters. Actions can then be performed on the results. For instance, if a notch is added to a piece, it is possible to search for all of the markers that contain that piece, and then easily reorder and remake one or more of the markers using Copy Marker or Regenerate Marker.

pages.title: Recycle Bin
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Recycle Bin This group contains Open and Clear. AccuMark data deleted from a storage area in Explorer will automatically be moved to the recycle bin. To restore data: Click the "Open" icon. Right click on a data item and select Restore . Or, left click and drag the data item back to the desired location.

pages.title: Utilities Group
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Utilities Group The Utilities Group provides tools to Move, Copy, Rename, and Delete data. “Include all Subfolders” options allow you to quickly and easily include all locations when copying, moving, deleting and renaming data items. Move will transfer data from one location to another. Copy will create an additional duplicate data item in a new location. Rename will change the data item name to a new one. Delete will remove the data item, moving it to the recycle bin to be discarded.

pages.title: Hardware Configuration
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Hardware Configuration In AccuMark Explorer, you can configure various devices connected to your AccuMark system. Hardware that can be configured includes: Digitizer Tablet Plotter Function Box Tracker To configure hardware: 1.From the AccuMark Options dialog located in the File Menu, click on the Hardware Configuration tab . The Hardware Configuration opens. 2. Select the device and complete information in that area of the dialog. 3. Click Apply to continue configuring another device. Click OK when finished.

pages.title: SQL Manager
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search SQL Manager Clicking the SQL Manager button will open the Read/Write assignment wizard for SQL storage areas. This utility allows permissions to be set on data item types within storage areas. NOTE: SQL Compatibility tools are need for SQL Manager to be able to function for SQL 2008, SQL 2012, and SQL 2014. SQL Manager has been updated to allow setting of AccuMark data type read / write controls on a group level. In earlier software versions you could only set permissions on a user level. Create and use windows groups for users in different departments or working roles, then allocate permissions more efficiently per group compared to each individual user. Then simply add or remove users to the groups you set up rather than modifying their individual data type permissions. Setting read and/or write access for users and now windows groups for the various AccuMark data types lets you control data creation and manipulation for SQL storage areas and subfolders. For example, allow pattern makers to read and write models and pieces, but only let marker makers read and use models and pieces to make their markers (assigning read-only permission will not let them make any modifications to the models and pieces). Users are also better informed with the improved messages regarding when and what permission they have when accessing data and storage areas.

pages.title: Upgrade SQL Storage Area
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Upgrade SQL Storage Area User selects the SQL device and then a storage area to upgrade using the dropdown selections then clicks on a button to update that Pre-version 8.2 SQL storage area to V8

pages.title: Userroot Backups
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Userroot Backups Clicking  the Userroot Backups button will open the Backup wizard for userroot storage areas

pages.title: Import Plot and Digitized Data
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import Plot and Digitized Data The File menu includes an "Import" selection that allows plot data and/or digitized data be imported into an AccuMark Storage Area.

pages.title: Import Zip
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import Zip Use the Import Zip function to un-compress a zip file(.zip) from a saved location that contains AccuMark data items. Zipped files may contain non AccuMark files as well; the location to place these files can be defined in the Import Zip dialog box. If the data originated in a version 9 AccuMark Storage Area, a warning message will appear if the selected import location is a version 8 area. Select File/ Import Zip from the File menu. The "Import From" dialog box appears. Choose the directory from which the data is to be imported. Select the data to be imported The import screen opens. Items to be imported will be listed by name, type, size, and date last modified. To import all of the items listed, Select OK . To import specific items, select the items you want to import, and choose OK . The system un-compresses the selected data items, and places them in the current storage area. If duplicate data items are detected, the system prompts "Data item already exists, do you wish to overwrite?" Choose YES or YES to All . When the system is finished importing, an AccuMark Explorer dialog box appears, which reads "Process Complete". Select OK . NOTE: Version 8 data may be imported into a version 8 or 9 Storage Areas. Version 9 data can only be imported into a version 9 Storage Area. Beginning with AccuMark version 9.0, version 7 AccuMark Storage Area data is read only, so data cannot be imported into these areas.

With this option selected, as the order is processed, each piece’s perimeter is slightly reduced, allowing placement of a piece that is exac

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marking Options Auto Update Marker AccuMark can automatically update a marker if the piece geometry was modified and the piece data saved.  The software simply compares the last modified date of the pieces with the last modified date of the marker.  If the last modified date of the piece is later than the last modified date of the marker, the basic piece geometry in the marker can be updated. This  edit would be a change that resides on the piece such as a notch or line change. The updates are applied when a marker is opened in marker making, accessed during cut generation or plotted. NOTE: This update does not re process the marker order, so only changes to the piece geometry that are stored within the piece data are applied. Dynamic changes that are applied by Marker Order process are not performed. To update a marker with dynamics applied during Order Processing, use Regenerate Marker . Only Regenerate Marker applies  the modifications that are performed during Order Process such as  Alterations, Size Code, Laylimits, Block Buffering,  etc. Auto Update does not process these dynamics, it only compares piece date to original marker date, and changes are only those that are found within the basic geometric piece  data. This field may be set to YES, NO or PROMPT. If the option is set to Yes, the marker is automatically updated when opened.  A message Regenerating Marker is displayed. If the option is set to No, the existing version of the marker is opened. If the option is set to Prompt, the system prompts to overwrite the marker and use the updated piece data. The updated marker is created using Copy Marker. If a change is made to a piece, such as adding an internal notch, all pieces will place successfully.  If changes are made to the p

pages.title: New
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search New The functionality of the File/New menu depends on the selection of a drive, or storage area in the All Folders (left pane) section of the Explorer. If a disk drive is selected , choosing New displays New V8 or V9 Storage Area. If an AccuMark storage area is selected , choosing New displays a submenu that contains commands for creating new AccuMark Editors and Parameter Tables in that open Storage Area. A V8 Storage Area name is restricted to eight characters and data item names cannot exceed twenty characters. Version 8 Storage Areas data is backwards compatible to AccuMark software version 8. AccuMark version 9 Storage areas support long file names, fifty character data item names, long fabric names, extended size names. To exchange piece and model with version 8 AccuMark software, use the export V9 to V8 feature from the File menu.

pages.title: Tips for New Users
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Tips for New Users The Marker Wizard will allow new users to quickly begin making markers. From AccuMark Explorer, you can select up to four models then open them in the Marker Wizard to create a marker. The Wizard can also be opened directly in Easy Marking from the File>New menu.

pages.title: New Users Can Quickly Make Cut Data
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search New Users Can Quickly Make Cut Data You can quickly create cut data for an automated cutter by right clicking on a placed marker. The cut data generation form will open allowing you to set a file location as the destination for the cut file or save it to the AccuMark storage area.

pages.title: More Tips for New Users
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search More Tips for New Users AccuMark Explorer allows you to easily open individual pattern pieces or even complete models in Pattern Design to make pattern changes. Pieces and models can be opened in the active PDS work area or a new area.

pages.title: Options
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Options Selecting Options from the File menu displays the  dialog box which includes tabs for: Configuration Storage Areas Hardware Configuration User Settings Default Open Options

pages.title: Overview
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Overview The AccuMark Explorer allows you to view all of the drives accessible to your computer that contain AccuMark storage areas. You can also view the data items in each storage area . You can generate reports from the Explorer, and view them through the report viewer. Using the Explorer you can create new AccuMark data items , and import, export, process or manage AccuMark data. You can also access the plotters available to your system, and monitor the status of all plotters from a single location. AccuMark Explorer lets you create new data items and import, export, process, or manage existing marker, model or piece data. The right mouse button shortcut menu lets you send selected data immediately to the next step in the workflow in the production process. For instance, you can generate a marker directly from an order, or generate cut data directly from marker data. AccuMark Explorer features a ribbon that includes tabs for File , Home , Process , Automation , Output, Reports , and View selections. The ribbon makes navigation of the AccuMark applications easier and the primary functionality more obvious. The AccuMark Explorer features panels for Navigation , Detail s, and a Preview Pane. The user’s working environment is maintained by keeping the selections for panes as well as the columns that are shown or hidden, sorting choices and columns widths. The explorer also has a  column for Status, which will allow sorting and filtering by Marker Status. The Options located under the AccuMark Explorer File menu allows users to set various work preferences including how data opens, SQL storage area locations, and how user information is displayed. Depending on the selection in the Navigation pane (All Folders) or the Details Pane (Contents

pages.title: Details Pane
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Details Pane Displays information about the storage areas if the drives are selected in the Navigation pane or the data items if a storage area is selected in the Navigation pane. The details display in column format, which allows sorting to be performed, such as arranging items by created or modified date.

pages.title: Navigation Pane
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Navigation Pane The navigation pane (the left pane) is used to display devices, storage areas, and data items. You can also move or copy items directly to a destination in the navigation pane.

pages.title: Preview Pane
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Preview Pane If a piece, model, marker, cut or plot file is selected, the item can be displayed in the preview pane. If previewing a model, you may choose to show a model's pieces or display a sketch (V9 storage area data). Preferences for displaying data in the Preview Pane are set in the View menu. (Preview/ Preferences) To display a sketch for V9 Storage Area models, the model editor must have a sketch file assigned.

pages.title: Plotters
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Plotters In AccuMark Explorer Navigation Pane, you can view a list of plotters available, a selected plotter's properties will display in the Details Pane, and a plot queue can be opened by right clicking on the plotter in the contents area.

pages.title: Plotting
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Plotting Plotter Queue Users who have administrator credentials can easily set up the required variables for various plotting environments. To use a Local plotter select the LOCAL radio button and then select OK. To configure a remote plotter using Peer to Peer networking, select the PEER radio button, and fill in the appropriate Plot Queue name of the network plotter to be used. To configure a remote plotter using Client Server networking, select the SERV radio button, and fill in the appropriate Plot Queue name and drive letter for the network plotter to be used.

pages.title: Print
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Print File/Print displays the Microsoft Windows Print dialog box. Use this command to print details on the contents of the currently selected folder, including the data items name, type, size, and data last modified. To print details on the contents of a folder: 1. In the All Folders section of the Explorer, select the folder containing the contents to be printed. 2. From the File menu, choose Print . 3.  When the Print dialog box displays, choose OK .

pages.title: Print Preview
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Print Preview Use Print Preview to view the layout of the selection to be printed. To preview the details of a folder before printing: 1. In the All Folders section of the Explorer, select the folder to be printed. 2. From the File menu, choose Print Preview . The print Preview screen opens, illustrating how the document will appear when printed.

pages.title: Print Setup
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Print Setup Displays the Microsoft Windows Print Setup dialog box. This allows the user to select the printing properties, paper size, source, and orientation to best suit company needs. To change printing properties: 1. From the File menu, choose Print Setup . The Print Setup dialog box displays, apply settings as necessary, and choose OK .

pages.title: Recycle Bin
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Recycle Bin The maximum size of the Recycle Bin is 1GB or 10,000 items. In addition, the user  has the ability to choose how often the data in the recycle bin will automatically be deleted. You may choose to automatically delete data in the recycle bin that is older than one week, older than one month, or older than one year. You can also choose to  never have it automatically delete, then manually empty the recycle bin when you like.

pages.title: Regenerate Marker
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Regenerate Marker This feature is useful if you make a change to a marker component such as a piece and then want to remake a marker that contains that piece. The system will order process the marker and then use Copy Marker in an attempt to re – place all pieces into the marker and the original marker is overwritten. The tables and editors used to create the marker are processed again to apply changes such as buffering or alterations. Depending on the significance of the change, the pieces may not fit back into their original locations without manual manipulation or re nesting using AccuNest or AutoMark. 1. In the Contents section of the Explorer, select the markers you want to regenerate. 2. Right click on the selected markers to display the Shortcut menu. Choose Regenerate Marker . The Regenerate Marker dialog box displays indicating the name of the marker that is about to be Order Processed. It also indicates that after the marker is created, Copy Marker will be used in an attempt to re – place all pieces into the marker. The original marker will be overwritten. 4. Choose Yes to regenerate the current marker or choose Yes to All to regenerate all selected markers without being prompted before each one. Once finished, the system indicates the number of markers that were successfully processed and the number of errors that occurred. A marker may report a status of Needs Approval or Partial if the pieces were not replaced fully in the Regenerated Marker. 5. Click OK .

pages.title: Retrv Original
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Retrv Original Choose this command if you make an incorrect or unwanted change to the digitized data for a piece. This command removes the current information from the screen and displays the original (as digitized) digitized data for the piece.

pages.title: Marking Rule Editor
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marking Rule Editor An enhancement to Batch Processing allows users to have pieces placed prior to the marker being made by a manual marker maker, AccuNest, or AutoMark. A new field has been added to the Batch Parameter Table, “PreMarking Rule” that will apply piece placements in a new marker based on user created rules. The Rule Editor allows users to define piece placement to specific locations in the marker and even place pieces relative to other pieces. An editor allows you to set up the rules to be applied prior to the marker being made. The Editor is launched from the Automation tab in AccuMark Explorer. The source size is a drop down that allows you to set the rule to be performed beginning with the largest or smallest size of the piece. If Source Size is left blank, then the rule can be performed in any sequence on the sizes. For example, if you wish to place the fronts in the center of the marker, beginning with the largest size, select “Largest” from the drop down. If the marker contains pieces with size 6, 8 and 10, then the size 10 fronts would be placed first in the center, next the size 8, and finally the 6.  Destination Size and Destination Category are used to set up rules that group pieces together or place pieces relative to other pieces.  If placing pieces in a certain position in the marker, then these fields can be left blank. In the example below, the defined rule will place the front pieces at the bottom edge of the marker, the backs are then placed above the fronts.  Finally, the waistbands are placed along the top edge of the marker border. The marker is then ready to be finished using Easy Marking, AccuNest or AutoMark to place any remaining pieces. If the piece category contains a space, then enclose the categor

pages.title: SQL Drive Number
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search SQL Drive Number Drive numbers are displayed in the AccuMark Explorer for SQL locations, similarly to drive letters used to display file based network storage areas. Users define the SQL location per number, with drive numbers 0-9 available, allowing up to 10 distinctly different SQL locations. Each number is available for use, but do not have to be defined in any particular sequence. A user may select to use the number "2" instead of "0" as a drive number so that when AccuMark Explorer is open and displaying locations, users who have a drive letter captial "O" as a network location can distinguish easily the capital letter"O"  compared to a "0", number zero.

pages.title: SQL Support

links.label: Generate Images is a selectable checkbox.
System ODBC connection to the SQL

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search SQL Support Select Configuration/SQL Support from the Options, and the SQL Support dialog window appears. This dialog box allows you to set the location of the SQL server that hosts the AccuMark Storage Areas. The dialog box also features an area to configure a CAD Relational Database. You can select a drive number 0-9 to identify the SQL drive number to display in the AccuMark Explorer for Storage Area locations. The CAD Relational Database is not an AccuMark Storage Area, but is a database that contains model, piece, and marker statistical information that can be used by Yunique PLM, Web PDM or any external query that you may set up directly in SQL server management or a similar program. Generate Images is a selectable checkbox. These image files can be displayed in Yunique PLM or WebPDM. Images can be created with or without Annotation on them. To have annotation appear on these images, specify an AccuMark annotation table to use. In order to create the binary image data that will be stored in the CAD Relational database temporary .wmf and .bmp are used. These files are created in the \userroot\temp folder. Unless delete restrictions are enforced, these files will automatically get deleted the next time the system is rebooted. User Authentication SQL Support features two modes of user authentication: Windows and SQL. If Windows authentication is used, then the user’s credentials are verified based on the Windows login. If SQL authentication is used, a username must be specified with the password. DSN (Data Source Administrator) The DSN in SQL Support will allow the user the option to use SQL Server authentication or Windows authentication. Users may create a System ODBC connection to the SQL server and use that DSN name in SQL Support.

pages.title: Storage Areas
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Storage Areas In AccuMark, pieces and other information are saved and organized in storage areas ,which can be located on the computer’s hard drive or on network drives.  On the local hard drive, storage areas are located in the c:\userroot\storage directory. AccuMark systems can work with a SQL server to enhance security features and increase the capacity of storage areas.  A SQL server is a database management program created by Microsoft. If your system has been set up with a SQL server, it is possible to make subfolders in storage areas on the SQL drives.

Delete inactive records from CAD RDBMS
back up a Userroot Storage Area

NOTE: SQL Compatibility tools are need for SQL Manager to be able to function for SQL 2008, SQL 2012, and SQL 2014. Easily Upgrade Your Storage Areas Now you can easily upgrade your version 7 and version 8 userroot and SQL storage areas. Upgrade version 7 to version 8 or version 9, and upgrade version 8 to version 9 with a few simple clicks. You no longer have to create newer versioned storage areas and copy data from your older versioned storage areas. NOTE: it is always best to make a backup of your current data before proceeding with any major change. Select File, Options and in the Storage Areas window are the new options for upgrading. Select the version you wish to upgrade your storage areas: Note: “Pre V8.2” identifies SQL storage areas that were created prior to version 8.2 software. For the source storage areas to upgrade, select to browse All storage areas, browse for only version 8 (V8) storage areas, or browse for only version 7 (V7) storage areas: For example, if you only want to upgrade your version 7 storage areas, then select V7 to see the list of version 7 storage areas available for upgrading: Only the version 7 storage areas will be listed from all available drives and devices: The Verbose option will display any messages as the upgrade progresses. For example: NOTE: for SQL storage areas, the user must have the proper SQL permissions (sysadmin) to perform the upgrade.

pages.title: Automation Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Automation Tab This tab contains entries for  Batch Automation, Add Jobs, and CSV Utilities. Batch Automation allows you to use a Wizard to create a template for importing orders from an ERP system or to open the Batch Processing queue file. You can also open the Rule Editor to create placement rules for pieces prior to completing them with AccuNest, AutoMark, or Easy Marking. Add Jobs allows you to send selected Markers or Orders directly to Batch Processing. CSV Utilities allows you to use the various Comma Separated Utility programs including Import , Query , and Reports .

pages.title: Home Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Home Tab The Home Tab contains Clipboard , Editing, Recycle Bin , and a Utilities group.

pages.title: Output Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Output Tab Entries on this tab allow Plotting and Cutting. You may also display a view of pieces, cuts, and plot files.

pages.title: Process Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Process Tab The Process Tab contains entries to allow you to work with Pattern Design, work with orders and markers, and perform conversion and plotting tasks. The Pattern Design group contains icons to launch the pattern design software , to open the grade rule editor , set Digitizing Processing Options , and edit Digitized Data . Utilities allow data conversion and plotting .

pages.title: Reports Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Reports Tab This tab allows you to select reports for data items and configure the units of measure for the report displays.

pages.title: View Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Tab Use the View tab commands to: View the Activity and Batch Log files. The logs record all processing information. Change the scale of the display to allow, Zoom In, Zoom Out, then full 100% scale. Customize the Explorer view, by showing or hiding the various panes of the window. Refresh the list of data items or Storage Areas. View the user documentation. Configure the Preview Now you can preview up to four data items at a time! An option has been added into the AccuMark Explorer’s Preferences to let the user select how many items to display at once. Data items can be the same or different types.The Preview Pane will be divided into concatenated windows to display the selected data item(s). The data items will display in the order they were selected. Zoom and pan is still available, and will resize or move the data in all the currently displayed windows. Marker view preferences Markers now have additional information that can optionally be displayed in the AccuMark Explorer’s Preview window.

pages.title: To  Find Data
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search To  Find Data 1. From the Explorer Toolbar, click the Find button located in the Edit group of the Home Tab. The AccuMark Find Utility window displays. Click here to see an example of the window. 2. With the Name & Location tab selected, type the name of the data items to search for in the Named field. 3. In the Look In field, select the drive or storage area you want to search through. 4. To search for data items that were created or modified between a specific date and time, or during a previous number of months or days, click the Date Modified tab and complete the window as needed. 5. To search for data items of a specific type and referenced by a certain data type, click the Advanced tab and complete the window as needed. For example, to search for all of the markers that contain a specified piece, select Piece , Not Contained In , and Marker or Model . To use the Marker filter, click the button to open this dialog. If the button is now shown when the Advanced tab is selected, widen the dialog box display. 6. Choose Find Now . When the system completes the search, the located data items display in the bottom half of the window.

pages.title: Training Docs
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Training Docs This folder located on the installation media contains reference material related to SQL, Data Conversions, and other relevant but not routinely accessed documentation.

pages.title: User Settings Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search User Settings Tab The User Settings page gives the user the ability to save or use various user settings for PDS and Marking. User Information: Radio button options for the user information or ID to assign when users update, modify or create data for Userroot storage areas. Choices include: Use Windows Login – AccuMark applications will use the currently logged in windows user name to assign to data Use these Initials - AccuMark applications will use the three initials as entered by the user in the associated textbox to assign to data PDS User Settings: contains buttons Export Settings to export settings and preferences for PDS application and Import Settings to imports saved settings and preferences for PDS application. Marking User Settings: contains buttons Export Settings to export settings and preferences for Marking applications and Import Settings to import saved settings and preferences for Marking applications. User Settings are helpful when switching computers or to use as a backup if changes are made. Choose if and how you would like to receive the optimistic concurrency prompts: If you work with several other users on shared network drives or SQL devices, and often in the same storage areas, it is advantageous to display the optimistic concurrency prompts. This will alert you if you the data item you are working on is also being worked on by another user, having the potential to lose either your modifications or your colleagues changes and updates. If this is your environment select to “Show concurrent opening warning”. Then optionally set the way to proceed with the choices in the “Show the concurrent editing warning” selections. Deselect the ‘show’ options if you do not want to be prompted continuously. For example, you may

pages.title: View Version Information
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Version Information Detailed version information is displayed here, useful when requesting customer support. Each application's information is listed as well as any service pack or hotfix information. Basic system information is also found here.

pages.title: AccuMark Explorer and Find
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search AccuMark Explorer and Find AccuMark Explorer is a powerful application that provides you direct access to all areas of the AccuMark software, allowing you to perform a variety of tasks including opening pieces  in PDS , making markers and creating cut data .  There is even a wizard to allow you to learn to import orders directly from an ERP system. The Find capability allows you to locate data and perform operations directly in the Results window. In AccuMark Explorer, you can view all of the devices, accessible to your computer, that contain AccuMark storage areas. You can also view and search the AccuMark storage areas , as well as all of the data items in each storage area. The Explorer also features a preview pane that displays a selected piece, plot, or cut file. You can even view information about a selected item or area in the details pane. AccuMark Explorer features a ribbon that includes tabs for File , Home , Process , Automation , Output , Reports , and View selections. The ribbon makes navigation of the AccuMark applications easier and the primary functionality more obvious. Depending on the selection in the All Folders pane or the Contents pane, certain options will display active or disabled in the ribbon.

pages.title: Marker Information Bar
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marker Information Bar The prompt bar is located (by default) below the marker screen, and displays messages about the current marker. The information displayed is related to the function being performed. Some fields are display-only and other fields are text editable and interact with a particular function. Most of the remaining fields can be edited from within Easy Marking. Some fields are updated as different pieces are selected (such as PN). Editable fields are highlighted when the cursor is placed over them. To make changes, click the field. You can toggle through available choices or enter a new value, depending upon the field. MD Displays the model name of the highlighted piece PN Displays the piece name of the highlighted piece LN (this field not editable) Displays the length of the current marker. Depending on the unit of measure selected in the User Environment, the length display can be toggled between inches and yards, or centimeters and meters. SZ Displays the size of the highlighted piece. WI Displays the width of the current marker. To change the width, click in the entry field, and enter the desired amount. Select OK to accept. SA Displays the seam allowance specified for dynamic or split piecing, established in the User Environment Parameter Table. OL Displays the amount of overlap allowed when placing pieces. If a piece overlaps another, the amount of overlap step will display in the field next to OL when a piece is highlighted. Negative numbers apply space between pieces and are commonly used. TI Tilt amount increments are set in this field. When the Tilt Clockwise or Tilt Counterclockwise function is used, each right click on a piece tilts it the amount defined in this field. PA The area of the currently highlighted pi

pages.title: Piece Display Area - Matrix Menu
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Piece Display Area - Matrix Menu The piece display area is located at the top of the marking screen where the pieces show as an icon menu or as thumbnail images.  Using the menu, clicking on a number will bring down that piece in the size selected.  Clicking on a thumbnail image will bring down that piece.  The shape will be larger in the marker than it is in the menu area. The icon menu displays symbols that represent each piece ordered for the marker. Beneath each piece icon are two additional columns. The first shows the quantities of left pieces ordered for each size. The second one shows the quantities of the right pieces. These are defined in the Model Editor. The "Left" is the "As Input" while the "Right" is the flipped as defined in the Model. Each time the user selects a piece from the icon menu, the quantity field reduces. If dashes display beneath an icon, it means that no pieces were ordered for that particular size or based on the Fabric Spread, Halfpiece, or Cutdown setting, no piece is required for placement. Icons display as digitized. When the piece is dragged down into the work area or into the marker, it reflects the flip code orientation that was assigned to it in Lay Limits and used in the Order.

pages.title: Prompt Bar
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Prompt Bar The prompt bar is located below the marker screen and displays messages  related to the function being performed. When a function requires input, it will provide instructions or display a status message regarding the completed task.

pages.title: Quick Access Toolbar
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Quick Access Toolbar The Quick Access Toolbar provides the ability to select functions in a single click from the task bar. It displays in the title bar but can be set to display below the Easy Marking ribbon. The Quick Access Toolbar can be displayed above the Ribbon on the title bar or below the Ribbon. It is also customizable. Default selections are checked and automatically appear on the toolbar. By selecting More Commands a dialog will appear and functions can be added or removed from the toolbar. .

pages.title: Ribbon Interface
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Ribbon Interface The Easy Marking menus are organized in a new modern ribbon interface. Functions are grouped in Tabs which include the File Menu, Piece, Marker, Fabric, Advanced and View. The ribbon commands are visible and self-explanatory using icons and tooltips.

pages.title: Scroll Bar
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Scroll Bar The scroll bar allows the user to view different portions of the marker. The up and down scroll arrows are located on the far right side of the window at the bottom of the marker. The left and right arrows are located on the far left. The scroll bar represents the maximum length of the marker (default – 100 yards). The true ends of the marker are indicated by a small vertical line near each end of the scroll bar. To scroll directly to the beginning or end of a marker, click one of these vertical lines. The current length of the marker is represented by a dashed vertical line on the scroll bar. The scroll box is the solid white box within the scroll bar. It represents the length of the marker currently visible on the screen, based on the maximum length. Click anywhere else within the scroll bar area to move the box, and the marker, in that direction. You can use Ctrl plus the arrow keys on the keyboard to scroll through the marker when your cursor is in the workspace.

pages.title: Thumbnail
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Thumbnail The Thumbnail window is a small representation of the current marker that can be used to compare to what is being viewed in the actual marker.

pages.title: Title Bar
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Title Bar The title bar contains the name of the currently open marker including the device and storage area name. It also includes the Quick Access Toolbar icons and the control buttons for closing, minimizing, maximizing, and restoring the window.

pages.title: Toolbox

links.label: To apply a function to a piece

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Toolbox When a marker is retrieved a Toolbox is provided with a list of functions used to manipulate the pieces in the marker. This floating toolbar gives you access to many useful functions quickly and easily. To view the Toolbox select the View Tab and then the Toolbox from the Layout Group in the ribbon. You can also access the toolbox from the marker info dialog box by clicking the TB button, or by pressing the toolbox icon on the Quick Access toolbar when it is configured. The Toolbox is divided into two sections: Functions and Modifiers. The Toolbox functions allow you to manipulate the pieces being placed in the marker area, by assigning the function to the right mouse button. The selected function is displayed in the "TB" field in the Marker Info dialog box. The function remains active on the right mouse button until another function is selected, regardless of whether the toolbox toolbar is displayed or not. Auto Slide and Rotate have a solid arrow to the right of the icons When you click on either of these, additional features display that can be used to further control how the function is applied to pieces. Several keys are available through the Toolbox, or by accessing the numeric keypad. The keypad keys allow access to rotate, flip, fit, slide, and center pieces in the marker. NOTE: the keypad NumLock must be off to access these functions. To apply a function to a piece All functions are applied to a piece using the right mouse button. This leaves the left mouse button available for sliding pieces into the marker. Special keys are available on the numeric keypad. Highlight the piece with your cursor, and select the functions from the keypad. To apply an active toolbar function to a group of pieces, use the marquee selection bo

pages.title: Marker Work Area
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marker Work Area The marking work area defines the space of the material or marker.  The percentages at the bottom edge of the marking area can be used as targets.  If all the pieces are place to the left of any one of these lines, that percentage will be the approximate utilization of the marker. The work area contains the marker border. The marker border appears on the screen as a rectangle along the bottom of the screen. Use the space above the marker border to arrange the pieces before placing them in the marker. In the marker border, a target or goal line is used to indicate the amount of fabric that ideally is to be used to make the marker. It displays in the marker as a dotted line. This "goal" is defined in during order entry and is based on historical information about that style or a similar type of marker. This optional setting can be target length or target utilization. Target length is the maximum length you want the marker to be once all the pieces have been placed. Target utilization is the percent of usage for the amount of material. In other words, how well did you make use of the area of the marker when placing the pieces. The target line remains and a second dotted line shows the last length of the marker when it was stored.

pages.title: Marker Wizard
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marker Wizard The Marker Wizard will allow you to make a marker without any prior set up.  From Easy Marking, just select File > New. A maximum of four models can be selected if using the Marker Wizard. Use the Easy Order form if more than four models are required for one marker. A corresponding order is not created, but a lay limits is created for each marker/fabric. These can be deleted later. Models The first step of the wizard allows you to select the models for the marker being created. Using the right mouse on a model in AccuMark Explorer and open with the Marker Wizard, the form will open with the models selected. If you start from Easy Marking, simply browse to the correct storage area and select the models for the marker. The Steps section give you a visual cue to show progress, and you can click on the buttons in the lower right to move to the next step. An explanation of the step located at the top of the window can help guide you as you work. Sizes “Sizes” displays all the selected models with the sizes available, allowing you to specify a quantity for an individual size. You can click “Next” to move on, Cancel to discard any changes made, or Previous to go back to make changes to the Models selected. Pieces “Pieces” show the pieces in the model. You can set options for pieces including: W- One way piece. Flip in X axis, no rotation. S- Allow 180 degree rotation. No Flip. 9- Allow 90 rotation. 4- Allow 45 rotation. F- Allow folds for mirrored pieces. Fabrics The “Fabrics” step allows you to see all the fabrics defined for the models chosen. You can assign names for the markers being created in this step and set the fabric width. Choose the correct fabric spread and the bundling from drop downs before clicking “Process.” This f

pages.title: Activity Log
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Activity Log Use the Activity Log to troubleshoot errors during marker processing. Clicking on this icon, the Activity Log window will automatically display. To close the window, use the X in the upper right corner. The Activity Log records all AccuMark activity processed on the system, including piece verification, order processing and plot processing. Clicking the plus sign will expand the individual entries to provide more information.

pages.title: Add/Delete
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Add/Delete Use this group of functions to add or remove pieces or bundles, as well as to duplicate placed pieces in the marker. A new size can also be added. Add New Size The Add New Size function allows user to add a size that was not originally ordered in the marker.
