This feature regenerates the marker and has the same limitations as copy marker - some pieces may unplaced, split pieces will join. To Add a New Size 1. From the Add/Delete group, select Add New Size 2. Choose the Model Name. 3. Enter the new size to add. The size must exist in the model's size line. Select one size with a mouse click or multiple sizes using the shift or control key. Add Piece Use Add Piece to add pieces to a marker if the model and the order allow for it. Use this function to add a piece during marker making. The Add PC function is found in the Model Form must be checked to be activated for the piece you want to add. In addition, the Add PC/BD field in the Order Form must also be checked. Only those pieces and sizes that currently exist in the marker can be added using Add Piece. To Add a Piece 1. From the Add/Delete group, choose Add Piece. 2. Select the piece you want added to the marker. The piece can be in the marker, the work area, or the icon menu.The piece displays as unplaced in the work area above the marker. It is assigned the next available bundle code and brackets display around the bundle code and the size. 3. You may continue to select pieces from the marker, work area, or icon menu until you have selected all that you want to use. 4. Click the OK button on the Add Piece dialog box to continue. Add Bundle Use this function to retrieve an additional bundle during marker making. The Add PC/BD field in the Model Form must be checked to be activa

pages.title: Assign Keys
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Assign Keys This function allows a user to assign keys on the keyboard to specific functions within marking. Assign keys allow you to customize keys for your most commonly used functions, including the Toolbox in place of the mouse and menus. When clicking on this icon, a dialog box opens. To select from a Category of functions, pick the category from the drop down selections. From the Category selected, scroll and highlight a function to assign a key combination. Press the keys on the keyboard to assign the key combination.

pages.title: Block/Buffer
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Block/Buffer Use this group of functions to modify the perimeter area of pieces set up with blocking or add space around pieces set up for buffering in the Block/Buffer and Laylimits tables. Certain functions in this menu apply only to "small" pieces. Small pieces are those that do not have an M (major piece) assigned to them in the Piece Options field on the Order Entry, Lay Limits Form. Buffer Buffering creates space around a piece that is not visible in Easy Marking.  This buffer "zone" is usually applied to aid in the cut quality of the piece, and surrounding pieces. Buffered pieces will appear in marker making with a dashed boundary.  Buffering can be applied to a segment of a line or to an entire piece.  Buffering creates a higher quality cut, because it prevents the cutting blade from cutting into the edge of an adjacent piece.Adding buffering to a piece does not affect the original cut dimension of the piece. Block Blocking is a visible area added to a piece for marker making.  This “zone” can be used for pieces that are die-cut or matched to the fabric.  The pieces can be plotted with the blocking lines drawn as well as the original perimeter lines.  Automated cutters will cut the outer, blocked perimeters. Block / Block All Use to add an amount of dynamic blocking to all pieces in the marker. Block / Block Small This function adds an amount of dynamic blocking to the small pieces in the marker. Block / Unblock All This function removes an amount of dynamic blocking to all pieces in the marker. Block / Unblock Small This function removes an amount of dynamic blocking to the small pieces in the marker. Buffer / Buffer All This function adds an amount of dynamic buffering to all pieces in the marker. Buffer / Buffer Small This func

pages.title: Block Fuse

links.label: To create a custom shaped block automatically
Workflow for Block Fusing When Using a GERBERcutter

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Block Fuse Use Block Fuse to create blocks in a shell marker and copy them to a fusing marker. Fusing interfacing to the fabric before cutting out the pattern is known as block fusing. This method is used to address concerns about shrinkage of pattern pieces from the fusing process and the fusing process is easier when working with a large piece of material.  Pieces are cut from both self and fusible fabrics in large rectangles and bonded together using heat and pressure.  After fusing, the finished pieces are cut from these rectangles. For example, a shell marker and a fusing marker are created. The parts to be fused are blocked in the shell marker and then copied to the fusing marker. Shell and fusible markers can be ordered at the same time from the Order form. The shell marker includes all the pieces of the garment. The fusing marker includes the fusible pieces from the shell marker. Create Use this function to make up the block for fusing. You have the option of creating either a rectangular perimeter or custom shaped perimeter around pieces. The block fuse amount specified in Preferences will be applied to the perimeter surrounding the selected pieces. Creating a Rectangular Fuse Block To make a rectangular shell marker 1. Select Settings from the View tab. In the Block Fuse section, set Block Notch to On in order to use the Block Notch for placement and save the setting. 2. From the Block Fuse group, select Create. 3. Select the pieces (placed or unplaced) that are to be included in the block. Click Rectangle on the Block Fuse dialog box, and the system automatically creates the block. 4. Place the block in the marker. If additional blocks are needed, repeat the steps 3 and 4. 5. Store the shell marker. 6. From the Block Fuse group

pages.title: Bump Line

links.label: 1. Select the unplaced piece you want to work with.

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Bump Line Use Bump Line functions to create vertical and horizontal lines (constructs) in a marker interactively, and slide pieces up against them. Using the Control Key, you may also create a diagonal bump line. Bump lines can also be deleted or annotated for plotting purposes. Override bump lines by positioning the selected piece over a bump line and then sliding it into place. Once bump lines are created for a marker, they can easily be used or overridden when placing pieces. It all depends on where the unplaced piece is positioned prior to sliding it into the marker. Now in addition to creating Vertical or Horizontal bump lines in Easy Marking, users can use the Control key in Manual mode to allow a diagonal line to be created.  Select Manual from the Bump line panel on the Fabric Tab. The prompt will display to select the start and end point of the bump line. Hold the Control Key while dragging the cursor from the start to the end point of the line, and a diagonal line will be drawn Vertical - Use this function to create a vertical line across the width of the marker. Annotation can then be added to the line. If the width of the marker is changed, the vertical lines are automatically extended or shortened to the new width. These user definable lines are created as solid, stationary lines used for sliding or bumping pieces against. For example, to keep a bundle, such as one jacket, grouped together in the marker, use the vertical lines to visually separate the groups. To Add a Vertical Line 1. From the Bump Line group, choose Vertical. 2. A dialog box displays. Enter the location to insert a line in the marker. The current length of the marker displays as the default entry. Click on OK at this point and a vertical line is created at t

pages.title: Bundle
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Bundle Use this group of functions to manipulate a bundle. Bundles are groups of pieces that make up one complete garment or item. For example, all the pieces for one size 12 jacket would be one bundle in the icon menu. If you choose Select Bundle and selected size 12, one complete garment is moved out of the icon menu and displays in the work area. The functions in this group are used to manipulate bundles that are in the icon menu or already placed in the marker. Flip Bundle To Flip a Bundle Use this function to turn a bundle, placed in a marker, horizontally and then vertically (about the X and Y axes). Use this function to turn a bundle, placed in a marker, horizontally and then vertically (about the X and Y axes). Select Bundle Use this function to bring an entire bundle of pieces down from the icon menu and display them, unplaced, in the work area. You can work with an entire bundle at once instead of bringing each piece out of the icon menu at a time. To Select a Bundle 1. From the Bundle group, choose Select. 2. Select the bundle in the icon menu that you want to retrieve. All of the pieces in the icon menu, corresponding to that bundle, display in the work area. 3. Press Cancel to abort the function. Reset Orientation Use this function to return all the pieces, in a bundle that has been flipped, to their original orientation. To Reset Orientation 1. From the Bundle group, choose Reset Orientation. 2. Select any piece in the marker that is part of the bundle that you want returned to its originally ordered orientation. The system returns each piece to the ordered orientation, and leaves them unplaced in the marker. If any piece in the bundle is married, the marriage is dissolved. 3. Press OK or Cancel to abort the function.

pages.title: Clipboard
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Clipboard Use Copy to Clipboard to copy an image of the marker and use it in other applications for documentation or printing. Copy to Clipboard Copy to Clipboard will create a file that includes the marker and marker information. This file may be pasted into other applications that support images, such as Microsoft Word or a graphics editing tool. Depending on the program to paste into, it is necessary to use the function Paste Special in order to paste the file as an emf file. Copy to Clipboard 1:1 Copy to Clipboard 1:1 will copy the placed marker at full scale allowing the file to be pasted as a special image into a graphics editing tool such as Adobe Illustrator or a program that processes raster images (RIP). The marker image can then be edited to send to a fabric printer. This feature is intended for use with graphics packages. Word processing software does not generally support full marker images.

pages.title: Compact Marker
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Compact Marker Use the Compact Marker function to tighten the marker layout during marking or on previously stored markers. During Compact Marker, pieces are shifted to the left to help shorten the marker. Compacting a marker will help shorten the length, saving fabric and increasing a marker’s efficiency. As a marker is made, the compact tool can help to shift pieces to allow the marker to be shortened.

pages.title: Cut Sequencing

links.label: To define a cut path from the first piece:
To define a cut path from a certain piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Cut Sequencing Use this group of functions to create a cut path through the marker. Cut sequencing in Easy Marking enables you to create a user-defined or automatic cut path through the marker. NOTE: In AccuMark V10.1.0 an enhancement in PDS allows users to select cut sequence within a piece, to define the order and direction of lines being cut on an individual piece basis. Automatic Creates a default cut path through the marker. The path will be shown as a line or as numbers depending on the selection in the Cut Sequencing Parameters. This function is automatically performed. Manual from Beginning This function can be used to create a user-defined cut path, starting with the first piece. The program will first show the default or automatic cut path as a reference. To define a cut path from the first piece: 1. From the Cut Sequencing group, select Manual from Start. 2. Click on the piece that should be cut first. 3. Click on any subsequent pieces to change in order. 4. Click OK to finish and exit the function. Manual after Piece This function can be used to change the cut path starting at a certain piece for as many pieces as needed. The program will first show the default or automatic cut path as a reference. To define a cut path from a certain piece: 1. From the Cut Sequencing group, select Manual after Piece. 2. Click on the first piece to change the order of the cut path. 3. Click on any subsequent pieces to change in order. 4. Click OK to finish and exit the function. Hide/Show Cut Path This is a toggle to display or hide the cut path, if one has been defined. This function is automatically performed. Hide removes the lines or numbers that show the cut path from the marker display. Cut Parameters This dialog box sets what type of bit

pages.title: Display
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Display Use the Display group to modify the color themes for the pieces and work area, refresh the displayed information and define the overall appearance and function behavior within marker making. Refresh When moving pieces on the screen while making markers, something known as "ghosting" may occur. This is residue from moved pieces that shows up as small particles on the screen. To remove these traces, select Refresh. Options and Colors These options allows you to change your color scheme used for pieces and menus in the Easy Marking work environment. Display Options set the icon size for functions to Small, Medium or Large. The Anti Alias checkbox is on by default but can turned off. This checkbox is used to change the display of piece lines. The setting does not impact the plotted lines, only the marker making display of line edges. Anti Alias is a way of smoothing the jagged appearance of diagonal and curved lines in an image. The pixels that surround the edges of the line are changed to varying shades of color in order to blend the sharp edge into the background. On high resolution, newer monitors this enhances the appearance of line display. However, on older monitors this may create a blurry effect or impact performance so turning off this checkbox may be preferred. The background can be set to one solid color or created as a gradient background by blending shades from one color to another. To create a gradient background, select the gradient radio button then selecting two background colors to blend. The piece fill can be selected by setting a color theme: Earth, Sea, Forest, Pink, or Classic Colors. Select the "Fill Unplaced Pieces" checkbox fill the pieces that are not yet placed in the marker. The color fill for the unplaced

pages.title: Dynamic Alteration

links.label: To make an alteration in marker making

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Dynamic Alteration Use this function to modify the geometry of a piece in marker making based on how the Order is set up using Alterations. To apply an alteration during marker making, you must complete the Dynamic Alt Library field in the Order with the name of your Alteration Library. For example, use this function to modify the width of a piece that does not fit in the ordered width of the fabric. To make an alteration in marker making 1. From the Advanced Tab, select Dynamic Alteration. 2. Select the piece you want to alter. You are prompted to enter the alteration rule name, and press OK.. 3. Enter the alteration amount. If the piece does not contain the point number, as listed in the alteration rule, you will get an error message indicating that the requested rule does not exist. 4. Choose OK and the piece will be altered, and appear as unplaced.

pages.title: Fabric Background
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fabric Background Use this group to apply an image of an actual fabric pattern to the background of a marker. Apply Allows the user to set an image as the background fabric for marking. File formats that can be selected include jpg, png, bmp, and gif. To select a fabric background click on Apply. When the dialog box appears, select the image type/file name and set the height and width of the repeat. Remove Removes the graphic image currently being used as the background fabric for marking.

pages.title: Fabric/Trim
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fabric/Trim This feature enables fabric images to be applied directly to the pieces when a Fabric Type is defined in the model. In addition, trim images such as buttons, appliques or logos can be applied to individual pieces and do not need to be associated with a Fabric Type. Once the images are saved in the model, they will automatically be a part of the marker after processing the order. To display images, select “Fabric/Trim” on the Fabric Tab. The display remains sticky until it is turned off by toggling the same function.

pages.title: Flip Marker
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Flip Marker Use these functions to  turn the entire marker (and all pieces in it) horizontally (Flip On X Axis), vertically (Flip On Y Axis), or horizontally and vertically (Flip on X,Y Axis). On X Axis Use this function to flip the entire marker across the X axis, from top to bottom. To flip the marker across the X Axis From the Flip Marker group, choose Flip/on X Axis. On Y Axis Use this function to flip the entire marker across the Y axis. To flip the marker across the Y Axis From the Flip Marker group, choose Flip/on Y Axis. On XY Axis Use this function to flip the entire marker top to bottom and end to end across the X and Y axis To flip the marker From the Flip Marker group, choose Flip/on XY Axis.

pages.title: Grid

links.label: Use this setting to toggle to three different options:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Grid This group designates how the Matching Grid is displayed and defines which Grid number is used for piece placement. Matching Grid If using Standard of Five Star matching on a marker with two or three grids, it may be difficult to work with all of the grid lines displayed on the screen at one time. The Matching Grid also corresponds to the Matching Grid in Settings/Marker Display and updates automatically when changed in the ribbon. Use this setting to toggle to three different options: All - Displays all matching grids in the marker area. Off- Selecting Off turns the grid view off. Active-Displays only the active matching grid in the marking area. The Matching Grid and Grid number fields work together. For example, to place all Backs and Fronts with Grid 1 active, place all Sleeves with Grid 2 active. Use Grid Number Use Grid Number determines the active matching grid for piece placement. It also corresponds to the Use Grid number in Settings/Matching and updates automatically when changed in the ribbon.  The offset 1, 2, or 3 corresponds to the multiple offsets specified in Order Entry. Use Grid Number can be changed at any time during Easy Marking.

pages.title: Layout
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Layout Use the Layout group to customize your work area or reset the entire layout to the original appearance when a component is turned off or closed. Reset Restores the layout to the original appearance (default). Essentials This  layout option will automatically rearrange your work space to make it more efficient.  The Marker Information and the Thumbnail windows will be moved vertically to the left side of the screen and the ribbon will be collapsed, providing more space to manipulate pieces in the work area. The screen layout remains sticky, so new markers will display as intended. At any time, the individual windows can be undocked and relocated to another part of the screen. To return to the default screen layout, select Reset in the Layout group. Quick Access Toolbar Turns the Quick Access Toolbar on or off in the Title bar. Toolbox Hides or Restores the toolbox when it is off or closed. Work Area If you close the work area, the marker display will close. Select "Work Area" from the Layout menu to reopen the work area. Marker Info Hides or restores the Marker Information Dialog. Thumbnail Hides or restores the Thumbnail window. Marker Bookmarks Allows users to preserve the marker in various layout states so that different piece placements can tried, then the marker returned to a previously edited state.  The feature is designed to be used and preserved during the active marking session. The marker is stored without these “revisions.”

pages.title: Marker Properties
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marker Properties Use Marker Properties to view the ordered sizes and edit the Order Number and Order Description of the current marker. Clicking on Marker Properties will open a dialog that displays the sizes, Order Number and Marker Description. To change the Order Number or Marker Description, click in the data field and enter the new information. Then, click on OK to confirm the change. The Order Number and Description can also be updated using File / Save As and clicking on the Options button to display the data fields.

pages.title: Marker
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marker Use this set of functions to duplicate or attach another made marker to the existing marker or split the current marker at a specified location. Copy Use this function to copy the piece placement of a similar marker to the current marker. This time saving function has the system make the marker for you. You may use this on markers that are similar, even if they have size differences. The system determines the placement of pieces based on the geometric center of common piece categories and the order of requested bundles. Copy Marker can be automatically applied in the Order Editor or in Easy Order. To copy a marker 1. Open the newly ordered, unmade marker. 2. From the Marker group, choose Copy. 3. The Lookup dialog box will display a list of stored markers. Select the marker you want to copy, and press the Open button. The system displays the new marker with eligible pieces positioned as they were in the marker you copied. You may see a combination of placed pieces, unplaced pieces, or pieces that remained in the icon menu. Attach Combine up to 99 markers, totaling 20,000 pieces. Markers must have the same matching types, and have the same lay limits, as well as being the same width. Use this function to combine up to 99 markers, totaling 20,000 pieces, or 1000 bundles. You can attach one marker after another using the open dialog box. To combine markers 1. From the Marker group, choose Attach. 2. In the dialog box, select the names of the marker or markers you want to attached to the one currently on the screen. They will appear in the list box located to the right of the open dialog box as they are selected. 3. The selected markers may be re-ordered by selecting a marker, and pressing the "move up" or "move-down" arrows located on

pages.title: Marry
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marry A marriage in a marker is a group of pieces that can be moved and placed without losing their arrangement.  Multiple marriages can exist in a marker.  Each piece can only belong to one marriage at a time. Use this group of functions to form a new marriage of pieces. Create Use to Create a Marriage Between a Group of Pieces. To Create a Marriage: 1.	From the Marry group, select Create. 2.	Click on the pieces to marry.  The selected piece will fill with a dark blue color. 3.	When finished, click OK. Modify Use to add or remove pieces from an existing marriage. To Change an Existing Marriage: 1.	From the Marry group, select Marry and then Modify. 2.	Click on one of the pieces in the marriage.  All the pieces in the marriage will highlight in blue. 3.	Click on a highlighted piece to remove it or click on other pieces to add to the marriage. 4.	When finished, select OK. Delete Use to remove a marriage from the marker. To Remove a Marriage: 1.	From the Marry group, select Marry and then Delete. 2.	Click on one of the pieces in the marriage to remove. 3.	When finished, select OK. Delete All Use to remove all marriages in the marker.  The function is automatically performed.

pages.title: Measure

links.label: To measure the distance between two points
To measure the distance between two pieces
To measure the distance to the edge

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Use the functions in this group to measure distances on the marker. You can measure the distance between two points, two pieces, or from the edge of the marker to a piece. Point to Point Use this function to measure the distance between two points on the marker. To measure the distance between two points 1. From the Measure group, choose Point to Point. 2. Select the first point. This point can be anywhere on the perimeter of the marker or inside the marker. 3. Select the point you are measuring to. The X,Y coordinates display in the status line along with the distance between the two points. Piece to Piece Use this function to measure the distance between two pieces in the marker. To measure the distance between two pieces 1. From the Measure group, choose Piece to Piece 2. Select the first piece that you want to measure from. The piece must be inside the marker. 3. Select the piece you are measuring to. The distance between the two pieces displays in the prompt bar. Piece to Edge Use this function to measure the distance from a piece inside the marker to a selected border line on the perimeter. To measure the distance to the edge 1. From the Measure group, choose Piece to Edge. 2. Select the piece you want to measure from. 3. Select the border line you are measuring to. The distance between the piece and the edge display in the prompt bar.

pages.title: Output
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Output Use this group of functions to generate a marker plot, cut file or send the marker to AutoMark. Send to Plotter - sends the active marker to a plotter through the Marker Plot form. Generate Cut Data - sends the active marker to a cut file through the Cut Generation form. AutoMark - sends the active marker to the AutoMark Editor for processing.

pages.title: Plaid
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Plaid Use the Plaid group to define a vertical repeat, including up to three offsets in Easy Marking. Stripe and plaid offset values can be defined or edited while in Easy Marking. When changing the values in the marker you are not required to reprocess that marker. The system makes the changes automatically. To define a plaid repeat: 1. Click on the Repeat field to edit and type in the repeat value. 2. Click on the Offset drop-down list box to choose Offset 1,2 or 3 The values assigned in the Repeat and Offset fields correspond to the same fields in the Order.

pages.title: Positional Layrules

links.label: To Save a Marker as a Layrule
To save the displayed marker as part of a Layrule Search Parameter Table

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Positional Layrules Use the functions in this menu to create, edit, and store positional layrules. Layrules enable AccuMark to reconstruct previously made markers. The system does this by employing sophisticated search and store techniques that automatically work like an advanced version of Copy Marker. Layrules can alleviate much of the task of placing pieces and can also significantly increase marker storage capacity in a system. Positional layrules store the original position of each piece in a marker.  This enables AccuMark to reconstruct previously made markers during order processing or marker making. Positional Search Use Positional Search to specify a Layrule Search Parameter Table for a Positional Layrule to apply to the displayed marker. The Layrule Search Parameter Table specifies the criteria of the Positional layrule that is applied to the displayed marker. Positional Layrule Search To search for positional layrules 1. From the Positional Layrule group select Search. 2. The Open dialog box displays a list of Layrule Search Parameter Tables in the selected storage area. Select a table and press Open. 3. The system will attempt to find a matching layrule based on the criteria set in the selected parameter table. If a match is found the marker is placed accordingly. Positional Apply Use Apply to specify a layrule to use in making the marker. To Apply a Positional Layrule 1. From the Positional Layrules group, select Apply. 2. In the dialog box, type the name of the layrule or select the name of the layrule from the list. Press Open to accept the selection. 3. The marker is made using the selected layrule. Positional Save Named Saves a Layrule of the displayed marker. To Save a Marker as a Layrule 1. From the Positional Layrules

pages.title: Report Results
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Report Results This function launches the Import Results window and displays the conversion details of an imported marker. The import results can also be displayed immediately after import when "Show Report Results" is turned on in Settings.

pages.title: Return
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Return Use the functions in this group to return pieces or bundles to the piece icon menu. All - Use this function to send all pieces in the work area (placed and unplaced) back to their original orientation in the icon menu. Matching edits are removed. Unplaced - Use this function to send all unplaced pieces in the marker back to their original orientation in the icon menu. Matching edits are removed. Split pieces are merged and all marriages between unplaced pieces are dissolved. Bundle - Use to return a complete bundle back to the menu area. One Piece - This function will put any piece, placed or unplaced, back into the menu.

pages.title: Scoop
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Scoop Use the Scoop function group to increase marker making productivity when making a marker for a large number of small pieces. The Scoop functions are used to select certain pieces from the icon menu and place them in a marker in a specific order. The system remembers the sizes selected and the order and placement of each one. The system then can automatically bring down the groups as created. Using Scoop Create, select certain pieces from the icon menu, and place them in the order. The system remembers the sizes, and the order and placement. The system will then automatically bring down the groups into the marker as created. The selection and placement of these pieces is called a scoop. Scoop Modify Use this function to make changes to the defined sequence of pieces in the scoop. Scoop Modify allows an operator to make modifications to a group of pieces selected as a scoop. Pieces may be added or deleted from the scoop. Select Tools, Scoop Modify from the menu bar to use this function. Scoop Delete Use this function to delete an existing scoop. Scoop Delete allows the deletion of a group selected as a scoop from the function. Select Tools, Scoop delete from the menu bar to use this function. Scoop Apply Use this function to place a scoop into a marker. You cannot apply another scoop until the first one is placed. The pieces will be unplaced and married. They will remain married until you choose Scoop/Apply again. Scoop Apply is selected from the Tool menu bar, and allows the placement of one scoop into the marker. Another scoop may not be applied until the first scoop has been placed. The pieces will be unplaced and married. They will remain married until Scoop Apply is chosen again. Scoop Build Up Use this function once a scoop is e

pages.title: Sliding Layrules

links.label: To apply a Sliding Layrule to a marker

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Sliding Layrules Sliding layrules record the sliding movement of pieces as they are placed into a marker. The purpose of sliding layrules is to build new markers based on the placement of pieces in previously made markers. Sliding layrules store information about the position of pieces, the piece vector history (slide information), and sequence of piece placement. It is done by recording the movement of pieces as they are placed into a marker.Then, new markers can be built based on this information. Note: Bundles added to the marker during marker making are not included in the layrules. Sliding Create Create will record the position of pieces as they are slid into the marker. To Create a Sliding Layrule 1. Make the marker from which you want to create the sliding layrule. 2. From the Sliding Layrules group select Create. The Create Sliding Layrules toolbox will display and placed pieces in the marker will become unplaced. Re-slide the pieces into the marker. As you re-slide the pieces the movements and position will be recorded. 3. The icons in the Create Sliding Layrules tools box can help you manipulate the order of placement if needed. • Moves the piece placement back one step. • Advances the piece placement forward one step. • Inserts a piece placement between two steps. • Deletes the previous step • Saves the layrules. • Saves the layrules using Layrule Search Parameter table criteria. It is recommended that you use the system-generated name. • Cancels and exits the Create Sliding Layrules process Sliding Modify Modify allows you to make a change to an existing Sliding Layrule. To Modify a Sliding Layrule 1. From the Sliding Layrules group, select Modify. The Open dialog box will display a list of layrules in the selected storage are

pages.title: Splice
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Splice Use Splice marks identify where the fabric must overlap when the end of a roll is reached or a fault in the fabric occurs. Splice marks are read in the direction in which the fabric is spread. The first part of the splice mark (the beginning of the bow tie) must be covered by the new roll of fabric. The second part of the splice mark (the end of the bow tie) must be covered by the original roll. Splice marks may be generated automatically by the system, based on values in Settings, and may also be deleted by using this function. Generate Splice will generate splices for the whole marker. Delete Splice will allow the user to delete one splice at a time from the marker. Automatic Use this function to create splice marks on the marker using the setting established in Settings. Settings/Splice marks can be generated in Marker Making or when you are ready to plot. The difference is that, in marking, splice marks can also be viewed, deleted, or re-generated if needed. If you add, move, or remove pieces from the marker after generating splice marks, you must choose this function again to generate new splice marks. To create automatic splice marks 1. From the Splice group, choose Automatic. 2. Depending upon the settings chosen on the View tab for Settings / Splice, the splice mark (or marks) display on the marker. Manual This provides the ability to create Manual Splices by selecting two points to add a splice. The width of the splice is based on the minimum and maximum values in the Settings dialog. Delete Use this function to remove any unwanted splices from a marker. To delete splices 1. From the Splice group, choose Splice/Delete. 2. Click the splices to be removed. 3. Press Cancel when you have finished deleting splices, or to abort

pages.title: Split Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Split Piece Use the Split Piece functions in this group to dynamically split a piece during marker making. Pieces can be manually split at a specified location or by entering a percentage from the edges of the piece where the split is to occur. Pieces that were split can also be joined back together. Points to Remember… • In order for pieces to be split, you must indicate the number of times a piece can be split in the model file. • The Piece cannot be in a marriage. Manual Use this function to manually select where you want a piece to split. Left Use this function to specify the amount or percentage that you want the piece to split, measuring from the left edge. Right Use this function to specify the amount or percentage that you want the piece to split from the right edge. Top Use this function to specify the amount or percentage that you want the piece to split from the top edge. Bottom Use this function to specify the amount or percentage that you want the piece to split from the bottom edge. Join Use this function to combine two pieces that were split using one of the other functions in the Piece/Dynamic Split menu. You must join a piece in the reverse order it was split. If you don’t, the system will display the error message, "Join the other half of piece first." Repeat the procedure, making sure you are selecting the pieces in reverse order.

pages.title: Stripe
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Stripe Use the Stripe group to define a vertical horizontal repeat, including up to three offsets in Easy Marking. Stripe and plaid offset values can be defined or edited while in Easy Marking. When changing the values in the marker you are not required to reprocess that marker. The system makes the changes automatically. To define a stripe repeat: 1. Click on the Repeat field to edit and type in the repeat value. 2. Click on the Offset drop-down list box to choose Offset 1,2 or 3 The values assigned in the Repeat and Offset fields correspond to the same fields in the Order.

pages.title: Translate Data
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Translate Data Use this function to display user defined annotation in another language by  selecting a translation library and display language. Translate Data PDS Annotation, Piece Annotation and Marker Annotation can be translated into any language. The AccuMark has always supported other languages for menu items but it has not been possible to translate user defined annotation. This option displays the Translate Data dialog box. The translation library and the display language can be selected in this dialog. The translated data can be plotted. This enhancement is not backwards compatible to versions prior to 8.4.0. Exporting data into AAMA and ASTM format will not include the translated annotation. The translation library, datatranslation.txt, contains a line of text in multiple languages. The text file can be located on a local or network drive. The first line of the text file contains an equals sign, ‘=Language’ followed by the languages supported in the translation library. The user can specify which languages will be supported. The same number of languages needs to be listed for every entry. The next contains ‘=Tag’ followed by an optional abbreviation. If the system finds the abbreviation, it will replace it with the string of the selected language. The following lines of text include the text string in every language supported by the library. If no abbreviation is needed, ‘=String’ is used followed by the lines of translations.

pages.title: Unplace
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Unplace Use the functions in this group to unplace pieces or bundles in the marker. All - Use this function to change the status of all pieces currently in the marker. This unplaces the pieces without the pieces affecting their position in the marker. Unplaced pieces are not calculated in the marker area, perimeter, efficiency and cannot be plotted or cut. Small - This function will take the small pieces out of the marker, but will not change their positions. After being unplaced, the piece is not part of the current calculation of utilization. Small pieces are those that are not assigned the M (major piece) option in the Laylimits. The function is automatically performed. If a small piece is married, the marriage is dissolved. Unplace Bundle - Use this function to reposition an entire bundle from the marker to the work area. The bundle must have already been placed into the marker. An unplaced piece positioned in the marker is not eligible for plotting, cutting, and will not be calculated in the area, length or efficiency of the marker. To Unplace a Bundle 1. From the Unplace group, choose Unplace Bundle. 2. Select one of the pieces that are in the bundle that you want to reposition (unplace). All the pieces that make up that bundle are outlined in a dotted line. 3. If pieces were married, they are removed from the marriage.

pages.title: User Environment
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search User Environment Selecting User Environment to view or change notation, decimal precision used in numeric entries. It also sets the default value for the spllit piece seam amount, overwrite marker preference and Layrule mode.

pages.title: Window
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Window Use the Split functions to display multiple markers horizontally or vertically in the work area. Split Horizontal Use this function to display markers horizontally. Split Vertical Use this function to display markers side by side.

pages.title: Zoom
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Zoom Use the Zoom group to increase the viewing size of the marker area. Zoom Use Zoom to enlarge a portion of the work area to view more closely. Select Normal to return to a regular view. Normal Returns marker display to regular view. Big Scale Use this function to enlarge the view of the marker area on your screen. You can select Normal to return to regular view. Full Length Use this function to reduce the image of your pieces so the entire marker displays on the screen. Select Full Length again to return the marker to normal size. Zoom Window This feature allows a user to view two independent marking windows of the current marker. There are three toolbars in the zoom window. Zoom, Full Length, Big Scale.

pages.title: Marker Bookmarks
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marker Bookmarks A new feature has been added under the Easy Marking View Menu to allow users to preserve the marker in various layout states so that different piece placements can tried, then the marker returned to a previously edited state.  The feature is designed to be used and preserved during the active marking session. The marker is stored without these “revisions.” User stored states appear with a while background in the list. AutoSaved versions of the marker layout appear in a grey background in the grid. While editing the marker, select “Store” in this View window to preserve marker layout, then continue editing. If your further edits do not produce the more efficient results, simply click on one of the previously user stored states (or AutoSaved states) then click “Restore”

pages.title: Overview of Easy Marking
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Overview of Easy Marking Marker Marking is the process of placing pattern pieces into a marker which represents the fabric from which it is to be cut. The task is to place the pieces in a way that makes the best utilization of the material to be used. Depending upon the limits set up in the Marker Order, pieces can be flipped, rotated, or overlapped during marker making. When you first access the Easy Making software, the main ribbon menu displays. This menu allows you to choose functions to retrieve a marker from either the default storage area or to choose a different storage area. Once a marker is retrieved, the marking window displays on the screen along with all of its elements. This is where all of the work that is necessary to create a marker is done. The Easy Marking Elements: Title Bar Quick Access Toolbar Ribbon Toolbox Piece Area Display Marking Work Area Scroll Bar Prompt Bar Marker Information Toolbar Thumbnail

pages.title: Advanced Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Advanced Tab Functions in the Advanced tab are used to modify pieces and position them in the marker. Cut sequencing can also be defined. Split Piece Dynamic Alteration Positional Layrules Sliding Layrules Cut Sequencing

pages.title: Fabric Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fabric Tab Use the Fabric group to modify the marker characteristics such as fabric repeats, backgrounds and block fusing or splices. Block Fuse Splice Bump Line Fabric Background Fabric/Trim Plaid Stripe Grid

pages.title: Marker Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Marker Tab Use the functions in this menu to maneuver pieces when making a marker. Clipboard Output Flip Marker Marker Measure Scoop Compact Marker

pages.title: Piece Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Piece Tab Us the Piece Tab to manipulate pieces and bundles in the marker. Return Add/Delete Unplace Bundle Block/Buffer Marry

pages.title: View Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Tab Use the View Tab to manage the screen layout, colors and themes as well as the zoom states for viewing the marker area. This group also includes keyboard functions and translation text viewed in the current marker. Display User Environment Marker Properties Report Results Activity Log Zoom Assign Keys Translate Data Layout Window

pages.title: Adjust Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Adjust Line Use to lengthen or shorten a line by selecting the end point to move. To Adjust a Line Length: 1.	From the Line Actions group on the Modify tab, select Adjust. 2.	Select a line to change the length. 3.	Select the end point to adjust. 4.	Move the end point by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the end point. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the amount to adjust the line.

pages.title: Anchor Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Anchor Line Use to move a line while maintaining the original length.  Locations can be selected on the adjacent lines for blending locations. To Move Line Anchor: 1.	From the Line Actions group on the Modify tab, Anchor or press the CTRL + F3 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Select Reference Location – use to control the line movement at a selected point. •	Show Thumbtacks – controls the display of the thumbtacks for defining a range.  Showing the thumbtacks will allow the user to define the range as a part of the function.  If this button is not selected, the range is automatically assigned based on the other options, Prev/Next Points or End Points. •	Prev/Next Points – places the thumbtacks at the point before and the point after the selected line by default. •	End Points – places the thumbtacks at the end points of the adjacent lines by default. 3.	Select line(s) to move.  If multiple lines are selected, they must be adjacent and on the same piece.  When finished, select OK. 4.	If Show Thumbtacks was selected, reposition the thumbtacks to define the range or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks. 5.	If the Select Reference Location option was checked, select a point to guide the line movement. 6.	Position the line in either cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the line. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the distance from the original line in the Dist or X and Y fields.

pages.title: Clip Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Clip Line Use to trim an internal line at an intersection with another line. To Clip a Line: 1.	From the Line Actions group on the Modify Tab, select Clip or press the CTRL + F8 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select the internal line to clip on the side to keep. 3.	If the internal line crosses more than one line, select the intersecting line to clip at.

pages.title: Combine Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Combine Line Use to join two or more perimeter or internal lines.  End of line symbols become intermediate points; graded end of line symbols become grade points.  Use this function before trying to delete an end point. To Merge Lines Together: 1.	From the Modify tab Line Actions group, select Combine or press the CTRL + F9 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Add Notch at Merge Point – check to add a notch where the two lines are joined. •	Type – If Add Notch at Merge Point was chosen, this setting controls the kind of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. •	Depth – determines the depth of a notch for MicroMark notches.  Type in the desired depth.  This option is only available for MicroMark users. •	N Attribute – check this option to make the base point of the notch a non-smoothing point. 3.	Select lines to merge.  When merging internals, select near the beginning of the lines.  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Curve Line
pages.bodySummary:
Filter: All Files Submit Search Curve Line This function will change an existing curved line or make a curve out of a straight line.  Intermediate points will be added to a straight line to hold the curve, if none exist. To Modify a Curve: 1.	From the Line Actions group on the Modify tab, select  Curve. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Show Thumbtacks – controls the display of the thumbtacks for defining a segment of a line.  Showing the thumbtacks will allow the user to define the segment as a part of the function.  If this button is not selected, the segement is automatically assigned based on the other options, Prev/Next Points or End Points. •	Prev/Next Points – places the thumbtacks at the point before and the point after the selected point by default.  
•	End Points – places the thumbtacks at the end points of the line by default. 3.	Select the line to change. 4.	If Show Thumbtacks was selected, reposition the thumbtacks to define the segment to change or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks. 5.	Reshape the curve in cursor or value mode:
•	Cursor Mode – left click to place the curve.
•	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the distance to move the selected point in the X and Y fields.

pages.title: Flatten Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Flatten Line Use to delete all of the intermediate points on a line segment with an option to keep the notches and dart points. To Flatten a Line Segment: 1.	From the Line Actions group on the Modify Tab, select Flatten or press the CTRL + F12 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Delete Notches – select to remove notches from the segment. •	Delete Dart Points – select to remove dart points from the segment. 3.	Select the line to flatten. 4.	Reposition the thumbtacks to define the segment to flatten or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks.

pages.title: Line Length
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Line Length Use this function to change the length of a curved line segment.  The end points will remain stationary, the intermediate points move to lengthen or shorten the curve. To Modify a Line Length: 1.	From the Line Actions group on the Modify tab, select Length. 2.	Select the curved line to change length. 3.	Reposition the thumbtacks to define the segment of the line to change or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks. 4.	Enter the desired length of the line.

pages.title: Move Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Move Line Use to move a line to a new location.  The line will be able to move in any direction.  This is useful when moving grain or annotation lines. To Move a Line: 1.	From the Line Actions group on the Modify tab, Move Line or press the CTRL + F2 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Select Reference Location – use to control the line movement at a selected point. •	Move Multi Line in Reverse – when checked, two selected lines will move in opposite directions. 3.	Select line(s) to offset.  When finished, select OK. 4.	If the Select Reference Location option is checked, select a point to guide the line movement. 5.	Position the line in either cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the line. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the distance from the original line in the Dist or X and Y fields

pages.title: Offset Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Offset Line Use to move a line to a new location, keeping it parallel to the original.  This function does not maintain the length of the original line. To Move Offset: 1.	From the Line Actions group on the Modify Tab,select Offset. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Select Reference Location – use to control the line movement at a selected point. •	Move Multi Line in Reverse – when checked, two selected lines will move in opposite directions. 3.	Select line(s) to offset.  When finished, select OK. 4.	If the Select Reference Location option is checked, select a point to guide the line movement. 5.	Position the line in either cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the line. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the distance from the original line in the Dist field.  Use a negative value to move the line inside the piece; a positive value to move the line outside the piece.

pages.title: Parallel Line

links.label: To Make a Line Parallel to Another Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Parallel Line Use to make a selected line(s) parallel to another line or the X or Y-axis. This function is useful to make a grain line parallel to the center front, after using the Silhouette Table to input the pattern as a knockoff. To Make a Line Parallel to Another Line: 1.	From the Modify Tab, select  Parallel from the Line Actions group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Line – makes the selected line parallel to another line on the piece. •	X Axis – makes the selected line horizontal. •	Y Axis – makes the selected line vertical. 3.	Select the line(s) to move.  When finished, select OK. 4.	If Line was chosen, select another line on the piece to use as a guide. 5.	Select the point on the line to remain stationary.  This is the point the line will pivot about to become parallel to the selected location.

pages.title: Replace Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Replace Line Use to change one or more internal lines into perimeter lines. The internal line (or group of internals) must intersect the perimeter at both ends. To Replace a Line: 1.	From the Modify Tab, Line Actions group select Replace or press the ALT + R keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Use Perimeter – applies the point information such as special point numbers, attributes, and grading from the perimeter line to the new perimeter intersection. •	Use Internal – applies the point information such as special point numbers, attributes, and grading from the internal line to the new perimeter intersection. •	Maintain Graded Nest – when checked, the system will calculate rules for the new perimeter intersections that maintain the original grading. 3.	Select the internal line(s).  When finished, select OK. 4.	Select the start and end points for perimeter replacement.

pages.title: Rotate Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Rotate Line Use to change the orientation of a line by a specific angle or distance while holding one point constant. To Rotate a Line: 1.	From the Modify Tab Line Actions group, select Rotate. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Select Reference Location – use to control the line movement at a selected point. •	Bump to Line – use to rotate a line until it touches another line at a certain point. 3.	Select line(s) to pivot.  When finished, select OK. 4.	Select the pivot point using one of the following methods: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to use as a pivot point. •	Value Mode – left click and drag the cursor to the point to measure from, click the right button and release both buttons.  Enter a distance in the Beg or End fields to place the pivot point. •	Right Mouse Button Menu – right click in the work area and select the desired option.  Read and follow the prompts for the steps to perform the function. 5.	If the Select Reference Location option is checked, select a point to guide the line movement. 6.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Bump to Line is checked, select a line to bump to.  The line will rotate until it touches this line. •	If Bump to Line is not checked, pivot the line by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the line. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the amount to rotate in the Dist (inches) or Ang (degrees) fields.

pages.title: Set/Rotate Line

links.label: To Set and Rotate a Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Set/Rotate Line Use to move an internal line to match exactly to a point on another line.  Once the line is moved, it can be pivoted to any angle.  The second point selected may be on the same piece or a different piece. To Set and Rotate a Line: 1.	From the Modify Tab, Line Actions Group, select Set/Rotate. 2.	Select match point on line to set (line to move). 3.	Select match point on target line (stationary line). 4.	Pivot the line by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the line. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the angle to rotate the line in the Ang field.

pages.title: Smooth Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Smooth Line Use to smooth a curved perimeter or internal line.  Points such as notches and intermediates are repositioned along the line.  Be aware that a curved line can be smoothed several times, but will flatten out more each time. To Smooth a Line: 1.	From the Modify Tab, select Line Actions group then Smooth. 2.	If desired, change the Smooth Factor.  (see NOTE below) 3.	Select the line to smooth. 4.	Reposition the thumbtacks to define the segment to smooth or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks. 5.	Select OK to smooth once.  If desired, select OK again to repeat the smoothing.  Select Cancel to exit smoothing. NOTE:  To smooth, the system calculates the distance from the smoothing point to a straight line drawn between the two adjacent points.  If the distance is greater than the smooth factor, the smoothing point is turned into an intermediate point.  If the distance is smaller, the point remains as a system smoothing point.

pages.title: Split Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Split Line Use to divide a single line into multiple lines.  When a line is split at an intermediate point, the point  will become an end of line point; when splitting at a grade point, the point will become a graded end of line point. To Split a Line: 1.	From the Modify Tab, Line Actions, select Split or press the CTRL + F10 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select the split location using one of the following methods: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to split the line. •	Value Mode – left click and drag the cursor to the point to measure from, click the right button and release both buttons.  Enter a distance in the Beg or End fields. •	Right Mouse Button Menu – right click in the work area and select the desired option. Read and follow the prompts for the steps to perform the function.

pages.title: Swap Line
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Swap Line Use to exchange a perimeter line with an internal line in order to create a new piece perimeter.  The internal line does not have to intersect the perimeter.  The system automatically extends or shortens adjacent line to close the perimeter. To Swap a Line: 1.	From the Modify Tab, select Swap Line from the Line Actions group or press the ALT + S keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Delete Original Line – when checked, the original perimeter line will be removed after the swap is performed. •	Use Perimeter – applies the point information such as special point numbers, attributes, and grading from the perimeter line to the new perimeter intersection. •	Use Internal – applies the point information such as special point numbers, attributes, and grading from the internal line to the new perimeter intersection. •	Maintain Graded Nest – when checked, the system will calculate rules for the new perimeter intersections that maintain the original grading. 3.	Select the internal line(s).  When finished, select OK. 4.	Select the perimeter line(s).  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Anchor Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Anchor Piece To anchor piece(s) in the work area so they cannot be accidentally repositioned.  The anchor status displays in the center of each piece. To Anchor or Unanchor Piece(s): 1.	From the Piece menu, select Modify Piece and then Anchor/Unanchor. 2.	Select the piece(s) to lock or unlock.  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Combine Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Combine Piece Makes two pieces into one piece.  Several grading options are available. The graded nest of the original pieces can be restacked using the Z and R attributes or the function View / Grade / Stack On/Off before they are combined.  Restacking will adjust the grading in the area the pieces area to be combined. To Combine Two Pieces Together: 1.	Arrange the pieces on the work area to be combined or merged. 2.	From the Modify Tab Piece Actions Group, select Combine. 3.	Select from the following User Input options: Grade Options •	Create Modified Rules – the grade rules on the merged piece are modified, so the piece maintains its nest in the new orientation. •	Alternate Grade Ref Line – the grain line on the merge piece becomes an alternate grade reference line. •	Target Piece Grade Ref Line – the grain line on the target piece becomes the new grain line, but the grade rules are not modified. Merge Line Rules •	Keep All Rules – all rules on both pieces are maintained. •	Keep Target Piece Rules – use to keep only the grade rules on the target piece at the merge location. •	Remove Rules – use to create no growth at the merge location. •	Delete Original Pieces – removes the original piece from the work area.  This option does NOT remove the piece from the icon menu or storage area. •	Convert Merge Line Into Internal – the merge line will become an internal line labeled I. •	Add Piece to Model/Style – use to add the new pieces to the current style or model. Category Copy Original Piece Name 4.	Select the merge line.  This is the line where the two pieces will be attached.  The piece that this line was selected on will move or rotate to match the other piece. 5.	Select the target line. This piece will not move during the function. 6.	If

pages.title: Flip Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Flip Piece Flips a piece along a line or in one of four quadrants. To Flip a Piece: 1.	From the Modify Tab, select Flip from the Piece Actions group or press the SHIFT + F9 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Flip About Line – flips a piece over a selected line. •	Flip About Common Line – flips a group of pieces over a single line. •	Flip Piece – flips a piece according to the selected quadrant. •	Quadrant – used with the Flip Piece option to determine direction of flip. 3.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Flip About Line was chosen, select a line(s) on the piece to flip about and select OK. •	If Flip About Common Line was chosen, select the piece(s) to flip and select OK.  Select a line to flip pieces over.  All selected pieces will flip. •	If Flip Piece was chosen, select one of the four quadrants pictured in the User Input box. Select the piece(s). Select OK. 4.	To save the flipped piece: •	In its new position - prior to saving, use Piece/Modify Piece/Realign Grain with the Realign Grain option selected. Select the grain line. •	In it’s original position, use the Save or Save As function.  The piece will be saved in its original orientation.

pages.title: Fold Keep Piece

links.label: To Use Fold Keep on a Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fold Keep Piece Use this function to divide a piece and discard the rest of the geometry.  The new piece can automatically have seam allowance added to the fold line. To Use Fold Keep on a Piece: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Fold Keep in the Piece Actions panel or press the SHIFT + K keys on the keyboard.. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Select Line – divides the piece along an existing line and discards the unwanted portion. •	Match 2 Points – folds the piece by selecting 2 points to fold the piece.  The piece will be divided on the fold line. •	Fold Internals – maintains the internal lines from the side of the piece that will be discarded. Those internals will be mirrored across the fold (division) line and maintained on the part of the piece that is kept. •	Mirror Piece – turns the fold line into a mirror line on the new piece. •	Fold After Mirror – if Mirror Piece was chosen, the new piece will be folded on the work area. 3.	Depending on the options chosen, the selection changes: •	If Select Line was chosen, select the line to divide the piece. •	If Match 2 Points was chosen, select the two points to match to create a fold line. 4.	Enter the seam allowance amount for the folding line. 5.	Select the side of the piece to keep by left clicking on it.

pages.title: Mirror Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Mirror Piece To create a piece that has two symmetrical halves. To Mirror a Piece: 1.	From the Modify Tab, select Mirror from the Piece Actions group. 2.	Select from the following User Input Options: •	Fold after Mirror – to automatically fold the piece after it has been mirrored. •	None – to NOT notch the mirror line. •	Add Notches – to add a notch at one or both ends of the mirror line. •	Add Intersection Notches – to add intersection notches at one or both ends. •	Type – controls the kind of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. •	Depth – determines the depth of a notch for MicroMark notches.  Type in the desired depth. 3.	Select the mirror line. Select OK. 4.	If Single End was selected under either notch option, select which end of the mirror line will be notched.

pages.title: Move Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Move Piece Use to move a piece a specific distance or to positioning on another piece. When positioning on another piece can be also performed by turning ON Snap to Geometry. Options: Select option Position to Piece or X/Y if you wish to snap to other piece geometry or to move the piece in value mode using X/Y amounts. Select Lock to Grid to move a piece and snap it to a Grid position. Grid values must be setup in Screen Layout located in the Edit tab under Workspace menu. Rotate after Lock is only available when using Lock to Grid and allows you to rotate a piece after it has been positioned in a grid location.

pages.title: Open Mirror
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Open Mirror Converts a mirrored piece to a closed (not mirrored) piece.  This can be done when the piece is folded or unfolded. To Open a Mirrored Piece: 1.	From the Modify Tab, Piece Actions menu, select Open. 2.	Select the mirrored piece(s) to open. When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Realign Piece

links.label: To Realign a Piece or Grainline:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Realign Piece Changes the grain line to match the new orientation of a piece or to reorient a piece according to its primary grain line.  The Orientation Symbol indicates the primary grain line.  This is often used after performing the function(s):  Move, Flip, and Rotate Piece or any of the Line functions that alters or creates a grain line. To Realign a Piece or Grainline: 1.	From the Modify Tab, Piece Actions group select Realign or press the SHIFT + F5 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Realign Piece – moves the whole piece to make the grain line horizontal on the work area. •	Realign Grain/Grade Ref – rotates the grain line to be horizontal on the work area. 3.	Select the piece or the grain line depending on which option is chosen. Realign Piece  has a right click option to Select All pieces in the work area. This allows multiple pieces to quickly realign to the original orientation after modifications have been made. To realign multiple pieces: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Realign Grain from the Piece Actions panel. 2.	Check the Realign Grain option located in the Value Input panel. 3.	Right click in the work area and choose Select All.

pages.title: Rotate Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Rotate Piece Use to pivot a piece about a selected point. Holding down the Shift key while rotating a piece will rotate the piece in 45 degree increments.   Make sure to set the user input options to “None” for the increment to use this feature To Rotate a Piece: 1.	From the Modify tab, select  Rotate from the Piece Actions group or press the SHIFT + F10 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Select Reference Location – use to select a specific point to measure rotation amount. •	Perform Alignment – rotates a piece to align with the X or Y axis. •	Increment – use to rotate a piece by common pre-defined amounts.  Select None to rotate the piece in cursor or value mode.  Select the increment and the direction, either clockwise (CW) or counter-clockwise (CCW). •	Alignment – use this option along with Perform Alignment.  Choose X Axis or Y Axis to define the direction for alignment. 3.	Select the piece(s) to rotate.  When finished, select OK. 4.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If an Increment was chosen, the piece will rotate that amount.  Left click on the piece to rotate the piece again by the defined increment.  When finished, select OK. •	If None was chosen in the Increment option, select a pivot point on the piece. If Select Reference Location was chosen, select the point to measure from. Pivot the piece by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the piece. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the amount to rotate in the Dist (inches) or Ang (degrees) fields. •	If Perform Alignment was chosen, select a pivot point on the piece. If Select a Reference Location was chosen, select a second point to define the area to align.

pages.title: Set/Rotate Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Set/Rotate Piece Use to position two pieces together at a match point and then pivot one piece to a new angle.  This function is useful when two pieces need to be overlapped in order to use the Trace functions or to check patterns for accuracy.  The User Input box and right button menu can be used to select points by measurement and define specific locations. To Set & Rotate a Piece: 1.	From the Modify tab, select  Set and Rotate from the Piece Actions group or press the SHIFT + F12 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Specify Location to Bump – determines whether an actual line or a system-generated line is used as a reference measurement.  If the option is checked, the system will use a straight line drawn between the match point and the set point on the set piece.  If unchecked, the system uses the actual perimeter line of the pattern piece between the match point and set point on the set piece. •	Perform Alignment – rotates a piece to align with the X or Y axis. •	Alignment – use this option along with Perform Alignment.  Choose X Axis or Y Axis to define the direction for alignment. 3.	Select the match point on the target piece(s) (A in the example below).  The target piece will not move during the function. 4.	Select the match line on the target piece (B in the example below). 5.	Select the match point on the set piece (C in the example below).  The set piece will move and rotate during the function. 6.	Select the set point on the set piece (D in the example below). 7.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Perform Alignment was chosen, the set piece will align with the chosen axis. •	If Perform Alignment was not chosen, pivot the piece by cursor or val

pages.title: Color Management Profiles
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Color Management Profiles Fabric and trim images added to pieces can be used in digital printing.  To ensure that colors match well through the process, color management profiles have been added to the image selection options in Pattern Design.  A color management profile is a mathematical description of the color used in an image.  All devices and software used in the process can be mapped to this profile to assist in color matching.  All images assigned in PDS now require a color management source profile to be assigned to the selected image. If an image contains an embedded profile, that profile is honored but the user may change it at any time. There is a new command in the File menu called Color Management.  Selections made in this function define how the color profile should be selected for each type of image.  This selection would be applied when an embedded profile is not found in the image.  “Always Ask” will prompt at the time the image is placed for a selection.  If a profile is selected here, it will be used each time for that type of image. If “Always Ask” is selected, you will see this dialog when an image is selected with no embedded color profile: The dialog shows the color space of the image, the image path/name and gives a list of all the image’s color space profiles on their system. Select the color profile to use in this dialog and select OK.  If you find you are always selecting the same color profile, click on Preferences and select it as the Default. In the Edit Image function, the assigned profile can be seen and changed as with images in the Image Properties dialog. In this example the system found that the selected image has an embedded profile and we will use it for the assignment. At any time the user is allowe

pages.title: Commands for a Custom Toolbar

links.label: Learn How to Create a Custom Toolbar:
Learn How to Move and Dock Toolbars

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Commands for a Custom Toolbar Customizing a toolbar can make for a more efficient work flow and make accessing functions easier. Learn How to Create a Custom Toolbar: 1.	From the Edit tab, select Custom Toolbars from the Customize function in the Workspace Group. 2.	The Custom Toolbar dialog box displays.  Select menu name from the Command Category box at the top of the dialog box. 3.	To add a button, left click and drag the desired function icon from the Custom Toolbar window.  The button can be placed in an existing tool bar or create a new custom tool bar by dragging the button onto the work area. 4.	When finished selecting toolbar buttons, select OK.  Select Reset to Saved to return the tool bar to its previous setting without saving the new changes. 5.	The toolbar will be saved when Pattern Design is exited. NOTE: To remove a custom toolbar button, right click over the desired button or toolbar. Select OK.  To remove an entire toolbar, left click and drag the toolbar into the work area and click the X in the upper right corner of the toolbar. Learn How to Move and Dock Toolbars Tool bars use standard Windows methods for dragging and docking.  A custom toolbar can be docked to a side of the screen or left free floating over the work area.  When Pattern Design is closed, it will be saved in that position. Listed below are some basic guidelines for moving and docking toolbars. •	To Dock a toolbar – drag a tool bar by its title bar or border to a screen edge and release when the outline becomes narrow or double click on the gray border of the icon or toolbar to dock it. •	To prevent a toolbar from docking – hold down the CTRL key while dragging the toolbar. •	To Un-dock a toolbar or icon – double click on the gray border.
