links.label: To Create a Dart With Added Fullness:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Darts Add Three options are available for Adding Darts: Add, Add with Fullness, and Fisheye. Add: Use to add a dart; the function does not add fullness to compensate for the dart. The dart will be cut out of the existing shape of the piece. To Add a Dart: 1.	From the Advanced Tab, select Darts and then Add Dart dropdown, then Add Dart. 2.	Select the new opening point where the dart fold line is to be located using one of the following methods: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the point to place the new dart. •	Value Mode – left click and hold on the line to place the dart, click right and release both buttons.  Enter the distance on the selected line to place the dart in the Beg or End fields. •	Right Mouse Button Menu – right click in the work area and select the desired option.  Read and follow the prompts for the steps to perform the function. 3.	A perpendicular line will be drawn from the new opening point.  Select the apex for the new dart in cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the apex of the new dart. •	Value Mode – click both buttons together and release.  Enter the length of the dart in the Dist field. 4.	Enter the dart width. Add with Fullness: Use to add a dart; the function adds fullness to the pattern to compensate for the dart. To Create a Dart With Added Fullness: 1.	From the Advanced Tab, select the Add dropdown from the Darts Group then Add with Fullness. 2.	Select the new opening point where the dart fold line is to be located using one of the following methods: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the point to place the new dart. •	Value Mode – left click and hold on the line to place the dart, click right and release both buttons.  Enter the distance on the selected line to place the dart in the Beg or End

pages.title: Convert Darts
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Convert Darts In previous versions, this function was applied to those darts that were originally digitized and later on user wanted to convert them to a valid PDS dart. Now it covers three possible conversions: Darts created in previous versions (up to version 10.0) as part of the digitized perimeter lines are converted into objects by making one of the two following options: •	By selecting the 1st and last point to create a dart as object; or •	Tip of the dart already exists. An existing dart created in PDS in previous versions is converted to object. A new dart as object is turned back as regular dart (non-object) Before performing this function, the dart legs must be merged into one line and should be connected with the piece perimeter. To Convert to Dart: 1.	From the Advanced Tab, select Convert Darts from the Darts Group. 2.	Select the dart tip (apex). 3.	Select the first point of the dart (moving clockwise). 4.	Select the last point of the dart (moving clockwise).

pages.title: Fold Darts
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fold Darts Folding a dart replaces an open/cut dart (one that is cut out of the perimeter of a piece) with an internal dart sewing line, notches, and a drill hole. The Fold Dart tool also modifies the perimeter of the piece to compensate for folding. To Fold a Dart: 1.	From the Advanced Tab, select Fold Dart from the Darts Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Include Fold Lines – select to create internal lines at the location of dart legs. •	Include Drill Hole – select to put a drill hole a specified distance from the dart apex. •	Include Notches – select to create notches on the perimeter at the end of the dart legs. •	Notch Type – select the number of notch to be added. 3.	Select the dart leg on the side the fabric will be folded toward. 4.	If Include Drill Hole was chosen, enter the distance of the drill hole from the apex.

This function can be used on either folded or open darts. To Pivot a Dart: 1.	From the Advanced Tab, select the Manipulate Darts drop down, then Rotate. 2.	Select the dart to pivot by left clicking anywhere on the dart legs. 3.	Select a dart opening option. pages.title: Open Darts
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Open Darts Use to change a folded dart into a cut out dart.  This function is helpful to use before the Change Dart Tip function. Open/Close Dart basically performs the same action as Asymmetric Dart fold. However, when using this function in dart objects, users are able to exit out and come back into the function to continue selecting more darts, meaning that multiple darts can be selected at once or at any time in the same piece. To Open a Dart: 1.	From the Advanced Tab, select  Open Dart from the Darts Group. 2.	Select the dart to open between the notches on the perimeter.

pages.title: Edit Seam Properties
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Seam Properties Seam Properties can be set prior to defining seams.  These properties indicate how the seam allowance should be graded.  Choose from the following options: Maintain Seam Properties – uses the settings already applied to the piece to grade the seam allowance. Edit Seam Properties – uses the settings in the Seam Properties box to grade seam allowance. •	Seam Extension - allows for invisible extensions to be drawn out from intersections of sew lines when seam allowance is defined.  These extensions prevent the shape of the corner from changing if the sew and cut lines are swapped.  To see these extensions, set the perimeter to Unclipped in Preferences/Options. •	Generate Seam/Corners – seams and corners are drawn on each graded size. •	Grade Seam/Corners – seams and corners will have grade rules applied to create the shape on each graded size. •	Auto Update Seam – used with Grade Seam/Corners.  Changes the sew and cut lines together as the piece is modified. Ignore Grade Rules- Grade Rules assigned to the base size are ignored in the seam lines. Grade Rules are automatically calculated to maintain the piece geometry in all sizes. •	Adjust Seam Grading – used with Grade Seam/Corners.  Modifies the grade rules to keep the seam lines parallel on all graded sizes. Copy Grade Rules- The grade rule used in the base size/main boundary line is always copied onto the seam internal line.

pages.title: Edit Dart
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Dart .Edit Dart allows you to edit a fisheye dart, either by eye, moving the control points (hot spots) or by editing the fisheye dart values. With the introduction of version 10.1, PDS saves in the piece memory the original values entered in the fisheye User Input box: •	Fisheye dart as object allows you to create multiple fisheye darts. When editing, the fisheye dart measurements are remembered so you can edit one dart at a time. •	When working on Click & Go mode, hold down the Control key to activate the hotspots. Release. Pick the hotspot point to modify the fisheye dart from. •	When in Edit mode, the Dimensions options (Horizontal and Vertical) and Show Center Options will be disabled

From the File menu select Close Model. The Close dialog box displays. 2.	Select the model name from the list and select OK.

pages.title: Copy Model
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy Model This function allows the user to copy a model and the pieces within the model. Copy Model can be used to quickly copy a model with a new style number.  The new style number is applied to both the model and the pieces during the function.  Additionally, the new style can be opened in Pattern Design or the Model Editor after the copy has been made. To Copy a Model: 1.	From the File menu, select Copy Model or press the CTRL + C keys on the keyboard. 2.	In the dialog box that appears, select the model name to copy.  Select Open. 3.	The Copy Model dialog box appears. 4.	Click Apply.  The piece names in the Destination Piece Name list should change. 5.	If desired, select from the following options: •	Edit New Model – opens the model editor screen after OK is selected to allow the user to change the information in the model such as fabric type or piece count. •	Open New Model – opens the copied model file into Pattern Design once OK is selected. •	Open Options – opens the pieces defined in Model Options into Pattern Design once OK is selected.  This option is only available if Open New Model is selected. 6.	When finished, select OK. 7.	The Save As dialog box will appear.  Type in the name of the new model and select the device and storage area to save it in.  When finished, select Save. NOTE:  When the Copy Model function is selected, the source model should not be open in Pattern Design.  If the source model is currently open, an error message will appear on the screen. •	Back – returns to the previous step, allowing the user to select another model •	Continue – closes the model that is currently open and continues with the Copy Model function. •	Save and Continue – saves the open model and then closes it so it can be copied. •	Cance

pages.title: Exit
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Exit Select Exit to close Pattern Design. Before exiting, be sure to save all desired pieces.

pages.title: Export
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Export Export allow you to create an AccuMark zipped file and select the component to include in the zipped package, such as Model Notes, Measure Charts, 3D components, or even the Grade Rule Table. Also, you may use this function to save data in a different file format, such as ASTM dxf, AAMA dxf,  Standard dxf, or IGS. Depending on the data type being exported, some file formats are restricted, for example a model is exported as ASTM /AAMA while pieces can also be exported as Standard dxf or IGS. The options dialog allow you to set how files are exported.

pages.title: Import
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Import Use this function to bring graphics (HPGL format) into the Pattern Design system.  These graphic files can be imported from non-AccuMark drawing packages and then moved, deleted, and copied as a group.  HPGL files import as internal lines within a rectangular piece. These graphics can then be added to pieces in Pattern Design.  For example, if a border was imported as an HPGL file, it could be added to a piece using Copy Line.

pages.title: Launch Yunique PLM
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Launch Yunique PLM Provides a dialog box to set up the connection information for Yunique PLM V7 and then open the application. Using the currently opened Model, the user will be presented with a list of PLM Styles that contain this model. The user selects the Style to use to display this model’s information and then the corresponding Style-model page will be displayed.

pages.title: Model Notes

links.label: To Create and Edit Model Notes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Model Notes Use this function to create, edit, or read existing notes on the current model. The default model notes path is defined on the Paths tab in the Preferences/Options. Each model notes doc is automatically named after the active model  in the work area and saved in the location defined in Preferences/Options. To Create and Edit Model Notes: 1.	From the File menu, select Model Notes.  The  Notes dialog box appears. 2.	Type in the desired information. 3.	From the File menu in the dialog box, select Save. 4.	Save the model as normal.

pages.title: New 3D Workspace

links.label: The 3D workspace hosts all the functionality to complete a 3D simulation. There are visual cues to identify and differentiate the 3D work ar

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search New 3D Workspace New 3D Workspace will appear in the File menu if your system has the 3D additional software module available. If it does not, please contact your local Gerber representative to find out more about this powerful visualization tool. The 3D workspace hosts all the functionality to complete a 3D simulation. There are visual cues to identify and differentiate the 3D work area. •	The icon in the 3D tabbed work area is an avatar. •	The work area color is darker. •	There are fewer tabs within the ribbon to focus only the functionality required for 3D simulation.

pages.title: New

links.label: To Open an Additional Work Area:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search New The New function will open a new, empty work area.  This is one way to work with multiple work areas open at one time. Each work area can have different models  opened. The model name is displayed in the Title Bar of the work area. To Open an Additional Work Area: 1.	From the File menu, select New or press the CTRL + N keys on the keyboard. A new work area displays. 2.	To switch to a different work area, click on Window. Work Areas are identified by the last piece, model or style opened. Use this list to switch between the multiple work areas. Click on the desired work area name.  The CTRL + TAB hotkey combination can also be used to switch to the next work area.  CTRL + SHIFT + TAB can be used to switch to the previous work area.

pages.title: Open
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Open Use this function to retrieve pieces, models, or digitized data from an AccuMark storage area. You can  open Measure Charts from this menu selection and even import AccuMark Zip files directly into PDS. A prompt will display when opening .zip files in Pattern Design to allow the user to select the destination storage area. Open will also convert non AccuMark data including MicroMark Styles, ASTM/AAMA, TIIP DXF, Standard DXF, IGEs, Assyst Design, Investronica Design, and Lectra Design files. To Open Data: 1.	From the File menu, choose Open or press the CTRL + O keys on the keyboard. 2.	In the Files of Type field, click on the down arrow to select the data type to open. 3.	In the Look In field, click on the down arrow to select the device and/or storage area where the pieces or models are stored. 4.	To shorten the list of data displayed type part of the style number in the File Name field.  For example, to find all pieces that start with 1954, type 1954* into the File Name field and press Enter or click Open.  The * serves as a wildcard, meaning the pieces must start with 1954, but can have any other characters after that number. 5.	Select the item(s), listed in the window.  Multiple files can be selected using the SHIFT or CTRL keys. 6.	Click on the Open button and the pieces will appear in the icon bar. The following options can also be used when opening pieces or models: •	Use Filename Filter Lookup – allows the user to view filtered file names only.  A wildcard filter must be typed into the file name box before any file names are displayed.  Once the filter is typed in, the Enter key or the Open button can be used to display the filtered list of file names. •	Open Separate Work Areas – select this option to open the retrieved file

pages.title: Open Work Session
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Open Work Session Work Sessions can be saved allowing the user to continue working on a project from the last stage it was left.  It is also possible to share work sessions from other users. Open Work Session will open PDS with the previously Saved Work Session. To Open a Work Session: 1.	From the File menu, select Open Work Session. 2.	The Open Work Session dialog box appears.  In the Look in field, select the location where the work session is stored.  In the File name field, select the work session and press Open.

pages.title: Piece from AccuScan
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Piece from AccuScan Piece from AccuScan: This function will open the AccuScan dialog and allow for additional images to be converted. This menu is visible only if AccuScan is installed. AccuScan is a program within the AccuMark Family Suite that allows images to be converted to AccuMark pieces.  This program can be used with  scanned images, camera images, or patterns.  The AccuScan program requires a separate purchase and installation from AccuMark.

pages.title: Plot Altered
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Plot Altered This function allows for plotting pieces that have alterations applied to them.  Alterations are special adjustments made to pieces based on point numbers. To Plot Altered Pieces: 1.	From the File menu, select Plot Altered. 2.	Select the piece or pieces to plot.  When finished, select OK. 3.	The Alteration Setup dialog box appears.  Select from the following options: •	Alteration Library – defines the Alteration table to be used.  Select from the drop-down list. •	Size Code – defines the Size Code table to be used.  If desired, select from the drop-down list.  This field does not have to be filled in. Type - •	Preference – controls how the altered piece should be plotted.  If Cumulative is selected, all requested alterations will plot and display blended on the piece.  If Nested is selected, each requested alteration will plot and display separately. •	Alteration Rule – determines which alteration rules should be used on the plotted piece.  A lookup is available. •	Amount – the measurement to be used in the alteration.  This value is typed in. 4.	When finished, select OK. 5.	The Plot Altered dialog appears.  Select the size or sizes to plot, then click OK.

pages.title: Plot

links.label: To Plot Using a Plot Form:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Plot Use this function to send pieces in the work area to the plotter.  Depending on what was chosen in Preferences/Options, the pieces will plot directly or the plot form will display. To Plot or Cut Directly: 1.	From the File menu, select Plot or press the CTRL + L keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Plot – the selected pieces will be drawn on the plotter paper. •	Cut – the selected pieces will be cut from the plotter paper. •	Number of Copies – set this to the number of times each piece should be plotted.  The maximum is 10 times. •	Media – use to change the Plotter Settings being used.  Select the desired file from the drop-down menu. •	New Page – if this button is selected, the plotter paper will advance before the pieces are plotted. •	Save As Image File – if checked, an image file will also be created from the pieces being sent to the plotter. 3.	Select the pieces to be plotted in the work area.  When finished, select OK. 4.	If Cut was selected, select the internals to be cut.  When finished, select OK. To Plot Using a Plot Form: 1.	From the File menu, select Plot.  The Plotter Window will display. 2.	From the View menu, select Bed Size.  Edit the Width and Length fields as needed. Select OK.  These fields are for visual display only.  The actual width and length of the plotter are defined in Plotter Settings. 3.	From the Edit menu, select Place Piece to plot or Place Cut to cut pieces.  Select the piece from the work area or the icon menu.  Left click in the Plot Form to place the piece. 4.	Select any of the following options to manipulate pieces in the Plotter Window form and control the plotter. •	Edit/Move Piece – used to move a pattern piece already placed in the form.  Once this option is

pages.title: Print Work Area
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Print Work Area Allows you to print the work area. Only parts that visible will print.

pages.title: Process Costing Marker
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Process Costing Marker This function will create a costing marker from the model in the current work area.  The size(s) requested must be one of the sizes available in the model’s size range. To Make a Costing Marker: 1.	From the File menu, select Process Costing Marker. 2.	In the dialog box that displays, fill in the following information: •	Size – type in the name of the size desired in the marker.  Use a comma to separate size names if multiple sizes are requested •	Quantity – type in the number of bundles to be included in the marker •	Width – type in the cutable width of the material •	Fabric – click the lookup or type in the  codes of the fabric from the model. Multiple fabric types can be selected. If more than one fabric code is entered, a separate marker will be created for each fabric code.  If no fabric code is typed in, all the pieces in the current model will be included in the marker. •	Easy Marking – if this box is checked, Easy Marking will automatically be launched •	AutoMark Edit – if this box is checked, AutoMark will be used to lay the pieces in the marker.  If this box is left unchecked, the user will lay the pieces in the marker. •	Fabric Cost – enter a cost for fabric if available. •	Fabric Weight – enter a fabric weight for costing if applicable. 3.	The Easy Marking window will be displayed.  If AutoMark was chosen, the pieces will already be placed in the marking area.  If AutoMark was not chosen, pieces can be placed by clicking on the piece at the top of the screen and then clicking and dragging it into the marking area.  For more information about Marker Making, see the Grading and Marking training guide. 4.	If the marker was manually nested or edited, go to the File menu and select Save.  The Easy Making windo

pages.title: Recent Files
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Recent Files A listing of previously opened pieces and models.

pages.title: Save As Image

links.label: To Save Pieces as Image Files:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Save As Image This function allows pieces to be output and saved as .BMP, .EMF, or .JPEG files. These images can be brought into other graphics programs for artwork or editing. To Save Pieces as Image Files: 1.	From the File menu, select Save as Image File or press the CTRL + Q keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select the pieces to create as an image file.  When finished, click OK. To Set the Image Type and Directory to Save the Image Files: 1.	From the Launch Pad, select AccuMark Explorer, Utilities then AccuMark Explorer. 2.	From the View menu, select Process Preferences then Plot Processing. 3.	In the Dialog Box that displays, the Default Image Directory is the folder the files should be saved in.  The Default Image Type can be set to BMP, EMF, or JPEG. 4.	When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Save As

links.label: To Save Pieces or Models with a Different Name:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Save As Used to save pieces or models with a new name or in a different location.  The original file is not changed. To Save Pieces or Models with a Different Name: 1.	From the File menu select Save As. 2.	Select from the following User Input Options: •	Save Models/Styles – to save an AccuMark Model •	Save Pieces [AM] – to save specific AccuMark pieces. 3.	Depending on what will be saved, the selection changes: •	If Save Models/Styles was chosen, select the desired model listed in the dialog box. Select OK. The Save As dialog box appears. From the Save in field, select the storage area where the model or style will be stored. In the File Name field, type in the new name. From the Save as Type field, select AccuMark Model.  Click the Save button. •	If Save Pieces was chosen, select the desired piece(s). The Save As dialog box appears.  From the Save in field, select the storage area where the pieces will be stored. In the File name field, type in the new name. Select the Options button to change the Category or Description. To save the relative position of the individual pieces in the work area, check the option Set Original Position. Click the Save button.

pages.title: Save As Work Session
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Save As Work Session Multiple Work Sessions can be saved allowing the user to continue working on a project from the last stage it was left.  It is also possible to share work sessions from other users

pages.title: Save
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Save Use to save a piece or model with the same name. To Save Pieces or Models: 1.	From the File menu, select Save or press the CTRL + S keys on the keyboard.  The dialog box displays. 2.	Select from the following User Input Options: •	Set Original Position – used to save the relative position of the individual pieces in the work area. •	Save Model – used to save an AccuMark model. •	Save Pieces – used to save specific AccuMark pieces. 3.	Depending on what will be saved, the selection changes: •	If Save Models was chosen, select the desired model listed in the dialog box and click OK. •	If Save Pieces was chosen, select the desired pieces.  When finished, select OK. NOTE: The Data Stored To field in the Preferences defines where the file should be stored when the Save function is used.  If this is set to Default Area, the file will be saved in the storage area defined in the Paths Tab of the Preferences.  If this is set to Retrieved Area, the file will be saved back to where it was opened from, regardless of which area is defined in the Preferences.

pages.title: Toggle Scanner Bitmap
pages.bodySummary:
Filter: All Files Submit Search Toggle Scanner Bitmap Toggle Scanner Bitmap: shows or hides the image behind the AccuMark piece.
Available only if AccuScan is installed. AccuScan is a program within the AccuMark Family Suite that allows images to be converted to AccuMark pieces.  This program can be used with  scanned images, camera images, or patterns.  The AccuScan program requires a separate purchase and installation from AccuMark.

pages.title: Delete Fullness
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Delete Fullness The Delete function can be used to remove a fullness object.  Before the object is deleted, you will be prompted for any internal lines to move as the fullness is being removed.  Select and internal lines and click OK to remove the fullness.

pages.title: Edit Fullness
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Fullness Once the fullness is closed, it can be edited.  To change the amount of fullness in the fullness object, select Edit function from the Fullness panel in the Advanced tab.  Select the closed fullness object to edit.  You will be prompted for the location to remain stationary while the fullness is being edited.  After selecting this location, you can choose any internal lines to move with the fullness.  When that selection is complete, you will be able to adjust the fullness to a new value.

pages.title: Open/Close Fullness
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Open/Close Fullness The following functions will be add fullness objects: 1-Point Fullness, Tapered Fullness, Variable Fullness, and Parallel Fullness. To edit an area of fullness after it has been created with one of the functions listed above, it will have to be closed.  To close a fullness object, choose the Open/Close function from the Fullness panel in the Advanced tab.  Select the fullness on the piece.  The fullness will be temporarily removed from the piece.  This function is also helpful to visualize the piece without fullness for commands like Walk Pieces.

Filter: All Files Submit Search 1:1 Displays the pieces in the work area so that one inch on the screen equals one inch in reality. Learn How to Zoom 1:1 1. To use this function, go to the View Tab and select  Zoom  1:1 from the Zoom Group. 2. The function is automatically performed.

pages.title: 1-Point Fullness

links.label: Learn How to Add or Subtract 1 Point Fullness:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search 1-Point Fullness Use to add or subtract an amount of fullness at a specific point along a line. Learn How to Add or Subtract 1 Point Fullness: 1.	From the Advanced Tab, select  1 Point Fullness from the Fullness Group. 2.	Select a perimeter point to add or subtract fullness by left clicking on it. 3.	Select a point to slash to by left clicking on it.  A line will be drawn between this point and the point for fullness to cut the piece for adding or subtracting fullness. 4.	Enter the fullness amount, either a positive or negative amount in inches or centimeters.

pages.title: Add Grade Point
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Add Grade Point Use to make an intermediate point or any location on piece perimeter or internal line into a grade point.  This allows for editing the grading values at that location.  To show that the rule does not correspond to the grade rule table, a pound sign (#) is automatically placed on the grade rule number. To Add a Grade Point: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Add Grade Point in the Modify panel or press the ALT + 1 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual – allows for the two corner end points to have different grading values applied.  This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Both if Same – applies grading to both corner end points if they had the same rule originally. This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Always Both – applies the grading to both corner endpoints. 3.	Select the point.  The graded nest displays to reflect the new grade rule.

pages.title: Align
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Align Use to line up a specific point with another point or line.  This function can be used to line up drills or notches, straighten a portion of a line, or help define a 90-degree angle. To Align 2 Points: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Align in the Point Actions panel or press ALT + F3 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Horizontal – use to line up 2 points along the X-axis. •	Vertical – use to line up 2 points along the Y-axis. •	Between 2 Points – use to align a point between two other points. •	Along Line – use to move a point onto an existing line. •	Show Thumbtacks – controls the display of the thumbtacks for defining a range.  Showing the thumbtacks will allow the user to define the range as a part of the function.  If this button is not selected, the range is automatically assigned based on the other options, Prev/Next Points or End Points. •	Prev/Next Points – places the thumbtacks at the point before and the point after the selected point by default. •	End Points – places the thumbtacks at the end points of the line by default. 3.	Select a point to move. 4.	If Show Thumbtacks was selected, reposition the thumbtacks to define the range or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks. 5.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Horizontal or Vertical was selected, select the point to line the first point up with (reference point). •	If Between 2 Points was selected, select 2 points.  The first point will be aligned with the imag

pages.title: View All Sizes

links.label: To View the Grade on All Sizes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View All Sizes Use this function  to display the graded nest of all sizes of a selected piece. These sizes correspond to sizes in the rule table for the piece. To View the Grade on All Sizes: 1.	From the Grade Tab, select View and then Show All Sizes or press the CTRL + G keys on the keyboard. 2.	Check the View Grade Rules option to display the grade rule numbers. 3.	Select piece(s).  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: View Altered Sizes

links.label: Learn How to View Altered Sizes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Altered Sizes Use to view the display of alterations assigned to the piece.  Alterations apply the movements necessary to create additional sizes from graded sizes. For example, alterations can create petite and tall versions of a regular size. Learn How to View Altered Sizes: 1.	From the Grade Tab, select Altered Sizes from View. 2.	Select piece(s).  When finished, select OK. 3.	A dialog box will display.  Select the Alteration Library.  Use the arrow on the right side of the box to select from a drop-down. 4.	Select the Size Code to be used, if desired. 5.	Select the display Preference by selecting Cumulative or Nested.  Cumulative will display all the alterations blended together as a single piece.  Nested will show each alteration separately in a different color. 6.	Depending on what was chosen, the selection changes: •	If a Size Code was specified, click OK. •	If no Size Code was specified, select the Alteration Rules to display and enter the amount of each alteration.  When finished, click OK. 7.	Select the size to view the alterations on.  Click OK

pages.title: Annotation
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Annotation Allows the user to type instructions and pattern notes directly on the pattern piece.  When the piece is plotted, this annotation will plot out as well.  In the marker, this annotation can be plotted or hidden depending on the setting chosen in the P-Marker-Plot table. Create Annotation can add the same annotation to multiple pieces in one step.  When prompted to select location for new annotation, hold the CTRL key down to select more than location for annotation.  This location can be selected on multiple pieces or on the same piece.  Each annotation can be independently edited or deleted NOTE: To make changes to existing annotation, select Annotation from the Edit Tab. To Add a New Annotation: 1.	From the Create tab, select Annotation in the Text panel. 2.	Select a location for the annotation. 3.	The Annotation dialog box will display. Type the desired text. 4.	If desired, change the character size, font rotation and grade rule to apply to this annotation.  If no rotation is applied, the annotation will place parallel to the grain line. 5.	When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Armhole/Sleeve Cap
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Armhole/Sleeve Cap Use to modify an armhole while updating the sleeve cap simultaneously.  Curves that span across multiple pieces for the armhole or the sleeve cap can be modified.  This function is divided into two sets of prompts.  The first set lets the user specify the groups of lines to be modified for the armhole and the second set lets the user specify the groups of lines to be modified for the sleeve cap. This function can also be applied to any group of pieces that should be modified as a group regardsless of the type of piece. To Modify an Armhole/Sleeve Cap: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select Armhole/Sleeve Cap in the Pattern Changes panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Create Composite Line – select if the curve to be modified spans multiple pieces. •	Armhole – to specify the type and direction of movement on the armhole. •	Sleeve Cap – to specify the type and direction of movement on the sleeve. •	% of Distance – specify the amount of the armhole movement that should be applied. •	Move Along Line – if the Move Smooth Line (+/-) option was selected for Armhole or Sleeve Cap, choose First Line to move only along an extension of the line before the chosen point.  Second Line can be used to move the point along the line after the chosen point. •	Show Thumbtacks – controls the display of the thumbtacks for defining a range.  Showing the thumbtacks will allow the user to define the range as a part of the function.  If this button is not selected, the range is automatically assigned based on the other options, Prev/Next Points or End Points. •	Prev/Next Points – places the thumbtacks at the point before and the point after the selected point by default. •	End Points – places the thumbtacks at the end points of th

pages.title: Assign Rule Table

links.label: Learn How to Assign a Rule Table:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Assign Rule Table Use to assign a new grade rule table to a piece. When a rule table is assigned: •	The piece becomes the same size as the base size in the rule table. •	The piece takes on the grading of the rule table. •	If the piece has grade rules that don’t exist in the rule table, no growth will be assigned to those points. Learn How to Assign a Rule Table: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Assign Rule Table in the Size Line panel or press the Ctrl + 3 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 3.	The Assign Rule Table dialog box displays.  Select the new library name. 4.	Select OK to accept or Cancel to close the dialog box without any changes.

pages.title: Attributes
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Attributes Use to display the point attributes on a piece. The attributes display on the screen next to the point. Learn to View Point Attributes: 1.	From the View tab, select Attributes in the Point panel or press Ctrl + B keys. 2.	Select the piece(s). Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 3.	To remove the point attributes from the work area, exit the function.

pages.title: Measure Between Notches

links.label: To Measure the Distance to a Notch for All Graded Sizes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Between Notches Use this function to measure the distance along the perimeter between a notch and the next notch along the line, or to measure the distance between a notch and the end of the line.  This function is the same function as in the Verify tab.  When performing the function from the Grade tab, it will generate measurements not only for the base size, but also for all the graded sizes. To Measure the Distance to a Notch for All Graded Sizes: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Between Notches in the Measure panel. 2.	Select the first segment to measure the distance. Select the following User Input option if: • Display X/Y Values – to include columns to display the X and Y differences between the selected points. X and Y guidelines are also displayed in the work area. 3.	Select another segment to measure, if desired.  This area will be added to the first area selected in the measurement chart. 4.	When finished, select OK for the graded measurement form to display. 5.	If desired, select another segment to measure.  This area will be compared to the first segments selected on the second chart. 6.	Select another segment to measure, if desired.  This area will be added to the first area selected in the measurement chart. 7.	When finished, select OK for the graded measurement form to display with comparison.

pages.title: Box Pleat
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Box Pleat Use to create a single or multiple box (or inverted) pleats. To Create a Box Pleat: 1.	Create an internal line where the pleating will begin.  This line will become the center of the first pleat.  Any of the functions from the Create/Line Actions tab can be used. 2.	From the Advanced tab, select Box in the Pleats panel. 3.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Both – adds notches at each end of the pleat. •	Single – adds notches to one selected end of the pleat. •	None – no notches will be added. •	Notching Folds – controls which folds will be notched for the pleat.  Check the desired locations to add notches. •	Notch Type – the notch number to place on the pleat. •	Notch Depth – view the notch depth defined in the P-Notch table.  This field is not editable. 4.	Select the internal pleat line. 5.	Enter half of the underlay. 6.	Enter the number of pleats. 7.	If more than one pleat is being created, enter the distance between the pleats.  Select the pleat open side.  This is the side where the additional pleats will be placed.

pages.title: View Break Sizes

links.label: Learn How to View the Grade on Size Breaks Only:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Break Sizes Use to display all size breaks and/or specific sizes. Learn How to View the Grade on Size Breaks Only: 1.	From the Grade Tab select View and then Show Regular/Break Sizes. 2.	Check the Select Sizes option to choose the sizes to display. 3.	Select piece(s). When finished, select OK. 4.	If Select Sizes was chosen, select the desired sizes from the dialog box.  Use the CTRL key to select more than one.  Click OK.  The break sizes will display along with the base size for reference. NOTE: Size Breaks are determined from the information typed into the grade rule editor.  If each and every size is typed into the Size Breaks section of the grade rule editor, then every size is considered a size break; and all sizes will display.

pages.title: View By Label

links.label: Learn How to Verify Line Labels:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View By Label Use to display all internals with the same label .  The internals will highlight. Learn How to Verify Line Labels: 1.	From the View tab, select By Label in the Lines panel or press the CTRL + W keys on the keyboard. 2.	Enter the desired label.  When finished, select OK. 3.	To remove the highlight from the requested label, exit the function.

pages.title: Calculator
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Calculator Use to show the Expression Calculator. To Show the Expression Calculator: 1.	From the View tab, select Calculator in the Utilities panel. 2.  The Expression Calculator will automatically open.

pages.title: Base Size

links.label: Learn How to Change the Base Size:
Learn How to Change the Base Dimensions:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Base Size Change Base Size This function will make a different size the base size for the selected pieces.  This function keeps the dimensions of the original sizes the same. Learn How to Change the Base Size: 1.	Place the graded base pattern piece in the working area. 2.	From the Grade tab, select the Base Size dropdown and then Change Base Size in the Size Line panel. 3.	Select the piece(s). Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 4.	The Change Base Size chart will display.  Select the new desired base size from the dialog box. Select OK. Change Base Dimensions Use to change the actual size/measurements of the base size pattern.  This function updates the dimensions of all sizes. Learn How to Change the Base Dimensions: 1.	Place the graded base pattern piece in the working area. 2.	From the Grade tab, select the Base Size dropdown and then Change Base Dimensions in the Size Line panel. 3.	Select the option Size Adjustment Amount (+/-)… 4.	Select the piece(s). Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 5.	The Change Base Dimensions chart will display.  Select the size to use as the shape of the base size from the dialog box.  Select OK.

pages.title: Clear
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Clear Use to remove the nested sizes from the display.  The function is automatically performed.  The CTRL + H keys on the keyboard can also be used to perform this command.

pages.title: Clipped
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Clipped Use to remove an existing line extension from a piece. The end of the perimeter line is moved to the perimeter intersection. To Trim Extended Lines: 1.	From the Edit tab, select Clipped in the Properties panel. 2.	The system displays the current status of the perimeter lines. 3.	Select the line(s) to be trimmed.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple lines. 4.	The system redisplays the current status of the perimeter lines.

From the Grade tab, select the Copy dropdown and then Copy Grade Rule in the Modify panel or press the ALT + 3 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select a reference point or piece. 3.	Depending on what was chosen, the selection changes. •	If a point was chosen, select a target point(s) to assign growth.  When finished, select OK. •	If piece was chosen, select the starting point on the reference piece. Select the starting point on the target piece.  If the number of grade rules on the reference piece does not match the number of grade rules on the target piece, the system will prompt for points to be de-selected on one piece.  When finished de-selecting, click OK. Copy Table Rule: Use to assign specific grade rule(s) from an existing Grade Rule Table to multiple points on multiple pieces with the same size line. Learn to Copy a Rule From a Rule Table: 1.	From the Grade tab, select the Copy dropdown and then Copy Table Rule in the Modify panel or press the ALT + 2 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select the point(s) to grade.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple points. 3.	Enter the new grade rule number in the User Input box. Select OK. Copy X Rule: Use to copy only the X grading values assigned from one point to another. Learn to Copy the X Value of a Grade Rule: 1.	From the Grade tab, select the Copy dropdown and then Copy X Rule in the Modify panel. 2.	Select a reference point. 3.	Select a target point(s) to assign growth in the X. When finished, select OK. Copy Y Rule: Use to copy only the Y grading values assigned from one point to another. Learn to Copy the Y Value of a Grade Rule: 1.	From the Grade tab, select the Copy dropdown

pages.title: Copy Size Line

links.label: Learn How to Copy a Size Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy Size Line Use to copy a size line from one piece to another. Learn How to Copy a Size Line: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Copy in the Size Line panel. 2.	Select the reference piece from which to copy the size line. 3.	Select the target piece(s) to receive the size line.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces.

pages.title: Copy to Clipboard
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy to Clipboard Copy to Clipboard - Copy  pieces in the work area to the Windows Clipboard, then they can be pasted into other applications such as Microsoft Word to create production documentation.

pages.title: Copy to Clipboard 1:1
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy to Clipboard 1:1 Copy to Clipboard 1:1 - Copy pieces in the work area to the Windows Clipboard in full life scale, then they can be pasted into other applications.

pages.title: Copy Piece

links.label: To Copy a Piece Without Seam & Corner Information:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy Piece Use to make a copy of a piece without carrying over the seam allowance or corner information from the original.  The copied piece can be edited without the restrictions of system generated corner shapes.  For example, the sew lines can be deleted or a point of a corner can be moved. The sew lines are carried over, but cannot be updated.  The seam lines will become internal lines. To Copy a Piece Without Seam & Corner Information: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select Copy Piece in the Seam panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Copy Original – copies the category of the original piece. •	Piece Name – uses the new piece name as the category. 3.	Select piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 4.	Enter a new piece name.

pages.title: Corners

To Add a Bisect Step Corner:
To Add a Slanted Step Corner:
