pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Corners Remove:Use to remove a special corner, including notches. To Remove a Special Corner: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select the Corners dropdown and then Remove in the Seam panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Point – to remove special corner types on specified point(s). •	Piece – to remove all special corner types on a piece. 3.	Select a corner or a piece.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple corners or pieces. Regular:Use to add notches to seam allowance lines.  The notches added using Regular Corner can be deleted using Remove Corner.  Since the notches are considered part of the seam allowance, Delete Point or Delete Notch will not remove these notches. To create a Regular Corner: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select the Corners dropdown and then Regular in the Seam panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	None – no notches will be added. •	Perpendicular – notches will be added to the cut line at a 90o angle to the corner. •	Extension – notches will be added to the cut line where the sew line intersects. •	Point – applies the corner to selected point(s). •	Piece – applies the corner to the entire piece. •	Notch Type – the notch number to place on the corner.  This field only becomes active if Perpendicular or Extension is selected. •	Notch Depth – view the notch depth defined in the P-Notch table.  This field is not editable. •	Both – to place notches on both lines of a corner. •	First Only – to place notches only on the line before the corner. •	Second Only – to place notches only on the line after the corner. 3.	Select a point or piece. Slant:Use to clip off excess seam allowance.  The seam allowance will be clipped off where the sew lines would intersect the cut lines if they were drawn out. To

pages.title: Create Delta

links.label: To Create a Delta Grade Rule:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Create Delta Use to apply X and Y grading values to a point where no grading exists.  To show that the rule does not correspond to the grade rule table, a pound sign (#) is automatically placed on the grade rule number.  Assign a grade rule table before using this function. To Create a Delta Grade Rule: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Create Delta or press the ALT + K keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual – allows for the two corner end points to have different grading values applied.  If a grade rule is copied with the “individual” option selected, the rule is only copied to one end of one of the lines of the corner.  This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Both if Same – applies grading to both corner end points if they had the same rule originally. This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Always Both – applies the grading to both corner endpoints. 3.	Select a point to create grading on. The Create Grade Point dialog box displays. 4.	Enter the desired values in the X and Y columns. 5.	Select from the following Create Grade Point dialog box options: •	Update – applies the change(s) and redisplays the piece in the work area. •	Grade Line – controls which grain line the grading values will reference.  G0 is the primary grain line. •	OK – accepts the values and closes the Create Grade Point form. •	Cancel ¬– closes the Create Grade Point form without changing the grading.

pages.title: Create Place Image
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Create Place Image The Place Image function is used to add fabric textures (fills), images to pieces and/or Seam Finish images to perimeter lines. After the function is selected the system displays 3 radio button options in the User Input box. The options are Fabric, Trim and Edge Finish. Fabric is used to add a texture fill to a piece and Trim is used to add an image to a piece. Edge Finish is used to add a top stitch design to an edge of a finish part of a product (only piece perimeter lines are a valid selection) When Fabric is selected the system prompts, “Select piece for new texture.”  After a piece is selected an Open dialog box displays.  Select the desired texture file.  Various file formats are supported including .png, .jpg, .tif, and .bmp. Note: A model needs to be opened to use the Fabric functions.  Make sure a Fabric Type is defined in the model. After the texture is selected and Open is selected to close the Open dialog, a dialog box displays with image properties.  In this dialog, various properties can be specified including the image height, width, thickness, DPI (dots per inch or resolution), and Symmetry and Rotation settings.  Symmetry is only used with Trim not Fabric.  The height, width and DPI are read from the image file. Height and width units are shown in current notation system. The Fabric Type of the selected piece is also displayed at the top of the dialog box.  When OK is selected the fabric is assigned to all pieces in the model with the same fabric type. After the properties are specified and OK is selected, the piece(s) display with the selected texture. When Image is selected the system prompts, “Select location for new trim image.”  After a location is selected an Open dialog box displays.  Select the

pages.title: Create Nest

links.label: Learn How to Create a Nest:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Create Nest Use to create a nest from pieces that were digitized or imported into the computer separately.  The pieces were digitized in separately because the grading or shape was not consistent from one size to the next. Learn How to Create a Nest: 1.	Place the pieces to be nested in the work area. 2.	From the Grade tab, select Create Nest in the Size Line panel. 3.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Add Piece to Model– use to add the piece to the active model. •	Use Base Size Line – uses the size line of the piece that will be the base size. •	Create New Size Line – use to create a new size line. •	Select Points – use to select a specific point on each size to stack the pieces on and build the nest. •	Use Piece Center – use to build the nest by using the center of each piece. 4.	Select the piece that will become the base size. 5.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Create New Size Line was selected, the dialog box appears.  Enter the base size, size step, smallest size, and all size breaks.  Select OK.  Then select a piece for each break size. •	If Select Points was selected, select a point on each break size to stack the pieces from. 6.	If desired, select additional grade points on the base size.  Select OK.  The new nested piece will appear. 7.	Type a new piece name.  Select OK.

pages.title: Create Offset
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Create Offset Use to create grading on a line where no grading exists.  Instead of grading points in an X and Y direction, offset grading is used to grade the line and have it remain parallel to the original.  To show that the rule does not correspond to the grade rule table, a pound sign (#) is automatically placed on the grade rule number. To Create Offset Grading: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Create Offset. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual – allows for the two corner end points to have different grading values applied.  If a grade rule is copied with the “individual” option selected, the rule is only copied to one end of one of the lines of the corner.  This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Prev/Next – allows for both offsets to be input at the same time. •	Always Both – applies the same grading to both corner endpoints. 3.	Select the piece to edit. 4.	Select an existing grade point, intermediate point, or location to grade on the piece.  This selection can be made on any size except for the base size.  The Edit Grade Point dialog box displays on-screen with the grading information for the current point on all sizes in the nest.  In the work area, a line connecting the same point on all sizes displays. This line visually represents the X and Y values in the form. 5.	Enter a value in the Offset dist field or select from the following Edit Grade point dialog box options.  If Prev/Next was selected from the User Input options, two columns will be available for editing – previous and next: •	Update – applies the changes to the piece on the work area. •	OK – accepts the values and closes the Edit Grade Point form. •	Cancel ¬– closes the Edit Grade Point f

pages.title: Create Piece

links.label: Learn How to Make a Draft Piece into a Valid Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Create Piece Use this function to convert a draft piece into a valid pattern piece. If the perimeter lines do not intersect, the lines may need to be lengthened using Trim/Extend Line.  Create Piece will not leave the draft piece on the screen. Learn How to Make a Draft Piece into a Valid Piece: 1.	From the Draft tab, select Create Piece from the Create Group. 2.	Select the piece. 3.	Select the grain line(s) for the piece. The first line selected is the primary grain line.  When finished, select OK.  If a grain line does not exist, select OK and the program will automatically create one. 4.	Select desired internal lines or points.  When finished, select OK. 5.	Enter the piece name.

pages.title: Dart Fold

links.label: Learn How to Fold a Dart:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Dart Fold Use to temporarily fold a dart(s). For example, to fold a dart to determine if the sew line will finish smooth or to create a facing without a dart. Learn How to Fold a Dart: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Dart in the Folding panel. 2.	Select the dart to fold.  The selected dart leg will move to close the dart.

pages.title: Define Bookmark

links.label: Learn how to Define a Bookmark

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Define Bookmark The Defined Bookmark is user definable at any time the pattern is being modified.  Only 1 Defined Bookmark exists for each piece. Learn how to Define a Bookmark 1. Click the Create Tab. 2. From the Bookmark Group, select Define. 3. Select the piece(s) to bookmark. 4. Click OK to complete the function.

pages.title: Defined
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Defined Use to display a user-defined bookmark.  Any previously set Bookmark will be overwritten; the original Bookmark cannot be changed by a user.

pages.title: Define Seam

links.label: To Add or Remove Seam Allowance:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Define Seam Use to add or remove seam allowances to one or more pieces, line-by-line or piece-by-piece.  Use a positive value to add cut lines or a negative value to add sew lines.  Use a value of zero to remove seam allowance. To Add or Remove Seam Allowance: 1.	Advanced Tab, select Define from the Seam group  press the SHIFT + F7 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Manual-Even creates seam lines parallel to the existing line. •Manual-	Uneven defines seam line point-by-point for a tapered seam line. Edit Seam Properties 3.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Even was selected, select the lines that will receive the same amount of seam allowance.  When finished, select OK. Enter the amount of seam allowance in the User Input box. •	If Uneven was selected, select the point(s) that will receive the same amount of seam allowance.  When finished, select OK.  Enter the seam allowance amount in the User Input box.  Continue selecting points until the seam is defined for the whole line or piece. NOTE: Uneven seam can only be applied to a piece on its Digitized Boundary.  Use Piece Properties to view this information.  When a piece with uneven seam is swapped, not all functions will be available for modifying the piece.

pages.title: Delete Pleat
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Delete Pleat Allows a pleat object created in version 10 software to be removed from a piece. This function applies only to pleats created in AccuMark version 10 software, not prior versions.

pages.title: Distribute

links.label: Learn How to Distribute Grading Proportionally between Sizes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Distribute Use this function in the Grade menu to automatically distribute grading proportionally between the smallest and base sizes, and the largest and base sizes.  Perform this function with the graded nest displayed to see the change.  On some pieces, the change that takes place is very subtle.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Distribute Grading Proportionally between Sizes: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Distribute Proportional. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	All Sizes – adjusts the grading of all sizes in the size line for the selected point. •	Base to Selected Size – adjusts only the sizes between the base size and the selected size. 3.	Select points to distribute proportionally.  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Draft Scale

links.label: Learn How to Scale the Screen to Table:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Draft Scale Use this function to automatically change the scale of the screen to equal the area of the table surface. Use this function prior to using Sketch or Line/Curve. Learn How to Scale the Screen to Table: 1.	From the Draft tab, select Draft Scale in the Work Area panel.  This function is performed automatically. Reorient: This function can be used to move a piece on the screen to the same relative position as the piece on the table.  A piece needs to be reoriented if it has been moved on the table or the screen and or if lines are being added using Sketch, Line/Curve, or Note/Illustrate.

pages.title: Draft Trace

links.label: Learn How to Make a Draft Piece into a Valid Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Draft Trace Use this function to create a valid piece after using functions Line/Curve and Sketch.  The user chooses which lines they want as perimeter or boundary lines, as well as internal lines.  The lines that are not selected will not be included in the validated piece.  Once the valid piece is created, the draft piece remains on the screen. Learn How to Make a Draft Piece into a Valid Piece: 1.	From the Draft tab, select Draft Trace from the Create Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Add Piece to Model/Style – use to add the piece to the current model. •	Normal – to create a closed piece. •	Use Perimeter – applies grade rules from the original perimeter lines to new piece. •	Use Internal – will use the grade rules on the internal lines used in tracing. •	Maintain Graded Nest – will establish grading on the traced piece like the nest of the original piece. 3.	Select perimeter lines to trace, working in a clockwise direction around the piece.  When finished, select OK. 4.	Select the grain line(s) for the piece. The first line selected is the primary grain line.  When finished, select OK.  If a grain line does not exist, select OK and the program will automatically create one. 5.	Select desired internal lines or points.  When finished, select OK. 6.	Enter the piece name.

pages.title: Edit Delta

links.label: Learn How to Edit a Delta Grade Rule:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Delta Adjust the X and/or Y values of an existing grade rule. Edit Delta offers many tools to assist in calculating grade rules.  Values can be selected from the chart for calculation.  Right clicking on the selected area will show the options.  A Constant field is available in the dialog box to enter a value to use in the calculation. Learn How to Edit a Delta Grade Rule: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Edit Delta or press ALT + J keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual – allows for the two corner end points to have different grading values applied.  If a grade rule is copied with the “individual” option selected, the rule is only copied to one end of one of the lines of the corner.  This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Both if Same – applies grading to both corner end points if they had the same rule originally. This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Always Both – applies the grading to both corner endpoints. •	Maintain Growths – controls how the sizes larger than the size being edited are modified.  When this option is checked, the grading amount for the larger sizes does not change.  Sizes smaller than the size being edited will not be affected. 3.	Select the piece to edit. 4.	Select an existing grade point, intermediate point, or location to grade on the piece.  This selection can be made on any size except for the base size.  The Edit Grade Point dialog box displays on-screen with the grading information for the current point on all sizes in the nest.  In the work area, a line connecting the same point on all sizes displays. This line visually represents the X and Y values in the form. 5.	There are two

pages.title: Edit Image
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Image The Edit Image Properties dialog displays the same dialog box displayed in the Create Image function.  After the various properties are edited and OK is selected, the pieces in the workarea are updated with the new values. This function allows you to edit Fabric and Trim as the same option and Edge as a separate option. To edit Edge/Seam Finish images, select Place Image again to re-assign another image or to modify values of existing one.

pages.title: Edit Line Names

links.label: To Assign a Name to a Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Line Names Use this function to assign names to lines. These names can consist of letters, numbers, or labels. Line names are used in procedures, such as Pattern Wizard scripts, to identify certain lines on a piece. To Assign a Name to a Line: 1.	From the Edit Tab, select  Edit Line Names from the Information Panel.  The line names will appear. 2.	Select the line to name. 3.	Enter the line name in the User Input box.

pages.title: Edit Offset

links.label: Learn How to Edit Offset a Grade Rule:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Offset Use to change the existing grading applied to a line.  Instead of grading points in X or Y directions, offset grading is used to grade the line and have it remain parallel to the original. Learn How to Edit Offset a Grade Rule: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Edit Offset. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual  – allows for the two corner end points to have different grading values applied.  If a grade rule is copied with the “individual” option selected, the rule is only copied to one end of one of the lines of the corner.  This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Prev/Next – only available with Create Offset. •	Always Both – applies the same grading to both corner endpoints. •	Maintain Growths – controls how the sizes larger than the size being edited are modified.  When this option is checked, the grading amount for the larger sizes does not change.  Sizes smaller than the size being edited will not be affected. 3.	Select the piece to edit. 4.	Select an existing grade point, intermediate point, or location to grade on the piece.  This selection can be made on any size except for the base size.  The Edit Grade Point dialog box displays on-screen with the grading information for the current point on all sizes in the nest.  In the work area, a line connecting the same point on all sizes displays. This line visually represents the X and Y values in the form. 5.	Enter a value in the Offset dist field or select from the following Edit Grade point dialog box options: •	Clear Offset – removes all the values from the Offset column. •	Copy Previous – makes the current offset amounts the same as the previous offset. •	Copy Next – makes the current offset amount

pages.title: Edit Pleat
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Pleat Allows changes to be made to values entered when creating a pleat object. Pleat objects are only created in version 10 software, this function does not apply to pleats created on earlier versions of software. To edit a pleat object, it must be in the closed state. Use Open/Close to close the pleat object for editing.

pages.title: Export Rules
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Export Rules Use to send grade rule(s) to: •	An existing rule table – the size range for this rule table must be the same as the piece. •	A new rule table – the system creates a rule table with the same size range as the piece. Learn to Export Rules: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Export Rules in the Modify panel. The Export Rules dialog box displays. 2.	Enter the name of the storage area in the path field. 3.	Enter the name of the rule table to create a new one or select a rule table name from the list. Select OK when finished. 4.	Select the point or piece to export rules from.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple points or pieces.

pages.title: View F Rotation

links.label: To Show a Piece in F-Rotation:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View F Rotation Use to display a piece as it will rotate for marker making.  The piece must have an F-Line to use this command.  F-Rotation is an abbreviation for Facing Rotation.  When two F attributes are assigned to a line on a piece, the piece is able to be graded in one orientation and placed in the marker in another.  The attributes can be placed along the perimeter edge or on an internal line. To Create an F-Line: 1.	Draw an internal line or identify the perimeter line to apply the F attributes.  If a new line is being created, any of the Create / Line Panel functions can be used. 2.	From the Edit tab, select Point in the Information panel. 3.	Select two points.  If an internal line is being used, select the end points.  Enter “F” in the Attributes box.  Click OK. To Show a Piece in F-Rotation: 1.	From the Grade tab, select F Rotation in the View Panel or press the CTRL + F keys. 2.	Select the piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple. 3.	To return the piece to its original orientation, select OK.

pages.title: Fan Fullness

links.label: Learn How to Fan a Pattern Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fan Fullness Use to slash and spread a pattern piece its curve matches another piece.  The modified piece is matched to the target piece in a clockwise direction.  The slash lines created during the function can be removed, drawn as internal lines, or converted to darts. Learn How to Fan a Pattern Piece: 1.	Arrange pieces to be fanned on the screen. 2.	From the Advanced Tab, select Fan from the Fullness Group. 3.	Select from the following User Input options for Drawing Slash Lines: •	None – slash lines are removed from the final piece. •	Keep as Internals – areas of fullness are indicated on the final piece with internal lines. •	Keep as Darts – areas of fullness become darts on the final piece. 4.	Select the match point on the target piece.  This will be the point where the two pieces will line up to add fullness.  The target piece will not be modified during the function. 5.	Select line to receive pivot end of slash lines.  This line will not change in length but will pivot to match the curve of the target piece. 6.	If desired, position the thumbtacks to define a range of the line to receive slash lines.  When finished or if the thumbtacks should remain where they are placed, left click to continue. 7.	Choose a cut method from the following: •	Manually – allows the user to draw the slash lines for each cut. •	Evenly (Perpendicular) – creates the slash lines perpendicular (90 degrees) to the target piece. •	Evenly (Proportional) – creates slash lines equally spaced along the pivot line and open line. 8.	Depending on the cut method chosen, the selection changes: •	If Manually was selected, draw each of the cut lines necessary on the piece from the pivot end to the open end.  Right mouse button options are available.  When finished, select

pages.title: Measure Finished

links.label: Learn to Measure the Finished Distance:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Finished Use to measure the straight distance between two selected points from sew line to sew line for all graded sizes. Learn to Measure the Finished Distance: 1. From the Grade Tab, select Finished in the Measure panel 2. Select two points on a piece to measure the straight distance between sew lines 3. Select the following User Input option if: • Display X/Y Values – to include columns to display the X and Y differences between the selected points. X and Y guidelines are also displayed in the work area. 4. Select OK to measure another area 5. Select OK again to display the measure chart: it displays the straight length value per size, X Distance and the X Difference between sizes. Same values for Y. the Total will display the total sum of all pairs of point distance(s) if more than one set was selected. Size Difference shows the difference between totals in all sizes. 6. Print – click on this button to output the chart directly to the printer of your choice 7. Copy – click on this button to copy the chart information and paste in the program of your choice. This information is output as csv format so if pasted in a spreadsheet in MS-Excel each column and value will be populated in separate fields. 8. Click the X button to close the dialog and continue working in the function 9. When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Fix
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fix Use this command to indicate whether the sew or the cut lines are the original piece perimeter/boundary.  This function also removes the seam extensions from sew lines and forces the intersection of the seam internals so that no extensions or gaps exist. To Fix the Boundary Type: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select Fix in the Seam panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Sew Boundary – the current perimeter (solid) line will be labeled a sew line. •	Cut Boundary – the current perimeter (solid) line will be labeled a cut line. 3.	Select piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces.

pages.title: Flip Grade

links.label: Learn to Change the Sign of the X Rule:
Learn to Change the Sign of the Y Rule:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Flip Grade Flip X Rule: Use to change the sign of the X value from positive to negative or vice versa.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is modified. Learn to Change the Sign of the X Rule: 1.	From the Grade tab, select the Flip dropdown and then Flip X Rule in the Modify panel. 2.	Select a grade point to flip. Flip Y Rule: Use to change the sign of the Y value from positive to negative or vice versa.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is modified. Learn to Change the Sign of the Y Rule: 1.	From the Grade tab, select the Flip dropdown and then Flip Y Rule in the Modify panel. 2.	Select a grade point to flip.

pages.title: Full Scale

links.label: Learn How to Make the Work Area Full Scale

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Full Scale Adjusts the size of the work area so that all pieces in the work area are visible. Learn How to Make the Work Area Full Scale 1. To use Full Scale, go to View / Zoom / Full Scale or press the F3 key on the keyboard. 2. The function is automatically performed.

pages.title: Generate Seam
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Generate Seam Converts internal lines labeled "S" to Seam allowance.

pages.title: Grade Rules

links.label: Learn to View Grade Rule Numbers:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Grade Rules Use to display the grade rule numbers on a piece. Grade rules display on the screen next to the point. Learn to View Grade Rule Numbers: 1.	From the View tab, select Grade Rules in the Point panel or press the Ctrl + J keys on the keyboard. 2.	The grade rule numbers immediately display on all pieces in the work area. 3.	To remove the grade rule numbers from the work area, select the function again

pages.title: Grade Options

links.label: Learn How to Set Grade Options:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Grade Options Learn How to Set Grade Options: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Grade Options in the Size Line panel.  Select the desired grading method from the drop-down menu and click OK: •	Small-Large Incremental – pieces will grade from the smallest size to largest size.  The value typed into the rule table will be the amount of grade between sizes. •	Base Up-Down Incremental – pieces will grade from the base size up to the next size break and from the base size down to the next size break.  The value typed into the rule table will be the amount of grade between sizes. •	Base Up-Down Cumulative – pieces will grade from the base size to each size break.  The value typed into the rule table will be the amount of grade from the base size.

pages.title: Group
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Group Use to create a reference notch group from existing notches.  The reference distance will be measured from the notch closest to the reference point. To Group Multiple Notches: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Group in the Notch Actions panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Type – controls the kind of notch being grouped.  All selected notches will become this type.  Select from the drop-down menu. •	Depth – displays the notch type from the P-Notch table.  This field is not editable. •	Distance Between – controls the measurement between the notches.  If left blank, the notches will be spaced evenly between the first and last notch in the group. •	Perpendicular – the notch will be placed on the seam allowance by extending a perpendicular (90-degree angle) line from the notched line. •	Notch Angle – notches will be placed on the seam allowance by extending the angle created by the original notch. •	Same Distance on Seam – notches will be placed on the seam allowance using the same measurement as the reference distance. 3.	Select notches to be grouped.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple notches. 4.	Select the reference point.

pages.title: Hide

links.label: Learn How to Hide Perimeter Lines:
Learn How to Hide Internal Lines:
Learn How to Reset Perimeter or Internal Lines:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Hide Perimeter: Use to hide perimeter lines. All but one line can be hidden. Learn How to Hide Perimeter Lines: 1.	From the View tab, select the Hide drop down and then Perimeter in the Lines panel. 2.	Select the perimeter line(s) to hide.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple lines. Internal: Use to hide internal lines.  All internals may be hidden. Learn How to Hide Internal Lines: 1.	From the View tab, select the Hide drop down and then Internal in the Lines panel. 2.	Select the internal line(s) to hide.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple lines. Reset: Use to redisplay all hidden lines. Learn How to Reset Perimeter or Internal Lines: 1.	From the View tab, select the Hide drop down and then Reset in the Lines panel. 2.	Select the piece.

pages.title: Horizontal Tab Group

links.label: To Create a New Horizontal Tab Group

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Horizontal Tab Group New Horizontal Tab Group: Use this function to show two work areas side-by-side by dividing the screen horizontally.  This option allows for comparison among pieces. To Create a New Horizontal Tab Group 1.	Open at least two work areas in Pattern Design using File / Open or View / New Window. 2.	From the View tab, select the Windows dropdown and then New Horizontal Tab Group in the Window panel. 3.	The screen will automatically split horizontally in two even sections.  Each window size can be adjusted manually as needed by left clicking and holding as the cursor shape changes to   around the gray work area border.

pages.title: Edit Annotation Information
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Annotation Information Annotation allows existing piece annotation to be changed.

pages.title: Copy Line Names
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy Line Names Use this function to copy the names of lines from one piece to another.  Internal lines should be copied individually. To Copy Lines Names: 1.	From the Edit Tab, select Copy Line Names.  The line names will appear. 2.	Select the start line on the source piece. 3.	Select the start line on the target piece

pages.title: Copy Point Numbers

links.label: Learn How to Copy Point Numbers:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy Point Numbers Use to copy special point numbers from one piece to another.  All point numbers must be unique on each piece. Special point numbers are used when applying alterations, Pattern Wizard scripts, and rule matching. Learn How to Copy Point Numbers: 1.	From the Edit tab, select Copy Point Number. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual Points – copies point numbers one point at a time. •	All Perimeter Points – copies all point numbers from one piece to another. •	Grade Rule Numbers – makes the point number the same as the grade rule number. 3.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Individual Points was selected, select the point to copy the number from (source point).  Then, select the point to copy the number to (target point). •	If All Perimeter Points was selected, select the starting point on the piece to copy the numbers from (source piece).  Next, select the starting point on the piece to copy the numbers to (target piece).  If the number of end points, intermediate points, and grade points are the same on both pieces, the point numbers will be copied.  If the number of points is not equal, click on the points to ignore to deselect them.  When finished, select OK. •	If Grade Rule Numbers was selected, select the piece(s) to copy.  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Edit Line Information
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Line Information Line opens the Tracking Information dialog box. While tracking on a piece, the internal line labels will display in the dialog box.

pages.title: Edit Notch Information
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Notch Information Notch opens the Tracking Information dialog box.

pages.title: Edit Piece Information
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Piece Information Piece opens the Tracking Information dialog box.

pages.title: Edit Point Information
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Edit Point Information Point opens the Tracking Information dialog box.

pages.title: Intermediate Point
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Intermediate Point Use to display the intermediate and smoothing points on a piece. Intermediate points are indicated by a ■ symbol. Learn to View Intermediate Points: 1.	From the View tab, select Intermediate in the Point panel or press CTRL + I keys. 2.	Select the piece(s). Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 3.	To hide the points again, perform the function again.

pages.title: Knife Pleat
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Knife Pleat Use to create single or multiple knife pleats. To Create a Knife Pleat: 1.	Create an internal line where the pleating will begin.  This line will become the leading edge of the first pleat.  Any of the functions from the Create/Line Actions panel can be used. 2.	From the Advanced tab, select Knife in the Pleats panel. 3.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Both – adds notches at each end of the pleat. •	Single – adds notches to one selected end of the pleat. •	None – no notches will be added. •	Notching Folds – controls which folds will be notched for the pleat.  Check the desired locations to add notches. •	Notch Type – the notch number to place on the pleat. •	Notch Depth – view the notch depth defined in the P-Notch table.  This field is not editable. 4.	Select the internal pleat line. 5.	Enter half of the underlay. 6.	Enter the number of pleats. 7.	If more than one pleat is being created, enter the distance between the pleats.  Select the pleat open side.  This is the side where the additional pleats will be placed. 8.	Left click on the pleat lay side.  This is the side the pleat will fold toward when it is sewn.

pages.title: View Labels

links.label: Learn How to  Display Line Types and

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Labels Learn How to  Display Line Types and Labels : 1.	From the View tab, select Labels in the Lines panel or press the CTRL + U keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select the piece(s) or line(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces or lines. 3.	To remove the line types and labels from the display, exit the function.

pages.title: Line/Curve

links.label: Learn How to Input a New Piece Using Line/Curve:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Line/Curve The Line/Curve function is similar to digitizing.  Pieces are input point by point, using either line (straight) points or curve points.  When using Line/Curve to enter a piece that contains sharp corners, the system will generate end points on these corners.  Pieces can be input from a paper pattern, a garment or a draped piece of fabric. Learn How to Input a New Piece Using Line/Curve: 1.	From the Draft Tab, select Draft Scale. 2.	From the Draft Tab, select Line/Curve. 3.	Click the button on the stylus pen and check the option Create Draft Piece. 4.	Press the stylus down along the perimeter line of the pattern to create a point.  Working clockwise, select additional points of the pattern.  To switch to curve mode, press the button on the side of the stylus pen and select OK.  To switch back to line mode, press the button on the side of the stylus pen and select OK. 5.	Finish selecting points at the starting point.  Click the button and select OK twice.  To complete the piece and exit the function, click the button and select Cancel. 6.	Use the Draft Trace or Create Piece functions to make the draft piece into a valid piece. NOTE: To erase a point, click the button on the stylus pen and select Erase.

pages.title: Line

links.label: Learn How to Fold Along a Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Line Use to fold a piece along a two point internal line. Learn How to Fold Along a Line: 1.	Create a line in the desired folding location if a line does not already exist. 2.	From the Verify tab, select Line in the Folding panel. 3.	Select line to fold along. 4.	Select a location on the perimeter in the part of the piece to fold.  The section containing this line will move to fold the piece.

pages.title: Line to Line

links.label: Learn How to Fold Between Two Lines:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Line to Line Use to fold a piece between two selected lines. Learn How to Fold Between Two Lines: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Line to Line in the Folding panel. 2.	Select the first line. 3.	Select a line to match to. 4.	Select a location on the perimeter in the part of the piece to fold.  The section containing this line will move to fold the piece.

pages.title: Measure Line Length

links.label: Learn to Measure the length of a line in all sizes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Line Length Use to measure selected line(s) for all graded sizes from end point to end point. This function is the same function as in the Verify tab. When performing the function from the Grade tab, it will generate measurements not only for the base size, but also for all the graded sizes. Measure information is output in both the work area as well as in a dialog box. The information in the dialog box can print out or copy/paste into another document such as a spreadsheet in MS-Excel Learn to Measure the length of a line in all sizes: 1. From the Grade Tab, select Line Length in the Measure panel 2. Select a line or lines to measure. When finished, select OK. 3. The Grade Measure Line displays. The chart shows the line length per size. If multiple lines are selected each line will be assigned a number and each line length will display in separate columns. The Total column shows the total length of the line(s) selected. The Size Difference 1 shows the difference between size lengths. 4. To compare against another set of line(s), stay in the function and select the other line(s). A second dialog displays with the line length information plus two more columns: Difference between Totals and Overall Size Difference to compare lengths from chart 1 versus chart 2 5. Print – click on this button to output the chart directly to the printer of your choice 6. Copy – click on this button to copy the chart information and paste in the program of your choice. This information is output as csv format so if pasted in a spreadsheet in MS-Excel each column and value will be populated in separate fields. 7. Click the X button to close the dialog and continue working in the function 8. When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Mark Point
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Mark Point Use to create mark points, which are visible reference points. To Mark a Location: 1.	From the Point group, select Mark  Point. 2.	Select the N Attribute option if the point being added should be a non-smoothing point. 3.	Select the point location using one of the following methods: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to add the point. •	Value Mode – left click and drag the cursor to the point to measure from, click the right button and release both buttons.  Enter a distance in the Beg or End fields to add a point on a line or the X and Y fields to add a point in space. •	Right Mouse Button group – right click in the work area and select the desired option.  Read and follow the prompts for the steps to perform the function. NOTE: To convert a Mark Point to an intermediate point, use Edit / Edit Point Info.  Select the point and uncheck the box labeled Mark.  Click Apply.  When finished, click OK.

pages.title: Match Points

links.label: Learn How to Fold Between Two Points:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Match Points Use to fold a piece between two selected points. Learn How to Fold Between Two Points: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Match Points in the Folding panel. 2.	Select stationary point 3.	Select the fold point.

pages.title: Measure Angle
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Angle Use to measure the angle between two adjacent lines. To Measure an Angle: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Angle in the Measure panel. 2.	Select two adjacent lines. The measurement will appear on the piece.

pages.title: Measure Area

links.label: To Measure the Area of a Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Area Use to calculate the total area of a piece. To Measure the Area of a Piece: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Area in the Measure panel. 2.	Select the piece or pieces to measure the area.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces.

pages.title: Measure Between Notches

links.label: To Measure the Distance to a Notch:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Between Notches Use this function to measure the distance along the perimeter between a notch and another notch along a line or to measure the distance between a notch and the end of the line.  This function is a one step process. To Measure the Distance to a Notch: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Between Notches in the Measure panel. 2.	Select the segment of the line to measure.

pages.title: Measure Clear

links.label: Learn How to Clear All Measurements:
Learn How to Clear Selected Measurements:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Clear Remove measurements displayed in the work area All Use to remove all measurements displayed in the work area. Learn How to Clear All Measurements: 1.	From the Verify tab, select the Clear dropdown and then All in the Measure panel. 2.	All measurements are automatically removed. Use Selected  to remove selected measurements from the work area. Learn How to Clear Selected Measurements: 1.	From the Verify tab, select the Clear dropdown and then Selected in the Measure panel. 2.	Select the measurements to delete.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple measurements.

pages.title: Measure Distance 2 Lines

links.label: To Measure the Distance Between Two Lines:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Distance 2 Lines Use to measure the distance between two lines. The User Input box allows the user to determine various vertical and horizontal measurements. To Measure the Distance Between Two Lines: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Distance 2 Lines in the Measure panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Vertical – calculates a measurement across a piece in the Y axis. •	Horizontal – calculates a measurement across a piece in the X axis. •	Perpendicular to Grain – calculates a measurement that is at a right angle to the grain line. •	Parallel to Grain – calculates a measurement that is equal distance from the grain line. •	Select 2 Lines to Measure – controls how the lines are selected for the function.  When checked, the user will select 2 lines to indicate where the measurement should be taken. 3.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Select 2 Lines to Measure was chosen, select 2 lines to measure in between. •	If Select 2 Lines to Measure was not chosen, select 1 line to measure. 4.	Place the measuring line by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the measuring line. •	Value Mode – enter a distance in the Beg or End fields to position the measuring line.  This measurement determines the placement of the measuring line along the selected line.

pages.title: Measure Finished
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Finished Use this function to measure the finished straight distance between two sew lines. To Measure the Finished Distance: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Finished in the Measure panel. 2.	Select the first point to measure from. 3.	Select the second point.  The straight distance between the sew lines appears on the screen.

pages.title: Measure Line Length

links.label: To Measure the Length of a Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Line Length Use to measure the length of a perimeter or internal line. In PDS, a line length is calculated with smoothing points included. Reports do not consider the smoothing points for its calculations so the line lengths may differ. To Measure the Length of a Line: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Line Length in the Measure panel. 2.	Select a line or lines to measure.   Use the Ctrl key to select multiple lines.

pages.title: Measure Perimeter
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Perimeter Use to determine the total measurement of perimeter lines on a piece. In PDS, a line length is calculated with smoothing points included. Reports do not consider the smoothing points for its calculations so the line lengths may differ. To Measure the Piece Perimeter: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Perimeter in the Measure panel. 2.	Select the piece or pieces to measure the perimeter.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces.

pages.title: Measure Perimeter 2 Points

links.label: To Measure the Perimeter Distance Between Two Points:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Perimeter 2 Points Use to measure the distance between two points along the perimeter of a piece. In PDS, a line length is calculated with smoothing points included. Reports do not consider the smoothing points for its calculations so the line lengths may differ. To Measure the Perimeter Distance Between Two Points: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Perimeter 2 Points in the Measure panel. 2.	From the right button menu, select an option if desired. 3.	Select two points in a clockwise direction to measure the perimeter distance.

pages.title: Measure Straight

links.label: To Measure the Distance Between Two Points:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Straight Use to measure the straight distance between any two points on a piece. To Measure the Distance Between Two Points: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Straight in the Measure panel. 2.	Select two points on a piece to measure the straight distance. 3.	Select OK to measure another area.

pages.title: Measurements
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measurements Use this toggle function to hide or display the pattern’s measurements in the work area. In PDS, a line length is calculated with smoothing points included. Reports do not consider the smoothing points for its calculations so the line lengths may differ.

pages.title: Modify Image
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Modify Image Move Image The Move Image function is used to reposition textures/fills or images within a piece.  Moving textures/fills is helping when controlling to position of prints within a piece.  Moving images is helpful when position images of buttons, embroideries or logos to a specific location. You may also use this function to move edge finishes. Select the appropriate radio button for the image type: Fabric/Trim or Edge. When the function is selected the system prompts, “Select image(s) to move.”  The CTRL key can be used to select multiple images.  After clicking on the image, the image is attached to the cursor and can be moved to the desired location.  Left click to place the image. Rotate Image The Rotate Image function is used to orient textures/fills or images within a piece. When the function is selected the system prompts, “Select image(s) to rotate.”  The CTRL key can be used to select multiple images.  After clicking on the image, the image is attached to the cursor and can be rotated to the desired location.  Left click to place the image. Note: this function is only available for Fabric and Trim images.

pages.title: Modify Size Line

links.label: To Add a Numeric Break Size:
To Add an Alphanumeric Break Size:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Modify Size Line Size Step:Use this function to change the size step.  By changing the size step, the size line will have more or fewer sizes available.  This function keeps the dimensions of the original sizes the same.  This function is only available for pieces graded using Numeric rule tables. To Change the Size Step: 1.	Place the graded base pattern piece in the working area. 2.	From the Grade tab, select the Modify dropdown and then Size Step in the Size Line panel. 3.	Select the option Add as Break Sizes if you wish to use the new sizes as break sizes. By doing so, you will be able to use them when editing grade rules with Edit Delta 4.	Select the piece(s). Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 5.	The Select New Size Step chart will display.  Select the new size step from the dialog box. Select OK. Redistribute:Use to change the size step of a pattern and also to change the actual size/measurements of the graded sizes.  By changing the size step, the size line will have more or fewer sizes available.  This function is only available for pieces graded using Numeric rule tables. To Redistribute the Growths: 1.	Place the graded base pattern piece in the working area. 2.	From the Grade tab, select the Modify dropdown and then Redistribute in the Size Line panel. 3.	Select the option Add as Break Sizes if you wish to use the new sizes as break sizes. By doing so, you will be able to use them when editing grade rules with Edit Delta 4.	Select the piece(s). Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 5.	The Select New Size Step chart will display.  Select the new size step from the dialog box. Select OK. Break Sizes:Use this function to add or delete sizes to the original size range.  This change will affect only the pieces selected

pages.title: Move All to Next Tab

links.label: To Move All to the Next Tab Group

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Move All to Next Tab Move All to Next Tab Group: Use this function to move all open workspaces in the current tab group to the next tab group.  This feature is helpful if the screen is split into three or more groups to join tabs together thus providing more visible space in the work area. To Move All to the Next Tab Group 1.	From the View tab, select the Windows dropdown and then Move All to Next Tab Group in the Window panel.  The tabs are moved automatically.

pages.title: Move All to Previous Tab

links.label: To Move All to the Previous Tab Group

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Move All to Previous Tab Move All to Previous Tab Group: Use this function to move all open workspaces in the current tab group to the previous tab group.  This feature is helpful if the screen is split into three or more groups to join tabs together thus providing more visible space in the work area. To Move All to the Previous Tab Group 1.	From the View tab, select the Windows dropdown and then Move All to Previous Tab Group in the Window panel.  The tabs are moved automatically.

pages.title: Move to Next Tab Group

links.label: To Move the Current Tab to the Next Tab Group:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Move to Next Tab Group Move to Next Tab Group: Once a tab group is created, use this function to move the selected tab to the next tab group.  Moving tabs to another group allows for different pieces to be viewed or compared simultaneously. To Move the Current Tab to the Next Tab Group: 1.	From the View tab, select the Windows dropdown and then Move to Next Tab Group in the Window panel.  The tab is moved automatically.

pages.title: Move to Previous Tab Group

links.label: To Move the Current Tab to the Previous Tab Group:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Move to Previous Tab Group Move to Previous Tab Group Once a tab group is created, use this function to move the selected tab to the previous tab group.  Moving tabs to another group allows for different pieces to be viewed or compared simultaneously. To Move the Current Tab to the Previous Tab Group: 1.	From the View tab, select the Windows dropdown and then Move to Previous Tab Group in the Window panel.  The tab is moved automatically.

pages.title: Multiple

links.label: To Add Multiple Points Along a Line:
To Add Multiple Points Along a Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Multiple The Add Multiple group contains four functions to add multiple drills, notches, and mark points either spaced proportionally or spaced a specific distance apart. Add Drills Use to add a specific number of drill holes to a piece that are spaced evenly. To Add Multiple Drills: 1.	From the Point group, select Add Multiple and then Add Drills or press ALT + F6 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	None – neither the start nor the end location will become drills. •	Both – both the start and end locations will become drills. •	First – only the start location will become a drill. •	Last – only the end location will become a drill. 3.	Select the start and end location for the drills using one of the following methods: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to mark the start or end location. •	Value Mode – left click and drag the cursor to the location to measure from, click with the right button and release both mouse buttons.  Enter a distance in the Beg or End fields to add a point on a line or the X and Y fields to add a point in space. •	Right Mouse Button group – right click in the work area and select the desired option.  The Multiple options will not be available.  Read and follow the prompts for the steps to perform the function. 4.	Type in the number of drills to add in between the start and end locations. Add Drills Distance Use to add drill holes spaced a specific distance apart. To Add Multiple Drills: 1.	From the Point group select Add Multiple and then Add Drills Dist or press ALT + F7 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	None – neither the start nor the end location will become drills. •	Both – both the start and end locations will become drills. •

pages.title: View Names

links.label: Learn How to Display Line Names:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Names Use to display line names. Learn How to Display Line Names: 1.	From the View tab, select Names in the Lines panel. 2.	Select the piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces or lines. 3.	To remove the line names from the display, exit the function.

pages.title: New Window
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search New Window New Window: Use this function to open a new, empty work area. To Open a New Window: 1.	From the View tab, select the Windows dropdown and then New in the Window panel.  A new, empty work area will open automatically.

pages.title: Notch

links.label: To Move a Notch Along a Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Notch Use to move a notch along a line. To Move a Notch Along a Line: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Notch in the Notch Actions panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Copy Distance – 3.	Select a notch to move. 4.	Move the notch to a new location by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to place the point. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter a distance in the Beg, End or Dist fields.

pages.title: Notch Positions
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Notch Positions Show notches whose distances will be maintained after applying shrink or stretch.

pages.title: Notch Shapes
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Notch Shapes Shapes (F12)- This function will show the plotted shape of a notch.  The shape is determined by the P-Notch table.  Notches will display as slit notches by default outside this function.  The function is automatically performed on all pieces in the work area.  To remove the notch shapes from the work area, exit the function.

pages.title: Notch Types

links.label: Learn How to View Notch Types:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Notch Types Types: - Use this function to see the notch type and the reference distance.  If there is a group of notches, the information will display only for the first notch in the group (the notch closest to the reference point). Learn How to View Notch Types: 1.	From the View menu, select Notch then Types. 2.	Select the piece(s) or notch(es).  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Notch

links.label: To Create a Notch Parameter Table:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Notch The Notch Parameter Table is where the notch types and sizes are defined that will be placed on pieces in a particular storage area. A single table can hold up to 99 different notches. More than one notch table can be created within a storage area. However, if only one is needed, it is recommended that the default name (P-NOTCH) remains unchanged. To Create a Notch Parameter Table: 1.	 From the Edit Tab, click the Notch icon in the Parameter Tables group. 2.	Complete the Notch Type, Perimeter Width, Inside Width, and Notch Depth fields as needed for up to 99 different notches. •	Notch Type – the shape that notch will be on the plotted piece or marker.  Choose from Slit, T, V, Castle, Left Check, Right Check and U. •	Perimeter Width – the gap of the notch at the perimeter of the piece. •	Inside Width – the width at the bottom of the notch. •	Notch Depth – the distance from the perimeter of the piece to the bottom of the notch.  An internal notch, like the Slit or Internal V Notch, will have a positive value for its depth.  An external notch, like the Castle Notch, will have a negative value for its depth. 3.	Select File, and then Save. NOTE:  The U Notch type is used when converting data in ASTM format.  If this notch type is plotted, the actual shape will be the same as a castle notch.

pages.title: Note/Illustrate

links.label: Learn How to Add Notes/Illustrations to an Existing Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Note/Illustrate Use this function to draw pictures or write construction notes on existing pieces. This function works similar to the Sketch command.  Any internal lines added with the Note/Illustrate function will automatically be labeled with an “I”. Learn How to Add Notes/Illustrations to an Existing Piece: 1.	From the DraftTab, select Draft Scale. 2.	Reorient the pattern on the screen to the pattern on the table. 3.	From the Draft Tab, select Note/Illustrate. 4.	Select the piece to write notes or add illustrations. 5.	Begin drawing a line by pressing and holding the stylus pen down. To finish the line, lift the pen tip off the table.  When finished, select OK. NOTE: To erase a note or illustration line, click the button on the stylus pen and select Erase.

pages.title: Numbers
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Numbers Use to display the point numbers on an AccuMark piece. The numbers display on the screen next to the point. Learn to View Point Numbers: 1.	From the View tab, select Numbers in the Point panel. 2.	The point numbers will immediately display on all pieces in the work area. 3.	To remove the point numbers from the work area, select the function again.

pages.title: Fullness On Line

links.label: Learn to Add or Subtract Fullness:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fullness On Line Use to distribute an amount of fullness evenly along an entire line. Learn to Add or Subtract Fullness: 1.	From the Advanced Tab, select On Line from the Fullness Group. 2.	Select a perimeter line to add or subtract fullness by left clicking on it. 3.	Select the line to slash to by left clicking on it.  Lines will be drawn between this line and the fullness line to cut the piece for adding or subtracting fullness. 4.	Select the line to hold by left clicking on it. This line will not move when the fullness is added or subtracted. 5.	Enter the fullness amount.  This can be a linear amount (in inches or centimeters) or a percentage.  For example, entering 200% would make the fullness line twice as long or add 2:1 fullness.

pages.title: Open/Close Pleat
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Open/Close Pleat Use this function to toggle the state a pleat object, open (it will appear unfolded) or closed ( it will appear folded). Pleat objects are only created in version 10 software. Pleats created on prior versions of AccuMark are not pleat objects; they are only a group of internal lines and notches.

pages.title: Original
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Original This function creates a copy of the selected piece which represents the original piece shape as well as internal lines.

pages.title: Pan
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Pan Change zoom area to without moving the pieces.

pages.title: Parallel Fullness

links.label: Learn How to Add or Subtract Parallel Fullness:
To Add or Subtract Parallel Fullness to Multiple Pieces:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Parallel Fullness Use to add or subtract fullness in order to lengthen or shorten a piece. Parallel fullness allows for an amount of fullness to be added or removed from a piece using slash lines.  A portion of the piece will be held stationary while the fullness is opened.  There are three options for selection of the location to remain stationary: •	The pivot point – by selecting the pivot point, the piece will open to both sides for the fullness, as shown below.  To select the pivot point, click and hold on the slash line.  Move the cursor to the pivot point of the slash line.  A circle will highlight to indicate the pivot point.  Once this point highlights, release the mouse button. •	Between two slash lines – allows multiple slash lines to open in different directions.  Left click on the line segment between the two slash lines. •	Another perimeter line – holds part of the perimeter while the fullness is opened or closed.  Left click on the perimeter line to hold on grain. Learn How to Add or Subtract Parallel Fullness: 1.	From the Piece menu, select Fullness and then Parallel Fullness. 2.	Draw slash lines by selecting a point on the perimeter where the fullness will begin (pivot point) and end (open point) in cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the beginning and end points of the slash line. •	Value Mode – left click and hold on the line where the slash line will begin.  Click right and release both buttons.  Enter the measurements for the position of the first point in the Beg or End fields.  Repeat these steps for the second point of the slash line. •	Right Mouse Button Menu – right click in the work area and select the desired option.  Read and follow the prompts for the steps to perform the function. 3.	Cre

pages.title: Measure Perimeter 2 Points

links.label: Learn to Measure the Distance Between Two Points along a line for all sizes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Perimeter 2 Points Use to measure along a line or curve between two selected points for all graded sizes. This function is the same function as in the Verify tab. When performing the function from the Grade tab, it will generate measurements not only for the base size, but also for all the graded sizes. Learn to Measure the Distance Between Two Points along a line for all sizes: 1. From the Grade Tab, select Perimeter 2 Points in the Measure panel 2. Select the first point on a piece perimeter line to measure the distance along the line from 3. Select the second point on a piece perimeter line to measure the distance along the line to Select the following User Input option if: • Display X/Y Values – to include columns to display the X and Y differences between the selected points. X and Y guidelines are also displayed in the work area. 4. Select OK to display the measure chart: it displays the straight length value per size, X Distance and the X Difference between sizes. Same values for Y. the Total will display the total sum of all pairs of point distance(s) if more than one set was selected. Size Difference shows the difference between totals in all sizes. 5. Print – click on this button to output the chart directly to the printer of your choice 6. Copy – click on this button to copy the chart information and paste in the program of your choice. This information is output as csv format so if pasted in a spreadsheet in MS-Excel each column and value will be populated in separate fields. 7. Click the X button to close the dialog and continue working in the function 8. When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Perimeter Point

links.label: Learn How to Fold Between Two Perimeter Points:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Perimeter Point Use to fold a piece between two selected perimeter points. Learn How to Fold Between Two Perimeter Points: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Perimeter in the Folding panel. 2.	Select the first fold point. 3.	Select the second fold point. 4.	Select the location on the perimeter in part of the piece to fold.  The section containing this line will move to fold the piece.

pages.title: Annotations
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Annotations Use this function to display all  annotations for pieces in the work area.

pages.title: Corners On/Off
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Corners On/Off Corners On/Off: Use to show/hide corners without removing corner information. To Show or Hide Corner: 1.	From the View tab, select Corners On/Off in the Piece panel. 2.	Select the piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 3.	Select the piece(s) again to redisplay the corner

pages.title: Curved Intersections
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Curved Intersections Displays unsevered curved intersection lines on selected pieces in red.

pages.title: Piece Info
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Piece Info Toggle the view to show/hide the piece information for all pieces in the work area.

pages.title: Intersection

This function applies the grading from the perimeter line to the end of the internal so that the internal line will intersect the perimeter of each graded size.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Grade an Internal Line in the X Direction: 1.	From the Grade tab, in the Create/Edit Rules panel select the Intersection Drop down and then Intersection X. 2.	Select the point to grade. Intersection Y:Use this function to find the grading for the end of an internal line that intersects a perimeter line, in an Y direction.  This function applies the grading from the perimeter line to the end of the internal so that the internal line will intersect the perimeter of each graded size.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Grade an Internal Line in the Y Direction: 1.	From the Grade tab, in theCreate/Edit panel select the Intersection Drop down and then  Intersection Y. 2.	Select the point to grade. Intersection Parallel: Use to find the X and Y grading for the end of an internal line, so that it remains parallel on all sizes and intersects with the perimeter, when the other end is graded.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Grade the Intersection of an Internal Parallel for All Sizes: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Create/Edit Rules and then Intersect Parallel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Find Rule for Both Ends – gradin

pages.title: Keep Angle

links.label: Learn How to Keep the Angle for All Sizes:
Learn How to Keep the Angle for All Sizes in the X direction:
Learn How to Keep the Angle for All Sizes in the Y direction:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Keep Angle Keep Angle Apex: Use this function to create a grade rule at a point to maintain the angle of the base size at that point for all sizes in the nest.   One of the two lines can be an internal.  Perform this function with the graded nest displayed to see the change.  On some pieces, the change that takes place is very subtle.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Keep the Angle for All Sizes: 1. Keep Angle Edge X: This function will create a grade rule at a point with growth in the X direction only and maintain one angle for all sizes.  One of the two lines can be an internal.  Perform this function with the graded nest displayed to see the change.  On some pieces, the change that takes place is very subtle.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Keep the Angle for All Sizes in the X direction: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Keep Angle Edge X. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual  – not available. •	Both if Same  – not available. •	Always Both – applies the same grading to both corner endpoints. 3.	Select the point to be graded.  This point should be an existing grade point. 4.	Select the apex point of the angle to maintain . 5.	Select the other point on the edge of the angle to maintain . Keep Angle Edge Y: This function will create a grade rule at a point with growth in the Y direction only and maintain one angle for all sizes.  One of the two lines can be an internal.  Perform th

pages.title: Match Line

links.label: Learn How to Match a Line in the X direction:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Match Line Match Line X: Use this function to create a new grade rule that lets the graded line length of one line match the grading of another.  A non-graded line is selected, and then the lines to match are selected. The result is a line graded in the X direction that matches the other line(s) for all sizes.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Match a Line in the X direction: 1.
