Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual  – not available. •	Both if Same  – not available. •	Always Both – applies the same grading to both corner endpoints. 4.	Select the line to be graded. 5.	Select the end point of the line to receive the new grade rule. 6.	Select the line(s) to match lengths .  When finished, select OK. Match Line Y: Use this function to create a new grade rule that lets the graded line length of one line match the grading of another.  A non-graded line is selected, and then the lines to match are selected. The result is a line graded in the Y direction that matches the other line(s) for all sizes.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Match a Line in the Y direction: 1.	Start with a grade point that has a growth of 0,0. 2.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Match Line Y. 3.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual  – not available. •	Both if Same  – not available. •	Always Both – applies the same grading to both corner endpoints. 4.	Select the line to be graded. Select the end point of the

pages.title: Mirror Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Mirror Piece Unfold Mirror Use to open or fold a  mirrored piece. Remember, if changes are made to a mirrored piece while it is unfolded, the system no longer considers it as a mirrored piece.  Measurements may be taken while the piece is unfolded. To Unfold a Mirrored Piece: 1.	From the View tab, select the Mirror dropdown and then Unfold in the Piece panel. 2.	Select the mirrored piece(s) to unfold.  Use the Ctrl key to unfold multiple pieces. Fold Mirror To fold a mirrored piece that has been unfolded. The mirror line displays as a dotted line. To Fold a Mirrored Piece: 1.	From the View tab, select the Mirror dropdown and then Fold in the Piece panel. 2.	Select piece(s) to fold.  Use the Ctrl key to fold multiple pieces.

pages.title: Parallel

links.label: Learn How to Create the New Grade Rule Parallel in the X direction:
Learn How to Create the New Grade Rule Parallel in the Y direction:
Learn How to Create a Grade Rule that remains parallel and also extends:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Parallel Parallel X: Use to create a grade rule at a point that makes one of the two lines of the intersection, parallel for all sizes.  This function creates a growth value in the X direction only.  Perform this function with the graded nest displayed to see the change.  On some pieces, the change that takes place is very subtle.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Create the New Grade Rule Parallel in the X direction: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Parallel X. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Individual  – allows for the two corner end points to have different grading values applied.  If a grade rule is copied with the “individual” option selected, the rule is only copied to one end of one of the lines of the corner.  This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Both if Same  – applies grading to both corner end points if they had the same rule originally. This option only applies when the Perimeter is set to Unclipped. •	Always Both – applies the grading to both corner endpoints. 3.	Select the point to be graded. 4.	Select the other grade point to maintain the parallel edge. Parallel Y: Use to create a grade rule at a point that makes one of the two lines of the intersection, parallel for all sizes.  This function creates a growth value in the Y direction only.  Perform this function with the graded nest displayed to see the change.  On some pieces, the change that takes place is very subtle.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is edited. Learn How to Create the New Grade Rule Parallel in the Y direction: 1.	From the Gra

pages.title: Piece Positions
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Piece Positions Displays pieces on screen according to how they were placed when a position was defined. To Use a Position: 1.	Bring the pieces into the work area. 2.	From the View tab, select the Positions dropdown and then Use in the Piece panel or press the Shift + F11 keys on the keyboard. 3.	Select the name from the Position Name field of the User Input box and select OK. Define : Use to define and store the screen placement of pieces.  This function is used in conjunction with Use Position. To Define a Position: 1.	Arrange the pieces in the work area in the desired layout. 2.	From the View tab, select the Positions dropdown and then Define in the Piece panel. 3.	Type a name for the position in the Position Name field of the User Input box. 4.	Select the desired piece(s) in the work area.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 5.	Use Save or Save As to save the pieces or models to save the position. Remove: Use to remove a position from pieces, created with Define Position. To Remove a Position: 1.	From the View tab, select the Positions dropdown and then Remove in the Piece panel. 2.	Select the name from the Position Name field of the User Input box or check the option, Remove All Positions. 3.	Select OK.

pages.title: Seam Amounts
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Seam Amounts Use this function to view the seam allowance amounts applied. To View the Seam Amounts: 1.	From the View tab, select Seam Amounts in the Piece panel. 2.	Select the line(s) or piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple lines or pieces. 3.	To remove the seam amounts, perform the function again.

pages.title: Seam Corners
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Seam Corners Use this function to display seam corner types. To View the Seam Amounts: 1.	From the View tab, select Seam Amounts in the Piece panel. 2.	Select the line(s) or piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple lines or pieces. 3.	To remove the seam amounts, perform the function again.

pages.title: Piece Utility

links.label: Learn How to Use the Piece Utility:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Piece Utility The Piece Utility function is used to reset point and line information on pieces. Six options are available in the function.  This function is also available by right clicking on the work area when no functions are active (idle state). Learn How to Use the Piece Utility: 1.	From the Edit tab, select Piece Utility in the Properties panel. 2.	Select from the following options: •	Match End Points – sets the end of both lines that make up a corner to the same point information. The grade rule, point number and attributes will all be copied from the beginning of the second line going in the clockwise direction to the end of the previous line. This can cause different results in the graded nest. •	Clear Point Numbers - removes all of the special point numbers from a piece. New point numbers can then be added individually using Edit Point Info or Copy Point Numbers can be used to copy numbers from another piece. •	Suppress Points – removes extra points when multiple points exist at the same location. This can be helpful when a piece is not smoothing properly because there are two intermediate points at the same location. •	Clipped Perimeter – changes any unclipped perimeter lines in the piece into clipped lines. •	Copy Point Numbers – use to copy point numbers from the perimeter to the seam internals. •	Remove Unavailable Grading – converts any graded points for which there is no corresponding growth information into a non-graded point. This is helpful when the error, "Error grading piece" is given when trying to display a graded nest for a piece. 3.	Select the pieces to change.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces.

pages.title: Pleat Fold

links.label: Learn How to Fold a Pleat:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Pleat Fold Use to fold a piece between two selected points in order to fold a pleat.  Multiple pleats can be folded to verify accurate underlay and a smooth sew line. Learn How to Fold a Pleat: 1.	From the Verify tab, select Pleat in the Folding panel. 2.	Select the first fold point. 3.	Select the second fold point.  If needed, repeat with additional pleats.

pages.title: Point
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Point Use to move a point in any direction; adjacent points will remain stationary. This function may also be applied to move a group of points by selecting more than one point to move. To Move a Point: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Point in the Point Actions panel or press ALT + F2 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select option Move Both Joined End Points to move an end point independent of the line extensions. If the option is unselected, an end point will only move along the extensions of the lines. 3.	Select the point(s) to move. Use the Ctrl key to select multiple points. 4.	Move the point(s) to a new location by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to place the point. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter a distance in the X or Y fields.

pages.title: Point/Drill
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Point/Drill Use to create intermediate or internal point(s) on a piece.  If a point is added to the interior of a piece, it is automatically considered to be a drill hole. To Add a Point: 1.	From the Point group, select Point/Drill or press ALT + F4 keys on the keyboard.. 2.	Select the N Attribute option if the point being added should be a non-smoothing point. 3.	Select the point location using one of the following methods: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to add the point. •	Value Mode – left click and drag the cursor to the point to measure from, click the right button and release both buttons.  Enter a distance in the Beg or End fields to add a point on a line or the X and Y fields to add a point in space. •	Right Mouse Button group – right click in the work area and select the desired option.  Read and follow the prompts for the steps to perform the function. NOTE: If a drill hole is created, it will automatically be labeled with a D.

pages.title: Point/Line

links.label: To Move a Point Along a Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Point/Line Use to move a point along a line.  This function can reposition an end point along the extension of a line while other points on the line remain stationary.  Move Point Line/Slide can also be used to adjust the placement of standard notches. To Move a Point Along a Line: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Point/Line in the Point Actions panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	First Line – when an end point is selected, the point will only move along the line before the selected point. •	Second Line – when an end point is selected, the point will only move along the line after the selected point. •	Closest Line – when an end point is selected, the point will move along both the lines before and after the selected point. 3.	Select a point to move. 4.	Move the point to a new location by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to place the point. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter a distance in the Beg, End or Dist fields.

pages.title: View Points of Measurement
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Points of Measurement View/Work Area/Point of Measurement is used to hide and show the Point of Measurement data on the workarea.  This function ia a toggle function and is ON by default.

pages.title: Positions
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Positions Use Change Keep Position to define whether a Notch position should maintain its relative position in a line or if it should be adjusted when Scale Piece or Shrink/Stretch is applied to a piece. Check the option Keep Position if the notch should be maintained at the same position as in the original piece geometry.

pages.title: Redo

links.label: To Redo the Last Operation that was Undone:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Redo Use this function to redo the last action that was "undone." The name of the last operation is listed in the drop-down menu.  This function is also available by right clicking on the work area when no functions are active (idle state). To Redo the Last Operation that was Undone: 1.	From the Edit menu, select Redo or press the CTRL + Y keys on the keyboard.  The function is automatically performed. 2.	If desired, continue to select this function to redo previously "undone" operations.

pages.title: Reference Notch: Add Group on Line

links.label: To Add Group of Notches on Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Reference Notch: Add Group on Line This function is used to add a group of notches evenly spaced between two points. When the line is modified the group maintains the spacing between the notches. The group maintains the spacing when geometry is modified. Reference notches maintain their distance to another point on all sizes.  Tangent notches are reference notches where the distance between the notch and the reference point changes on graded sizes. To Add Group of Notches on Line: 1.	From the Create tab, select the Reference dropdown and then Add Group on Line in the Notch panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	None – adds no notches to the ends points defined for the group. •	Both – adds a notch to both end points defined for the group. •	First – adds a notch to the First point of the group going clockwise. •	Last – adds a notch to the Last point of the group going clockwise. •	Type – controls the kind of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. •	Depth – view the notch depth defined in the P-Notch table.  This field is not editable. •	Number Of – indicates how many notches should be added.  Type in the desired number. •	Perpendicular – the notch will be placed on the seam allowance by extending a perpendicular (90-degree angle) line from the notched line. •	Notch Angle – notches will be placed on the seam allowance by extending the angle created by the original notch. •	Same Distance on Seam – notches will be placed on the seam allowance using the same measurement as the reference distance. 3.	Select a line to receive notches. 4.	Reposition the thumbtacks to define the range or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cur

pages.title: Reference Notch: Add Group on Line Distance

links.label: To Add Group of Notches on Line by Distance:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Reference Notch: Add Group on Line Distance This function is used to add a group of notches spaced by a specified amount. When the line is modified the group maintains the spacing between the notches. The group maintains the spacing when geometry is modified. Reference notches maintain their distance to another point on all sizes.  Tangent notches are reference notches where the distance between the notch and the reference point changes on graded sizes. To Add Group of Notches on Line by Distance: 1.	From the Create tab, select the Reference dropdown and then Add Group on Line Distance in the Notch panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	None – adds no notches to the ends points defined for the group. •	Both – adds a notch to both end points defined for the group. •	First – adds a notch to the First point of the group going clockwise. •	Last – adds a notch to the Last point of the group going clockwise. •	Type – controls the kind of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. •	Depth – view the notch depth defined in the P-Notch table.  This field is not editable. •	Dist Between – the measurement between each notch in the group.  Type in the desired amount. •	Perpendicular – the notch will be placed on the seam allowance by extending a perpendicular (90-degree angle) line from the notched line. •	Notch Angle – notches will be placed on the seam allowance by extending the angle created by the original notch. •	Same Distance on Seam – notches will be placed on the seam allowance using the same measurement as the reference distance. 3.	Select a line to receive notches. 4.	Reposition the thumbtacks to define the range or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the th

pages.title: Reference
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Reference Use to select new reference point for a reference notch.  This function can also be used to change a reference notch to a standard notch and vice versa. Reference notches maintain their distance to another point on all sizes.  Tangent notches are reference notches where the distance between the notch and the reference point changes on graded sizes. To Change a Notch Reference: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Reference in the Notch Actions panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Add Base Point – adds a base reference point to the notch.  Used when converting a reference notch into a standard notch. •	N Attribute – check this option to make the base reference point a non-smoothing point. 3.	Select the notch to change. 4.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Add Base Point was not chosen, select the new reference point for the notch.  The notch will remain a reference notch. •	If Add Base Point was chosen, click the left button to change the reference to the new base point.  The notch will become a standard notch.

pages.title: Regroup
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Regroup Regroup: Use this function to regroup all tab groups into one work area.  Once selected only the current tab work area will display. To Regroup All Tab Groups: 1.	From the View tab, select the Windows dropdown and then Regroup in the Window panel.  The tabs are joined automatically into one workspace with the current tab displayed.

pages.title: Reorient

links.label: Learn How to Reorient a Piece that Has Been Moved:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Reorient Use this function to establish a relationship between a pattern on the Silhouette table and its corresponding draft piece or working piece on-screen. A piece needs to be reoriented if it has been moved on the table or if you are modifying an existing pattern that has recently been taped to the table. For example, a pattern is entered into the system using the Sketch or Line/Curve functions. The pattern on the table is moved or work is interrupted. Use this function to return the draft piece on-screen exactly in the same position as the pattern on the table. Learn How to Reorient a Piece that Has Been Moved: 1.	From the Draft tab, select Draft Scale in the Work Area panel. 2.	From the Draft tab, select Reorient in the Work Area panel. 3.	Select the piece to reorient.  When finished, select OK. 4.	Select two points on the piece in the work area from left to right. To ensure accuracy, select the two furthest points. 5.	Select the two corresponding points on the piece on the table, in the same order. 6.	A dialog box will display showing the difference between the piece on the screen and the piece on the table. Select Yes to move the piece on the screen using these points.  Select No to select points on the piece on the table again.

pages.title: Report Results
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Report Results Use to show the conversion report results.

pages.title: Reset Original Bookmark

links.label: Learn how to Reset Original Bookmark

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Reset Original Bookmark Reset Original: Resets the original bookmark to match the current piece shape. Learn how to Reset Original Bookmark 1. From the Edit Tab, select Reset Original from the Bookmark group. 2. Select the piece(s) to reset the bookmark. 3. Click OK to complete the function.

pages.title: Reshape Curve
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Reshape Curve Use to change the shape of a curve that spans across multiple pieces. Placing the pieces together first may make it easier to visually see the effect on the curve.  When selecting the lines to reshape, the clockwise direction is determined on the pieces as if they were one larger piece. To Reshape a Curve: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select Reshape Curve in the Pattern Changes panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input Options: •	Show Thumbtacks – controls the display of the thumbtacks for defining a range.  Showing the thumbtacks will allow the user to define the range as a part of the function.  If this button is not selected, the range is automatically assigned based on the other options, Prev/Next Points or End Points. •	Prev/Next Points – places the thumbtacks at the point before and the point after the selected point by default. •	End Points – places the thumbtacks at the end points of the line by default. 3.	Select lines to reshape going clockwise.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple lines. 4.	Select a point(s) to move.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple points. 5.	If Show Thumbtacks was selected, reposition the thumbtacks to define the range or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks. 9.	Move the point(s) to a new location by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to place the point. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter a distance in the X and Y fields.

pages.title: Restack

links.label: Learn How to Stack a Nest at a Selected Point:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Restack Use to change the point where the graded sizes are lined up on a nest.  This function shifts the grading, but the dimensions of the graded sizes do not change.  Stacking can be applied to one or two points. Learn How to Stack a Nest at a Selected Point: 1.	Display the graded nest of sizes by using the function Grade / All Sizes. 2.	From the Grade tab, select Restack in the View panel or press the CTRL + K keys on the keyboard. 3.	Check the Stack 2 Points option to select 2 points to restack the graded nest.  This option allows for the graded sizes to be restacked and then rotated to align the graded sizes along a line or portion of a line. 4.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Stack 2 Points was selected, select the first stack point by left clicking on the point on the base size.  Select the second stack point in the same manner. •	If Stack 2 Points was not selected, select the first stack point by left clicking on the point on the base size. 5.	The graded nest will be restacked at the selected point(s).  To remove the new stacking, select the point again without exiting the function.

pages.title: Restore Defined Bookmark
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Restore Defined Bookmark Allows you to extract a copy of the defined piece perimeter when using Define Bookmark

pages.title: Rotate Grade 90

links.label: Learn to Rotate the Growth 90 Degrees:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Rotate Grade 90 Use to rotate the growth of a grade rule assigned to a point, 90 degrees clockwise.  The X values will become the Y values and the Y values will become the X values.  To show that a change has been made, an asterisk (*) will be put on the grade rule number after it is modified. Learn to Rotate the Growth 90 Degrees: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Rotate 90 in the Modify panel. 2.	Select a grade point to rotate 90 degrees.

pages.title: Rule Number
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Rule Number Use to assign grade rules numbers to selected points. To Edit the Grading: 1.	From the Grade tab, select Rule Number in the Modify Panel.  The Tracking Information dialog box displays. 2.	Select a point(s).  If Tracking is used, wait for the point to highlight and click Stop.  To deselect a point, select it again.  To completely clear the selection, right click in the work area and select Clear All. 3.	To edit the Grade Rule, click in the Grade Rule field and type in the new grade rule number or type –1 to remove the existing grading. 4.	Select Apply.  Select the next point to edit. 5.	Click OK to close the dialog box.

pages.title: Scale Piece

links.label: Learn How to Apply Scaling to a Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Scale Piece Use this function to scale a piece larger or smaller using a percentage or linear value. Learn How to Apply Scaling to a Piece: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select Scale in the Fabric panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Linear - to apply a scale amount in inches or centimeters. Use a positive amount to make the piece larger and a negative amount to make the piece smaller. •	Percent - to apply a scale amount as a percentage of the overall piece size. The number typed in is based on 100%.  For example, to make a piece larger by 5%, enter 105. To make a piece smaller by 5%, enter 95. 3.	Enter the Scale Amount for X and Y. 4.	Select the piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces.

pages.title: Zoom to Selected

links.label: Learn How to Zoom to a Selected Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Zoom to Selected Makes the highlighted piece the largest piece in the work area.  Other pieces will remain on the work area. Learn How to Zoom to a Selected Piece: 1.	Highlight a piece by placing the mouse over the desired piece.  Do not pick the piece up with the cursor. 2.	From the View tab, select Selected in the Zoom panel or press the F4 key on the keyboard.  The function is automatically performed

pages.title: View Selected Sizes

links.label: To View the Grade on Selected Sizes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search View Selected Sizes Use to display specific sizes from the graded nest. To View the Grade on Selected Sizes: 1.	From the Grade Tab, select View and then Show Selected Sizes. 2.	Select a piece(s). When finished, select OK. 3.	A dialog box will display.  Select the desired sizes.  Use the CTRL key to select more than one. 4.	Click OK.  The selected sizes will be displayed along with the base size for reference.

pages.title: Separate

links.label: Learn How to Separate Pieces in the Work Area

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Separate Use to display the pieces in the work area lined up at full scale. Learn How to Separate Pieces in the Work Area 1. To use this function, from the View Tab, select  Separate Pieces from the Zoom Groupor press the F2 key on the keyboard. 2. The function is automatically performed.

pages.title: Set Selected

links.label: To Set a Piece as the Selected Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Set Selected Use this function to set a piece as the selected piece.  The pieces will remain selected Set Selected is chosen again.  This function can be helpful if several commands need to be done to the same group of pieces (Shrink/Stretch, Rotate, etc.). To Set a Piece as the Selected Piece: 1.	From the Edit tab select Set Selected. from the Selection Group. 2.	Select piece(s) to set current. 3.	When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Shrink/Stretch

links.label: Learn How to Apply a Shrink or Stretch Tolerance to a Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Shrink/Stretch Applies a fabric shrink or stretch tolerance to a pattern piece.  The Shrink Stretch (><) symbol will display on the piece in the piece geometry in the work area. The actual fabric shrink or stretch value is applied to each graded size. Pattern Design automatically creates modified grade rules to maintain both, the grading and the shrink/stretch amount applied for all sizes. Learn How to Apply a Shrink or Stretch Tolerance to a Piece: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select Shrink/Stretch in the Fabric panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Linear – to apply a shrink or stretch amount in inches or centimeters.  Use a positive amount to make the piece smaller and a negative amount to make the piece larger. •	Percent – to apply a shrink/stretch amount as a percentage of the overall piece size.  Use a positive percentage to make the piece smaller and a negative amount to make the piece larger. •	Remove – removes any applied shrink or stretch and returns the piece to its original size. Only available if a selected piece has applied shrink/stretch. This option has no effect once the piece has been saved. •	Clear Symbol – removes the Shrink/Stretch symbol from the piece icon without changing piece dimensions. 3.	Enter the Shrink/Stretch Amounts for X and Y. 4.	Select the piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces.

pages.title: Single Point
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Single Point This function moves a single point in any direction; adjacent points will remain stationary.  This method is often used to move individual points to edit the shape of a curve. To Move a Single Point: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Single Point in the Point Actions panel or press ALT + F12 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select option Move Both Joined End Points to move an end point independent of the line extensions. If the option is unselected, an end point will only move along the extensions of the lines. 3.	Select the point to move. 4.	Place the selected point in a new location by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to place the point. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter a distance in the X or Y fields.

pages.title: Sketch

links.label: Learn How to Sketch a New Pattern:
Learn How to Sketch Lines on an Existing Pattern:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Sketch Use this function to input a new pattern or draw lines on an existing pattern using the Silhouette table.  Paper patterns can also be traced using Sketch.  The stylus pen can be used the same way a pencil would.  As lines are drawn on the table, the system will simultaneously display the lines on the screen. Learn How to Sketch a New Pattern: 1.	From the Draft Tab, select Draft Scale. 2.	From the Draft Tab, select Sketch. 3.	Click the button on the pen and check the option Create Draft Piece. 4.	Begin drawing a line by pressing and holding the stylus pen down. To finish the line, lift the pen tip off the table.  Use patterns, curves, rulers, or sketch freehand to create lines. When using sketch to trace around a hard paper pattern, it is best to stop slightly before the corner to produce sharp corners. 5.	When finished with the draft piece, click the button and select OK. 6.	Use the Draft Trace or Create Piece functions to make the draft piece into a valid piece. NOTE: To erase a sketched line, click the button on the stylus pen and select Erase. Learn How to Sketch Lines on an Existing Pattern: 1.	From the Draft Tab, select Draft Scale. 2.	Reorient the pattern on the screen to the pattern on the table. 3.	From the Draft Tab, select Sketch. 4.	Click the button on the pen and uncheck the option Create Draft Piece. 5.	Select the piece to add lines. 6.	Begin drawing a line by pressing and holding the stylus pen down. To finish the line, lift the pen tip off the table.  Use patterns, curves, rulers, or sketch freehand to create lines. 7.	When finished adding lines to the piece, click the button and select OK. NOTE: Sketched lines will automatically be labeled with an “I”.

pages.title: Slash n Spread

links.label: Learn How to Add or Subtract Tapered Fullness to Multiple Pieces:
Learn How to Add or Subtract Tapered Fullness to Multiple Pieces:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Slash n Spread Tapered Slash n Spread:Use to add or subtract tapered fullness to more than one piece at a time.  Pieces can be stacked in the work area to add the same fullness or lined up next to each other to add a tapering fullness through all pieces. Learn How to Add or Subtract Tapered Fullness to Multiple Pieces: 1.	Arrange the pieces as desired on the work area. 2.	From the Advanced tab, select the Slash n Spread dropdown  and then Tapered in the Fullness panel. 3.	Select the pieces to add or subtract fullness.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 4.	Draw slash lines by selecting a point on the perimeter where the fullness will begin (pivot point) and end (open point) in cursor or value mode.  No fullness will be added at the pivot point of the slash line: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the beginning and end points of the slash line. •	Value Mode – left click and hold on the line where the slash line will begin.  Click right and release both buttons.  Enter the measurements for the position of the first point in the Beg or End fields.  Repeat these steps for the second point of the slash line. •	Right Mouse Button Menu – right click in the work area and select the desired option.  Read and follow the prompts for the steps to perform the function. 5.	Create additional slash lines, if desired.  All slash lines must start on the same perimeter line.  When finished, select OK. 6.	Select a point on the piece perimeter to remain stationary.  Select one of the following: •	The pivot point •	Between two slash lines •	Another perimeter line 7.	Select any internal lines to move while adding or removing the fullness.  Internal lines that are not selected will remain in the same position relative to the grain line.  When finished,

pages.title: Smooth
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Smooth Use to move points in any direction.  The point(s) and lines adjacent to the point being moved are smoothed or curved by the system.  Thumbtacks can isolate a section of the line to change. To Move Smooth a Point: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Smooth in the Point Actions panel or press ALT + F11 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input Options: •	Show Thumbtacks – controls the display of the thumbtacks for defining a range.  Showing the thumbtacks will allow the user to define the range as a part of the function.  If this button is not selected, the range is automatically assigned based on the other options, Prev/Next Points or End Points. •	Prev/Next Points – places the thumbtacks at the point before and the point after the selected point by default. •	End Points – places the thumbtacks at the end points of the line by default. 3.	Select point(s) to move.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple points. . 4.	If Show Thumbtacks was selected, reposition the thumbtacks to define the range or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks. 5.	Move the point(s) to a new location by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to place the point. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter a distance in the X and Y fields.

pages.title: Smooth Grade

links.label: Learn How to Smooth Grading on a Curve:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Smooth Grade Use to automatically create smoother grading along a curve.  The result is similar to removing the grade rule(s) along a curve to allow the curve to “relax” and then using the function Add Grade Point to add grade points back in. Learn How to Smooth Grading on a Curve: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Smooth Grade. 2.	Select the points to smooth evenly.  The points selected can be intermediate points or existing grade points.  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Smooth/Line

links.label: To Move Smooth a Point Along a Line:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Smooth/Line Use to move a point along a line extension.  The point(s) and lines adjacent to the point being moved are smoothed or curved by the system.  Thumbtacks can isolate a section of the line to change. To Move Smooth a Point Along a Line: 1.	From the Modify tab, select Smooth/Line in the Point Actions panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	First Line – when an end point is selected, the point will only move along the line before the selected point. •	Second Line – when an end point is selected, the point will only move along the line after the selected point. •	Closest Line – when an end point is selected, the point will move along both the line before and after the selected point. •	Show Thumbtacks – controls the display of the thumbtacks for defining a range.  Showing the thumbtacks will allow the user to define the range as a part of the function.  If this button is not selected, the range is automatically assigned based on the other options, Prev/Next Points or End Points. •	Prev/Next Points – places the thumbtacks at the point before and the point after the selected point by default. •	End Points – places the thumbtacks at the end points of the line by default. 3.	Select point(s) to move. 4.	If Show Thumbtacks was selected, reposition the thumbtacks to define the range or click left to keep the current placement of the thumbtacks.  To move a thumbtack, click on the thumbtack to move and either use Cursor mode to position it by eye or use Value Mode to type in measurements.  Left click in the work area to finish positioning the thumbtacks. 5.	Move the point(s) to a new location by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to place the point. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release

pages.title: Specify Distance

links.label: Learn How to Specify the Graded Distance of a Notch:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Specify Distance Specify Distance is used on notches to control the notch positioning along curved lines when grading.  It maintains the smoothness of the curve as the notch is graded.  A tangent grade rule is created.   This type of rule uses only one value, as opposed to two values (X and Y) required in delta grading.  Positive and negative values determine whether growth is in the clockwise or counter-clockwise direction from the sample size (Base up-down grading methods) or previous size (Small-Large Incremental method).  To show that the rule does not correspond to the grade rule table, a pound sign (#) is automatically placed on the grade rule number. Learn How to Specify the Graded Distance of a Notch: 1.	From the Grade menu, select Create/Edit Rules and then Specify Distance. 2.	Select the location for the new grade point. 3.	Select the previous or next grade point for distance measurement.  The Distances dialog box displays. 4.	Specify the length grade for the notch or select from the following Distances dialog box options: •	Clear – removes all values from the Distances fields. •	Update – fills in any blank chart fields with the same value as the field above. •	Cancel – closes the Distances dialog box without making any changes. •	OK – accepts the values and closes the Distances dialog box. NOTE: Entering 0.00 for all sizes keeps the notch the same distance for all sizes in the nest.

pages.title: Specify Length

links.label: Learn How to Grade a Line by a Specified Length

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Specify Length Use this function to grade a line by a specific length or amount.  This allows for a line to be graded by a growth amount or a specific length.  The angle of the line is maintained after the grading is updated. Learn How to Grade a Line by a Specified Length 1.	From the Grade tab, select Specify Length in the Create/Edit panel. 2.	The Specify Length dialog displays. 3. Select from the following User Input options: • Individual – not available. • Both if Same – not available. • Always Both – applies the same grading to both corner endpoints. 4. Select the line to be graded 5. Select the end point of the line to receive the new grade rule 6. Select OK. The Specify Length dialog box displays 7. By default, the current difference in growth and length between size breaks display: 8. Edit values manually in single size breaks. If the Growth amount is changed then the Length will adjust automatically and vice versa or Use the Constant field to determine a specific amount to be applied to all or certain size breaks: •	Right click to display the context menu to use a specific math operation using the Constant value or to divide in half or double the current value. •	Use the Clear Growths/Lengths buttons to delete current values •	Click on Update to preview the changes in the pieces shown in the work area 8. Select OK to finish or Cancel to exit out without applying any changes

pages.title: Measure Straight

links.label: Learn to Measure the Distance Between Two Points in all sizes:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Measure Straight Use to measure the straight distance between two selected points for all graded sizes. This function is the same function as in the Verify tab. When performing the function from the Grade tab, it will generate measurements not only for the base size, but also for all the graded sizes. Learn to Measure the Distance Between Two Points in all sizes: 1. From the Grade Tab, select Straight in the Measure panel 2. Select two points on a piece to measure the straight distance 3. Select the following User Input option if: • Display X/Y Values – to include columns to display the X and Y differences between the selected points. X and Y guidelines are also displayed in the work area. 4. Select OK to measure another area 5. Select OK again to display the measure chart: it displays the straight length value per size, X Distance and the X Difference between sizes. Same values for Y. the Total will display the total sum of all pairs of point distance(s) if more than one set was selected. Size Difference shows the difference between totals in all sizes. 6. Print – click on this button to output the chart directly to the printer of your choice 7. Copy – click on this button to copy the chart information and paste in the program of your choice. This information is output as csv format so if pasted in a spreadsheet in MS-Excel each column and value will be populated in separate fields. 8. Click the X button to close the dialog and continue working in the function 9. When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Stream Sketch

links.label: Learn How to Sketch a New Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Stream Sketch Use this function to create sketched lines with the pen tip up (not dragging on the table).  Stream Sketch is useful for copying style lines off a thicker object, such as a jacket with a shoulder pad.  The pen tip can be up to 3/8” (1cm) above the table. Learn How to Sketch a New Piece: 1.	From the Draft tab, select Draft Scale in the Work Area panel. 2.	From the Draft tab, select Stream Sketch in the Input panel. 3.	Click the lower button on the stylus pen and check the option Create Draft Piece. 4.	To begin drawing a line, press down once with the tip of the stylus pen.  Move the pen to draw the line.  To finish a line, press down again with the stylus pen. 5.	When finished with the draft piece, click the button and select OK. 6.	Use the Draft Trace or Create Piece functions to make the draft piece into a valid piece.

pages.title: Swap

links.label: To Swap the Sew and Cut Lines:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Swap Use to change the line that can be modified in Pattern Design. The solid line is the only line that can be modified.  Since the cut line is automatically sent to the plotter and marker making, this function should only be used when necessary.  Special options can be used for digitized corners – special shapes in the seam allowance only that were digitized or created in Pattern Design. To Swap the Sew and Cut Lines: 1.	From the Advanced tab, select Swap in the Seam panel or press the SHIFT + F8 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Ignore Digitized Corners – use when swapping a piece that has no digitized corners or for a piece that has computer-generated corners. •	Remove Digitized Corners – eliminates digitized corner shapes when the piece is swapped.  These corner lines are identified by defining 0 (zero) seam allowance on the corner line before swapping the seams. •	Manual/Sever Digitized Corners – keeps digitized corner shapes when the piece is swapped.  These corner lines are identified by defining 0 (zero) seam allowance on the corner line before swapping the seams. •	Ignore Grade Rules – keeps the existing grading when the piece is swapped.  This setting is used with the Generate Seam/Corners method in Seam Properties. •	Adjust Seam Grading – modifies the grade rules to keep the seam lines parallel on all graded sizes.  This setting can be used with Grade Seam/Corners method in Seam Properties. •	Copy Grade Rules – places the grade rules from the perimeter on the system generated seam lines. •	Copy Point Numbers – places the point number information from the perimeter on the system generated seam lines. 3.	Select piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces.

pages.title: Tapered Pleat
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Tapered Pleat Use to create single or multiple tapered pleats.  A taper pleat is similar to a variable pleat except only one end of the pleat is opened.  Each pleat may be knife or box style.  New grade rules are calculated if Modify Grade Rules is checked in Edit/Customize/Preferences. To Create a Taper Pleat: 1.	From the Advanced tab, Tapered in the Pleats panel. 2.	Draw slash lines by selecting a point on perimeter where the pleat will begin (pivot point) and end (open point) in cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the beginning and end points of the slash line. •	Value Mode – left click and hold on the line where the slash line will begin.  Click right and release both buttons.  Enter the measurements for the position of the first point in the Beg or End fields.  Repeat these steps for the second point of the slash line. 3.	Create additional slash lines, if desired.  All slash lines must start on the same perimeter line.  When finished, select OK. 4.	Select a point on the piece perimeter to remain stationary.  Select one of the following: •	The pivot point •	Between two pleat lines •	Another perimeter line 5.	Select any internal lines to move while opening the pleat.  Internal lines that are not selected will remain in the same position relative to the grain line.  When finished, select OK. 6.	Position the piece to define the underlay of the pleat on the open end.  This can be defined in cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click to determine the pleat underlay for the open end. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the full pleat underlay in the Dist field or enter the angle of pivot in the Ang field. 7.	If more than one pleat is being created, repeat this positioning step for each slash lin

pages.title: Tapered Fullness

links.label: Learn How to Add or Subtract Tapered Fullness:
To Add or Subtract Tapered Fullness to Multiple Pieces:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Tapered Fullness Use to add or subtract fullness to the open end of the slash line, tapering to nothing at the pivot end. Tapered  fullness allows for an amount of fullness to be added or removed from a piece using slash lines.  A portion of the piece will be held stationary while the fullness is opened.  There are three options for selection of the location to remain stationary: •	The pivot point – by selecting the pivot point, the piece will open to both sides for the fullness, as shown below.  To select the pivot point, click and hold on the slash line.  Move the cursor to the pivot point of the slash line.  A circle will highlight to indicate the pivot point.  Once this point highlights, release the mouse button. •	Between two slash lines – allows multiple slash lines to open in different directions.  Left click on the line segment between the two slash lines. •	Another perimeter line – holds part of the perimeter while the fullness is opened or closed.  Left click on the perimeter line to hold on grain. Learn How to Add or Subtract Tapered Fullness: 1.	From the Piece menu, select Fullness and then Tapered Fullness. 2.	Draw slash lines by selecting a point on the perimeter where the fullness will begin (pivot point) and end (open point) using one of the following methods.  No fullness will be added at the pivot point of the slash line: •	Cursor Mode – left click to place the beginning and end points of the slash line. •	Value Mode – left click and hold on the line where the slash line will begin.  Click right and release both buttons.  Enter the measurements for the position of the first point in the Beg or End fields.  Repeat these steps for the second point of the slash line. •	Right Mouse Button Menu – right click in the work area

pages.title: Translate
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Translate This option displays the Translate Data dialog box. The translation library and the display language can be selected in this dialog. The translated data can be plotted. This enhancement is not backwards compatible to AccuMark versions prior to 8.4.0. Exporting data into AAMA and ASTM format will not include the translated annotation. The translation library, datatranslation.txt, contains a line of text in multiple languages. The text file can be located on a local or network drive. The first line of the text file contains an equals sign, ‘=Language’ followed by the languages supported in the translation library. The user can specify which languages will be supported. The same number of languages needs to be listed for every entry. The next contains ‘=Tag’ followed by an optional abbreviation. If the system finds the abbreviation, it will replace it with the string of the selected language. The following lines of text include the text string in every language supported by the library. If no abbreviation is needed, ‘=String’ is used followed by the lines of translations

pages.title: Trim/Extend Line

links.label: Learn How to Lengthen or Shorten Lines:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Trim/Extend Line Use this function to lengthen or shorten lines that were created using sketch. The end point of the line is moved along the same axis or angle of the line. Using Trim/Extend Line allows the system to find an intersection when using the Create Piece function.  This function works similarly to Modify – Point/Line. Learn How to Lengthen or Shorten Lines: 1.	From the Draft tab, select Trim/Extend Line in the Edit panel. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	First Line – •	Second Line – •	Closest Line – 3.	Select an end point to move. 4.	Move the end point to its new location and left click to drop the point.

pages.title: Trim/Extend Piece

links.label: Learn How to Trim a Piece After Sketching:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Trim/Extend Piece When sketching a hard pattern, the thickness of the stylus can cause the piece to be created slightly larger than the original. This function is used to trim half of the pen thickness from the perimeter of the finished piece. Trim/Extend Piece can be used after Create Piece or Draft Trace.  The maximum amount is +/-.25” (.635 cm). Learn How to Trim a Piece After Sketching: 1.	From the Draft tab, select Trim/Extend Piece in the Edit panel. 2.	Select the piece(s).  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple pieces. 3.	Enter the amount to trim off the piece perimeter. A negative value should be used to make the piece smaller.  A positive value should be used to make the piece larger.

pages.title: Unclipped
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Unclipped Use this function to indicate which lines should be allowed to have the line extend beyond the normal perimeter intersection. This allows having two unique points exist at an intersection. The two points can have different grade rules and point types. To Allow Line Extensions: 1.	From the Edit tab, select the Customize drop down and then select Preferences in the Workspace Panel.  Select the Display tab. 2.	Set Perimeter to Unclipped to view the line extensions. Then OK. 3.	From the Edit tab, select Unclipped in the Properties panel.  The system displays the current state for the perimeter/boundary lines of the pieces in the work area. 4.	Select the line(s) to be extended.  Use the Ctrl key to select multiple lines.  The system redisplays the current state for the perimeter/boundary lines.  When the lines of a piece are set to Unclipped, point and line functions can be used to extend the lines beyond the intersections.

pages.title: Undo
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Undo Use this function undo the last function completed. This command will allow for the last 20 steps to be undone in consecutive, reverse order.  Moving and deleting pieces in the work area are included in the steps that can be undone.  This function is also available by right clicking on the work area when no functions are active (idle state). To Undo the Last Operation: 1.	From the Edit tab, select Undo or press the CTRL + Z keys on the keyboard.  The function is automatically performed. 2.	If desired, continue to select this function to undo previous operations in consecutive reverse order.

pages.title: Undo Buffer

links.label: To Delete, Add, or Edit Intersection Notches:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search To Add an Intersection Notch Use to delete, add, or edit intersection notches. An intersection notch is located where one internal line intersects a perimeter line or would intersect if extended.  The notch will be placed at the same angle as the notching line.  This type of notch can be used to maintain notches at the extensions of dart and pleat lines.  If the internal line is moved, the notch will also move to the new intersection. To Delete, Add, or Edit Intersection Notches: 1.	From the Notch menu, select Intersection Notch. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Delete – use to remove an intersection notch. •	Add – use to add a new intersection notch. •	Edit – use to change an existing intersection notch type or depth. •	Type – controls the kind of notch being used.  Select from the drop-down menu.  This option is only available if Add or Edit was selected. •	Depth – displays depth of the notch type selected. 3.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Delete was chosen, select the line or piece with the notches to be removed.  When finished, select OK. •	If Add was chosen, select the perimeter line to notch.  Select the internal notching line(s).  When finished, select OK. •	If Edit was chosen, select the line or piece with the notches to change.  When finished, select OK.

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search To Add a Reference Notch A Reference Notch is a notch whose reference point is at a location other than the notch location.  When a reference notch is created, the distance between notch and reference notch is maintained as the piece is modified.  When the Notch Types are shown, the number of the notch and its reference distance will display. A single Reference Notch can be added or groups can be added on a line or on a line with a distance . To Add a Reference Notch 1.	From the Notch menu, select Reference Notch and then Add. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Type – controls the kind of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. •	Depth – displays the depth for selected notch type. •	Copy Distance – check this option to add a new notch with the same reference distance as another notch. •	Perpendicular – the notch will be placed on the seam allowance by extending a perpendicular (90-degree angle) line from the notched line. •	Notch Angle  – notches will be placed on the seam allowance by extending the angle created by the original notch. •	Same Distance on Seam – notches will be placed on the seam allowance using the same measurement as the reference distance. •	Group Notches – check to add more than one notch at a time. •	Distance Between – the measurement in between the notches. •	# Of Notches  – how many notches to add. 3.	Select the reference point. 4.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Copy Distance was chosen, select the line to place the notch.  Then, select the notch to copy the reference distance from. •	If Copy Distance was not selected, mark a location for the notch by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to add the notch. •	V

pages.title: To Add a Tangent Notch

links.label: To Grade the Position of a Notch along a Line using a Tangent Grading:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search To Add a Tangent Notch Use to grade the position of a reference notch along a line.  This function can be used to add a new notch or grade an existing notch.  If the notch is not currently a reference notch, it will be converted into a reference notch.  Tangent grading values are defined so that the notch will be graded at a distance along the line from the reference point.  To maintain the reference distance on all sizes, enter a value of 0 for each size break.  The symbol used to represent a Tangent rule is slightly different than the symbol for a regular grade rule. Reference notches maintain their distance to another point on all sizes.  Tangent notches are reference notches where the distance between the notch and the reference point changes on graded sizes. To Grade the Position of a Notch along a Line using a Tangent Grading: 1.	From the Notch menu, select Tangent . 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Type – controls the kind of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. •	Depth – determines the depth of a notch.  Type in the desired depth. •	Perpendicular – the notch will be placed on the seam allowance by extending a perpendicular (90-degree angle) line from the notched line. •	Notch Angle – notches will be placed on the seam allowance by extending the angle created by the original notch. •	Same Distance on Seam – notches will be placed on the seam allowance using the same measurement as the reference distance. •	Group Notches – check to add more than one notch at a time. •	Distance Between  – the measurement in between the notches. •	# Of Notches  – how many notches to add. 3.	Select an existing notch or mark a location by cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location to add the notch.

pages.title: Bookmark Group
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Bookmark Group The Bookmark function allows you to save a visual display of the piece shape before modifications are made to the piece.  As modifications are made, the original geometry is still shown so that the “before and after” versions can be compared. There are 2 types of Bookmarks, Original and Defined. The Original Bookmark is the initial version of the piece when AccuMark PDS is first used.  The Defined Bookmark is user definable at any time the pattern is being modified.  Only 1 Defined Bookmark exists for each piece. The bookmarked version of the piece will be preserved when the piece is saved.  The bookmark geometry is not selectable. Bookmarks help you to identify the piece that a contractor will use to begin with in addition to the modifications and balance between the original started piece and the modified piece. In addition the original used piece name will be displayed to make it easier to ensure the correct “block” piece (slopers) was used to begin with.The Original Bookmark is automatically created when the piece is opened. Select from the following User Input options: •	Add Grade Rules on Intersection – applies a proportional grade rule where the digitized line intersects a graded perimeter line. •	Modify Length – use to adjust the length of the line to a specific measurement after it is created. 3.	To create a new piece from the digitized lines, right click and select the Create Draft Piece option.  Enter the new piece name. 4.	Select the first point of the line using one of the following methods: •	Cursor Mode – left click on the location of the first point. •	Value Mode – left click and drag the cursor to the point to measure from, click the right button and release both buttons.  Enter a distance in the Beg or End fields t

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Create a Mirrored Line Use to copy and flip a line or lines over another line.  The copied lines will remain on the same piece as internal lines. Learn How to Mirror a Line: 1.	From the Create tab, select Mirror from the Line Group. 2.	Select the line(s) to mirror.  When finished, select OK. 3.	Select the line to mirror about.  The selected lines will flip over this line to create the mirror image. NOTE: Line and point information is copied over with the line.  This includes internal labels and point attributes, except stack (Z) and rotation (R) attributes.

pages.title: Altered Size
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Altered Size Altered sizes can be viewed to check alteration amounts and locations. To Display an Altered Size: 1.	From the Create Tab select Altered Size in the Piece Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	New Piece Name – when checked, adds a prompt to name the new piece.  If left unchecked, the piece will have the same name as the original. •	Keep Grade Rules – allows for the altered piece to have the original grade rules.  If this option is left unchecked, all the grading will be removed from the piece. 3.	Select the piece(s) to create the altered size from.  When finished, select OK. 4.	In the Alteration Setup window, use the drop-down menu to select the Alteration Library. 5.	If desired, select the Size Code table. 6.	Select the Alteration Rule from the Rule Name box.  Select OK. 7.	Type in the Amount of the Alteration.  Select OK. 8.	From the Altered Size window, select the size to display.  Select OK.  The new piece will appear on the work area. 9.	If the New Piece Name option was chosen, enter the piece name for the new piece.

pages.title: Binding
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Binding Binding pieces can be created by selecting the corresponding lines.  Notches will be placed along the length to indicate seam positions and notches from original lines.  Grading is also applied to the piece to fit the original lines for all sizes. Using options in the function, the piece width, grading, and rotation can be set.  To create the rectangle, select lines.  If the Grade Piece option was turned on, the piece will match the selected lines for all graded sizes. To Create a Binding Piece: 1.	From the Create Tab select Binding from the Piece Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Name – enter the piece name for the new piece. •	Add Piece to Model/Style – use to add the piece to the current style or model. •	Binding Width – enter the width measurement of the new piece. •	Depth – determines the depth of a notch for MicroMark notches.  Type in the desired depth. •	Type – controls the kind of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. 3.	Select the lines in a counterclockwise order.  The lines can be selected from multiple pieces.  When finished, select OK. 4.	Left click to drop the new piece on the work area.

pages.title: Collar
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Collar Collars are created by entering dimensions and notch information. Information related to collar behavior for 3D simulation can also be added. To Create a Collar: 1.	From the Create Tab select Collar from the Piece Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Name – enter the piece name for the new piece. •	Add Piece to Model/Style – use to add the piece to the current style or model. •	Collar Width – measurement of the collar at the center back line. •	CB to Shoulder – back neck measurement. •	Shoulder to CF – front neck measurement. •	Line Rotation – determines the upward curve at the neckline edge for a convertible collar. •	Shoulder Notch – places a notch at the shoulder of the collar. •	Depth – determines the depth of a notch for MicroMark notches.  Type in the desired depth. •	Type – controls the kind of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. 3.	Select OK.  The piece will appear in the work area.  Select Cancel to exit the Collar command

pages.title: Copy Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Copy Piece Use to create an exact duplicate of a piece.  This is helpful to compare a piece before and after changes are made. To Create a Copy: 1.	From the Create Tab, select Copy from the Piece Group. 2.	Select the Add Piece to Model/Style option if the new piece is to be added to the current style or model. 3.	Select a piece. Left click to place the duplicate in the work area. 4.	Enter a piece name for the new piece.

pages.title: Extract Piece
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Extract Piece This tool will create pieces using sections of an existing piece.  The user creates design lines on a piece.  The closed sections defined by these lines are selected by the Extract Piece tool to define the area to be made into a new piece.  Sections can be selected on one piece only. To Extract a Piece: 1.	Create design lines to define the area of the new piece.  Any of the create line functions  can be used. 2.	From the Create Tab select Extract from the Piece group or press the SHIFT + F4 keys on the keyboard. 3.	Select the Add Piece to Model/Style option if the new piece is to be added to the current style or model. 4.	Select the piece to extract regions from. 5.	Sections of the piece will highlight as the cursor is passed over them.  Select the first section to create the new piece. 6.	If desired, select additional adjacent regions. When finished, select OK. 7.	Enter a piece name for the new piece. 8.	Select internal line(s). When finished or if none were selected, select OK.  The new piece will be attached to the cursor.  Move the piece to a new location and left click to place it in the work area.

pages.title: Facing
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Facing Facings are created by using a pre-defined facing line or by digitizing a new line.  Any internal lines or points will automatically be included in the new facing piece. To Create a Facing: 1.	From the Create Tab, select Facing in the Piece Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Add Piece to Model/Style – use to add the new piece to the current style or model. •	Define Seam on Facing Line – use to add seam allowance to the selected facing line. Piece must already have system generated seam allowance to use this option. •	Modify Length – used with the Digitized Line option.  When checked, the system will prompt to adjust the length of the line to a specific measurement after it is created. •	Existing Line – use to select a line already defined on the piece. •	Digitized Line – use to draw the line for the facing as a part of the function. 3.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Existing Line was chosen, select the line to create the facing from. •	If Digitized Line was chosen, left click to define the first point of the line.  Value mode can be used to place the line at a specific point.  Right mouse button options are also available.  When finished drawing the line, select OK.  If Modify Length was chosen, type in the desired length of the line. 4.	Select the facing piece. 5.	Left click to drop the new piece in the work area.  Enter the new piece name.

pages.title: Filled Pieces On/Off
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Filled Pieces On/Off Toggle the view to show/hide the interior of a piece with color or fabric, as set in the Preferences.

pages.title: Fusible
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Fusible Creates a fusible piece by copying an original piece and trimming off a specified amount from the perimeter shape.  This function can trim off up to 1” (2.54cm).  The original grading and seam allowances are maintained on the new piece. To Create a Fusible Piece: 1.	From the Create Tab select Fusible from the Piece Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Selection – controls how the piece will be trimmed to create the fusible piece.  Select Line to choose the lines to be trimmed; select Piece to trim the same amount of the whole piece. •	Add Piece to Model/Style – use to add the new piece to the current style or model. •	New Piece Name – when checked, adds a prompt to name the new piece.  If left unchecked, the piece will have the same name as the original. •	Remove Notches – deletes all notches from the new fusible piece. 3.	Depending on what was chosen in the User Input options, the selection changes: •	If Line was chosen, select the line(s) to trim to make the fusible piece.  When finished, select OK. •	If Piece was chosen, select the piece(s) to create fusibles.  When finished, select OK. 4.	Enter the amount to trim off the original piece.  This value must be negative. 5.	If New Piece Name was selected, enter the piece name for the new piece.

pages.title: Graded Size
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Graded Size Sizes other than the base size can be displayed for comparison purposes.  The new piece will have zero growths assigned to all graded points. To Display a Non-Base Size: 1.	From Create Tab select Graded Size from the Piece Group. 2.	Select the New Piece Name option to give the new piece a different name, 3.	Select the piece(s) to create the graded size from.  When finished, select OK. 4.	A Graded Size dialog box will open. The dialog box displays the existing graded sizes, breaks, and base size information. Select the graded size desired for the new piece(s) and click OK. 5.	If the New Piece Name option was chosen, enter the piece name for the new piece. NOTE: If the new piece is saved, the selected size will be its base size. Delete this text and replace it with your own content.

pages.title: Rectangle
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Rectangle Use to create rectangular pieces by eye or by entering exact measurements. To Create a Rectangle: 1.	From the Create Tab select Rectangle in the Piece group or press the SHIFT + F6 keys on the keyboard. 2.	Check the Add Piece to Model/Style option if the new piece is to be added to the current model. 3.	Left click in the work area to select the first point of the rectangle. 4.	Draw the rectangle in cursor or value mode: •	Cursor Mode – left click in the work area to determine the size of the rectangle. •	Value Mode – click both buttons and release.  Enter the measurements of the rectangle in the Dist, X or Y fields. 5.	Enter a new name in the Piece Name field, if desired.

pages.title: Ruffle
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Ruffle This function will create a new spiral ruffle from an existing piece.  This function “wraps” the original piece around a user-defined circumference. To Create a Ruffle: 1.	From the Create Tab select Ruffle from the Piece Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Add Piece to Model/Style – use to add the piece to the current style or model. •	Interior Diameter – controls how tightly the center of the ruffle wraps.  Enter the desired measurement. •	Distance Between Spirals – determines the spacing between the circular wraps of the ruffle. 3.	Select the slash line.  This line’s length will be maintained when creating the ruffle. 4.	Select the location to remain stationary at the beginning or end of the slash line. 5.	Select any internal lines to move.  Only selected internals will be carried over to the new piece.  When finished, select OK. 6.	Select a method to slash the piece to create the ruffle: •	Evenly (Perpendicular) – creates the slash lines perpendicular (90 degrees) to the selected line. •	Evenly (Proportional) – creates slash lines equally along the selected line. 7.	Enter the new piece name. NOTE: To add seam allowance after creating a ruffle, enter an amount two times the seam allowance or two times the seam allowance plus spacing in the Distance Between Spirals field. Then, add seam allowance after the ruffle has been created.

links.label: To Create a Circle Skirt Piece:

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Skirt Creates a 1/4 panel of a circular skirt.  Ruffles and collars can also be created with this function. Enter the total circumference and length measurements of the skirt. To Create a Circle Skirt Piece: 1.	From the Create Tab select Skirt in the Piece Group. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Name – enter the piece name for the new piece. •	Add Piece to Model/Style – use to add the piece to the current style or model. •	Show Center Point – adds a mark point indicating the center of the pattern •	Waist – the total waist length used to calculate the waist of the new piece.  This measurement will be divided by 4 to create the skirt waist. •	Length – total length measurement of new piece •	Dist Between Points – controls the distance between the points on the perimeter when the circle is created.  Default will let the system decide the spacing of the points. 3.	Select OK.  The piece will appear in the work area.  Select Cancel to exit the Skirt command.

With the front and back pattern in the work area, select the Verify tab and choose Line Length. 2.	Select the front and back armhole line to measure.  These measurements will be required to create the sleeve pattern. 3.	Once the armhole measurements are noted, go to the Create tab and select Sleeve in the Piece panel. 4.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Name – enter the piece name for the new piece. •	Add Piece to Model – use to the piece to the current model. •	Sleeve Length – enter the total length measurement from the sleeve cap to sleeve wrist. •	Cap Length Front – enter the front armhole length referenced from the front bodice pattern. •	Cap Length Back – enter the back armhole length referenced from the back bodice pattern. •	Cap Height – the height of the sleeve cap. •	Wrist Width – the opening width at the wrist. •	Notch Type – controls the type of notch being added.  Select from the drop-down menu. •	Notch Depth – view the notch depth defined in the P-Notch table.  This field is not editable. 5.	Select OK.  The piece will appear in the work area. pages.title: Pleats Group
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Pleats Group Beginning in AccuMark PDS version 10, the software remembers pleat information after  pleats are created.  This means that pleats can  be edited or deleted after the pleats are created and saved. Pleats are then pleat objects. These improvements are extremely valuable because a second copy of the piece without the pleats does not have to be saved with the model.  Edits can be made directly to the piece with the pleats. When several pleats are created at one time, those pleats are created as a group.  This means if one of the group is selected for Open/Close, Edit or Delete, all pleats of the group are effected. No I User Defined Internals* – an internal line drawn with any of the Create Line functions.  This label is assigned automatically to new internal lines. No J No K No L No M Mirror Line* – the fold line for a mirrored piece.  This label is automatically assigned when a piece is mirrored. No N Yes O Yes P Fixed Piecing Line* – a line used for splitting a piece in marker making. Yes Q Yes R Yes S Seam Allowance Lines*– lines that define the amount of seam defined on a piece.  This label is assigned automatically when using Define Seam.
