pages.title: Reduce Points
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Reduce Points Use to remove unnecessary intermediate points from a line or piece.  This function will not remove grade points or notch points.  Reduce Points can be useful after inputting a piece with the Draft / Sketch function. Learn How to Reduce Points: 1.	From the Point menu, select Reduce Points. 2.	Select from the following User Input options: •	Reduction Factor – controls how many points will be removed.  Set the reduction factor to a higher number to remove more points or a lower number to remove fewer points. •	N Attributes/Turn Points – allows points with N attributes to be removed, if necessary. •	S Attributes/Curve Points – allows points with S attributes to be removed, if necessary. •	Remove Notch Turn/Curve Points – is used to remove any turn or curve points from a notch location. 3.	Select the line(s) or piece(s).  When finished, select OK.

pages.title: Pleat to Internal
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Pleat to Internal The creation of pleats has been improved to be more productive. Pleat to Internal can be used to add one or more pleats to one end inside of a piece without the need to split a pattern piece. The pleats are added to all graded sizes of the piece. This type of pleat is not saved as an object; therefore Close, Edit or Delete Pleat functions don’t apply. Follow these steps to create pleats to internal positions: Function prompts: •	Select first point of ending line for pleat (A) •	Select second point of ending line for pleat (B) •	Create slash line from pivot end to open end; create as many lines as pleats to be created. (C) When finished, click OK to continue •	At this point while working on cursor mode, position the parts of the piece to create spread or toggle to value mode to enter an amount. •	Drag the mouse along the slash line. When creating the pleat: a)	In cursor mode, as mouse moves, the two sub-blocks rotate against two different ending locations (two end points on ending internal line).  There are several mouse locations that will get the same open value. b)	In Value mode, there will be only one result because the value is measured along the slash line. •	When complete, select the desire type of pleat and complete the function as usual. The pleat has been created.

pages.title: Preferences: Color Tab
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Preferences: Color Tab To make it easier to identify pieces in the workspace, colors of pieces and nested sizes can be changed.  Colors for text, prompts, background, and grid in the work area can also be adjusted. To Change Colors: 1.	From the Edit Tab, select Preferences/Options. 2.	Select the Color tab. 3.	Left click on the color swatch next to the item to change. 4.	Select a new color by selecting a color swatch from the Predefined Colors or creating a new color by dragging the Red, Green and Blue levels.  A preview of the color is shown in the Current Color box.  When finished, click OK. 5.	Click Apply to show the changed color on the screen. Piece Colors: •	Original – indicates the color to be used for perimeter and internal lines that have not been modified. •	 Highlighted – indicates the color of the current piece (perimeter and internal lines). When multiple pieces are in the work area, the piece that the cursor is currently on displays in this color. •	Near – indicates the color an object will be when the cursor is close enough to select it. •	Modified – indicates the color of a piece (perimeter and internal lines) that has been edited.  The piece will return to the Original color after it is saved. •	Selected – indicates the color of pieces, points or lines that have been selected for a specific function. Original Bookmark- indicates the color of the original bookmarked piece Defined Bookmark-indicates the color the defined bookmark Fabric Fill: •	Fabric Name – indicates the color to be used in the piece icon menu and for color fill on pieces in a model. pages.title: Working with Seams for AccuMark 3D
pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Working with Seams for AccuMark 3D Stitching relationships in 3D preparation are defined on the sew lines of a pattern. This ensures the completed 3D virtualization is based on the finished garment measurements. For this reason, it is important that the garment is saved in the sew state prior to opening the model in the 3D workspace. The functions below discuss how to view, define, and swap seam allowance. General seam allowance information includes: •	A Cut Line is a line on a piece that will be used for cutting. •	A Sew Line is a line on a piece where the pattern will be sewn when making the item. This is desired line for garment 3D preparation. •	Pieces can be stored with either the sew or cut line as the piece perimeter/boundary. When a piece with the sew line as the perimeter is sent to marker making or to plot, the cut lines are automatically used. •	Once seam allowance has been defined, the amount assigned to each line is saved as part of the piece information. •	A warning message can be displayed when a selection is made on a non-perimeter (dashed) line.  These selections will be ignored. •	Sew or Cut displays in the Pattern Design Info bar when a piece is highlighted, indicating which line is currently the perimeter (solid) line. •	Hide Seams located in the Information bar can toggle the seam allowance display within the work area.

pages.bodySummary: Filter: All Files Submit Search Getting Started AccuMark 3D is a product that allow users to simulate 2D patterns onto 3D forms for pattern validation, fit verification, art placement and more. The workflow is simple and integrated within AccuMark PDS. Simply specify additional details for 3D in the AccuMark model, define stitching and placement information in PDS, and then simulate the garments in 3D. 3D Workflow 3D garment simulation is a sequential process. If specific steps are missed, the 3D rendering will not be successful. To successfully render in 3D, users need to follow a sequential order, beginning with the Model Editor. This guide is organized to follow the order of operations required to complete a 3D simulation.  Each chapter covers a step in this process. 1. Pattern Design: 3D Place pieces in work area Rotate pieces to the correct orientation as needed Create Relationships Place on Avatar Cloth Simulation Image Library Image Library-Images as AccuMark Data Types The powerful Image Library is used to organize and maintain all images used within the system. The Image Library displays crucial image info relating to the size and color space of the files while also providing thumbnails to quickly view. With version 12.2, we have introduced the ability to assign multiple size codes to one model or multiple models associated to the same Size Code table. Refer to the AccuMark What’s New document under the Easy Plan section for further details. In AccuPlan, users can enable a preference before selecting sizes and size codes. When the Size Selection is checked, AccuPlan automatically opens a dialog box to select only the desired sizes to be used in the cutwork order. (See the example image below.) In addition, users can always edit the size line at any time to add/remove sizes to the current work order.  Once the size table has been created in the Cut Plan Input, right-click anywhere in the size header and click on Edit Size Line .  Then select the size(s) to include in the work order.
